嘉靖四十四年三月十五日早，諸貢士赴內府殿試，上御皇極殿，親賜策問。

三月二十日早，文武百官朝服侍班。是日，錦衣衛設鹵簿于丹陛丹墀內。上御皇極殿，鴻臚寺官傳制唱名。禮部官捧黃榜，鼓樂導引出長安左門外張掛畢，順天府官用傘盖儀從送狀元歸第。

三月二十一日
translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month in the forty-fourth year of Jiajing (1565), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in the Hall of Imperial Supremacy (Huangji dian) and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the twentieth day of the third month, the civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard arrayed the imperial ceremonial regalia on the vermilion steps and in the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in the Hall of Imperial Supremacy. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow proclamation of successful candidates, led by drums and music, out beyond the Left Chang'an Gate. After the proclamation had been posted, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with a ceremonial parasol and retinue.

On the twenty-first day of the third month…

賜宴於禮部，宴畢，赴鴻臚寺習儀。
三月二十三日，賜狀元朝服冠帶及進士寶鈔。
三月二十四日，狀元率諸進士上表謝恩。
三月二十五日，狀元率諸進士詣先師孔子廟，行釋菜禮。
禮部奏請，命工部於國子監立石題名。
translation_en:
…a banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates proceeded to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the rites.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a girdle were bestowed upon the first-place graduate, and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for the imperial favor.
On the twenty-fifth day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite.
The Ministry of Rites submitted a petition requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe their names upon it.

punctuated:
第一甲三名，賜進士及第。

范應期〔貫浙江湖州府烏程縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字伯楨，行一，年三十九，十月初七日生〕。曾祖縉，祖完，父萱，母陸氏。慈侍下，弟應明〔監生〕、應光、輝、嘉、朝，娶沈氏。順天府鄉試第七十名，會試第一百九十三名。

李自華〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉善縣民籍，直隸松江府華亭縣人，嘉善縣學生，治詩經，字元實，行三，年三十，正月初九日生〕。曾祖淮，祖祚，父學孟，母郁氏，繼母江氏。具慶下，兄守敬、守教，弟守亨、守斅、守敘、守貞，娶陸氏。浙江鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百三十四名。

陳棟〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字隆之，行八，年二十九，三月二十七日生〕。曾祖進國，祖亢初，父光〔典史〕，母宗氏。具慶下，兄柯，弟梁、椿、桂、栢、檀、模、楹、梅、植，娶樊氏。江西鄉試第六十六名，會試第一名。
translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate (jinshi) with distinction.

Fan Yingqi: registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bozhen; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Wan, his father Xuan, and his mother née Lu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yingming (a National University student), Yingguang, Hui, Jia, and Chao. He married a woman née Shen. He placed seventieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zihua: registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; a student of the Jiashan County Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanshi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huai, his grandfather Zuo, his father Xuemeng, his mother née Yu, and his stepmother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shoujing and Shoujiao; his younger brothers were Shouheng, Shouxue, Shouxu, and Shouzhen. He married a woman née Lu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dong: registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi; an attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Longzhi; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinguo, his grandfather Kangchu, his father Guang (a Chief Clerk), and his mother née Zong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ke; his younger brothers were Liang, Chun, Gui, Bai, Tan, Mo, Ying, Mei, and Zhi. He married a woman née Fan. He placed sixty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐雲程〔貫江西臨江府清江縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字允登，行一，年四十一，九月二十日生〕。曾祖南育，祖巽〔壽官〕，父相，母楊氏。具慶下，弟雲同、雲衢，娶陳氏。江西鄉試第八十三名，會試第一百三十七名。

伊在庭〔貫應天府上元縣匠籍，直隸蘇州府吳縣人，國子生，治易經，字繼美，行二，年二十九，九月二十日生〕。曾祖乘〔按察司僉事〕，祖伯熊〔府同知，贈奉政大夫〕，父敏生〔布政司參政〕，母葉氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄在道，弟在選、在迪、在遇、在暹、在達，娶韓氏。應天府鄉試第六十八名，會試第三名。

鄒國儒〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣民籍，秀水縣人，嘉興縣學生，治書經，字醇甫，行一，年三十七，正月十九日生〕。曾祖裕〔壽官〕，祖鑑〔聽選官〕，父浩，母程氏。慈侍下，娶唐氏。浙江鄉試第十九名，會試第二百四十八名。
translation_en:
Second Class: seventy-seven men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi).

Xu Yuncheng, registered in a military household in Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yundeng. First in birth order, he was forty-one years old and was born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Nanyu; his grandfather, Xun, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Xiang, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuntong and Yunqu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Zaiting, registered in an artisan household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jimei. Second in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Cheng, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather, Boxiong, was a Prefectural Vice Prefect, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Governance; his father, Minsheng, was an Administration Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Ye, was granted the title Lady (ruren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zaidao; his younger brothers were Zaixuan, Zaidi, Zaiyu, Zaixian, and Zaida. His wife was née Han. He placed sixty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Guoru, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a native of Xiushui County. He was a student of the Jiaxing County school specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Chunfu. First in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the nineteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Yu, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, Jian, was an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father was Hao, and his mother was née Cheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Tang. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

馮子京〔貫浙江杭州府仁和縣民籍，錢塘縣人，國子生，治易經，字仲元，行三，年三十六，七月十四日生〕。曾祖斌，祖財，父睿，前母吳氏，母周氏。永感下，兄子堂、子立，弟子庸、子卞，娶胡氏，繼娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第二百七十三名。

涂淵〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，府學附學生，治易經，字時躍，行二，年三十七，十月二十八日生〕。曾祖春山，祖鳳池，父棟，母羅氏。慈侍下，弟津、渭、濬，娶魏氏。江西鄉試第十一名，會試第一百八十五名。

陳經邦〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，府學增廣生，治書經，字公望，行一，年二十九，十月二十三日生〕。曾祖必清〔壽官〕，祖一通〔壽官〕，父言〔南京刑部郎中〕，母朱氏。具慶下，弟經世、經正、經義，娶林氏。福建鄉試第十名，會試第二名。
translation_en:
Song Nuo, registered in a civilian household in Gucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a native of Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Luan, his father Liangchou, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yu, Zhao, and Gao, and his wife was née Li. He placed 108th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 92nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Zijing, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a native of Qiantang County and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongyuan; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Cai, and his father Rui; his father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zitang and Zili, and his younger brothers Ziyong and Zibian. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed 14th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Yuan was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiyue; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chunshan, his grandfather Fengchi, his father Dong, and his mother née Luo; his father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Jin, Wei, and Jun, and his wife was née Wei. He placed 11th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jingbang was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was an added student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Gongwang; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Biqing and grandfather Yitong both held honorary official status granted for longevity. His father Yan was a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice at Nanjing, and his mother was née Zhu; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jingshi, Jingzheng, and Jingyi, and his wife was née Lin. He placed 10th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 2nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

周鐸〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州民籍，常熟縣人，太倉州學增廣生，治詩經，字子振，行二十，年三十六，五月初十日生〕。曾祖棠〔七品散官〕，祖燁〔贈按察司副使〕，父室，前母凌氏，母譚氏。永感下，兄錫〔通判〕、鈺〔鴻臚〕、鑾、鍔、鍊、鑛〔俱監生〕、鍵〔工部主事〕、金僉〔進士〕、鑫，弟釬、鏜、鑠，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第六名，會試第一百十六名。

translation_en:
Tu Yuanmu, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rixin; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Peng, was an unranked assistant magistrate; his father was Gao, and his mother was née Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Yuansong, Yuanxiang, and Yuanxi. He married a woman née Yin. He placed sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Duo, registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from Changshu County. He was an added student of the Taicang Subprefectural School, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he ranked twentieth among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the tenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Tang, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Ye, was posthumously granted the title of Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father was Shi; his father's former wife was née Ling, and his mother was née Tan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xi, a subprefect; Yu, an official of the Court of State Ceremonial; Luan, E, Lian, and Kuang, all students of the Directorate of Education; Jian, a bureau secretary in the Ministry of Works; Jin Qian [?], a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); and Xin. His younger brothers were Han, Tang, and Shuo. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Zi, registered in a civilian household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dacai; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Minze, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his grandfather was Mingju; his father was Changsen, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tan, Song, and Nan, and his younger brother was Tong. He married a woman née Shen. He placed seventy-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Ximin, registered in a civilian household in Shidai County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weixian; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Tingxun, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his grandfather, Dong, was a tribute scholar. His father was Huan; his legal mother was née Yang, and his birth mother was née Peng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xicheng, who held a seventh-rank prestige title, and Tianxi, a provincial sacrificial official [?]. His younger brothers were Xiyan, Ximo, and Xijia. He married a woman née Li. He placed ninety-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yidi, registered in a civilian household in Maoming County, Gaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Junzhe; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keyou, a tribute student; his grandfather was Ju, who held an honorary longevity title; his father was Xuezhu, who likewise held an honorary longevity title; and his mother was née Lu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jian, Sheng (Assistant Magistrate of Ruichang County), Ti (Registrar), Lan (Assistant Instructor), Fang (Assistant Instructor), and Mu; his younger brother was Cheng, a government student. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Du. He placed forty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Chaoyang, registered in an artisan household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Jiashan County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenrong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather was Ang, his father was Xian, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Tang. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 347th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Zhiyi, registered in a civilian household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Jiazheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather was Wan, and his father was Yun; his father's principal wife was née Fei, and his birth mother was née Ling. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Zhigao. He married a woman née Lu. He placed 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiayan, registered in a civilian household in Dongguang County, Jingzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Kongzhang; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather was Xin, his father was Ji, and his mother was née Liang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Jiabin. He married a woman née Li. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Rujie, registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from She County, Huizhou Prefecture. An attached student of the Jiading County school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daoheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the twentieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chongqing; his grandfather, Shebing; his father, Wenbang; and his mother, née Cheng. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Rujian, Ruji, Rujun, Ruli, and Rushao. His wife was née Cheng. He placed twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jian was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruming; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zong (an honorary official for longevity); his grandfather, Ze (honorarily appointed Director in the Nanjing Ministry of War); and his father, Wen (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner). His mother was née Li (granted the title Lady of Suitability), and his stepmother was née Yuan (also granted the title Lady of Suitability). His father alone was living. His elder brother was Jin; his younger brothers were Qin (a tribute scholar, gongshi) and Gao. His wife was née Liu; he subsequently married a woman née Bao. He placed eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Yilong was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yueqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Tai; his grandfather, Jue; his father, Yi; and his mother, née Qiao. His mother alone was living. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Ruchun was registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An added-quota student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaojing; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather, Yuanshun; his father, Gang; and his mother, née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruli; his younger brothers were Rujin and Rudeng. His wife was née Chen. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Yingchang, registered in a military household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shixiang, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Fu, his father Ru, and his mother née He; his father was living and his mother deceased; his elder brother was Yingqi, his younger brothers Yinglong and Ying'e, and his wife née Gu; he placed thirteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 399th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, registered in a military household of Qingzhou Left Guard in Shandong and a native of Laiyang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Qiheng, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Song, his grandfather Nanyu, his father Shixian, and his mother née Zou; his mother was living and his father deceased; his younger brothers were Ye and Kan, and he married a woman née Fu and subsequently a woman née Zhang; he placed sixty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 400th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zihua, registered in a civilian household in Gaoling County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Boshi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-nine years old, born on the thirtieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiben, his grandfather Yancheng, his father Qian (Administrator, granted the dress and salary of rank 4a), and his mother née Li; both parents were living; his elder brother was Zixiu and his wife née Mo; he placed sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 364th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Cunwen, registered in a civilian household in Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingkui, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Shaoqing (Assistant Prefect), his father Kecheng, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living and his wife was née Ruan; he placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Tongwen, courtesy name Zishang, was registered in a military household in Shouchang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was originally from Shenyang Guard in Liaodong. A student of the Shouchang County school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was seventh in family order, aged twenty-three, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shihong; his grandfather, Qi, served as a Registrar; his father was Qian, and his mother was née Hong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tongdao, Tongsheng, and Tongyin. He married a woman née Weng and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 388th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ziyi, courtesy name Yifang, was registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An expanded-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in family order, aged thirty-two, and born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Changyan; his grandfather, Jian; his father, Jun; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zijing. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed seventy-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Li, courtesy name Shouli, was registered in an artisan household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in family order, aged twenty-five, and born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather, Wen; his father, Rui; and his mother, née Yu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Ben, and his younger brother was Zai. He married a woman née Yan. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 356th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Yinglong, courtesy name Ruyi, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in family order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather, Liangfu, served as a Steward (dianshan); his father was Gun, and his mother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yinglin and Yingfeng. He married a woman née Feng. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yuan Zunni, registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Wu County, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Luwang; he ranked first in birth order, was forty-three years old, and was born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Zi, was granted the title of Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his father, Zhi, was an Education Intendant serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, née Ma, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his stepmother was née Wen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Menglin. His younger brothers are recorded as Mengli, who passed an examination in the xinchou year (1541); Mengqi, approved for tribute-student status; Lianbi; and Mengkui, a government student [the annotation boundaries are garbled, making the grouping uncertain [?]]. His wife was née Lao. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Mei, registered in a civilian household in Zunhua County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guangda; he ranked fourth in birth order, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Kai, his father Jing, and his mother née Meng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dong, Ying, and Lou; his younger brothers were Qiao, Song, and Nan. His wife was née Zhao. He placed twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 340th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mei Yousong, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maoqing; he ranked first in birth order, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yongxin, his grandfather Bing, his father Eryuan, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Youbai, Youli, and Youzhu. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Jiashan, registered in a civilian household in Dai Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tiheng; he ranked sixth in birth order, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Xin, and his father Qi, a Subprefectural Assistant Judge. His legal mother was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Wang. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jinshan, a Medical Officer, and Mingshan, a District Magistrate. His wife was née Sun. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiao Zichun 焦子春, courtesy name Deyuan, was registered in Dengfeng County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Min, was an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his father was Xun. His father's former wife was née Jia, and his mother was née Du. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Zimei and Zicheng, and his wife was née Gao. He placed eleventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Sizhong 張思忠, courtesy name Zizhen, was registered in Feixiang County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ben, was a Chief Office Manager; his grandfather was Wei, and his father was Dong. His legal mother was née Qiao, his stepmother née Fan, and his birth mother née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Sicheng, was an Imperial University student, and his younger brother was Silian. His wife was née Zhao; he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yide 陳懿德, courtesy name Boqiu, was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi, his grandfather Chen, his father Jue, and his mother née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tiande, Jiude, and Maode, and his wife was née Huang. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yuncheng 林雲程, courtesy name Dengqing, was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. An supplementary student at the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuxue; his grandfather, Zhaoxian, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Zhi, his mother née Zhou, and his stepmother née Su. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rongchun, and his younger brothers were Yunqiao, Yuncan, and Yunke. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

丘雲章〔貫山東青州府諸城縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治禮記，字伯卿，行三，年二十四，六月初九日生〕。曾祖玘，祖讓〔贈戶科右給事中〕，父橓〔前兵科都給事中〕，母范氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄雲崠、雲嶼，弟雲峽、雲嶠、雲峴、雲嵠、雲峕，娶王氏。山東鄉試第三名，會試第九十八名。

劉志業〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字可大，行二，年三十五，八月初七日生〕。曾祖鏻，祖源〔同知府〕，父安〔知府〕，母周氏〔封恭人〕。慈侍下，兄志中、志德，弟志和、志弘、志毅、志立，娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百二十二名。
translation_en:
Chen Wangdao, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingfu, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Fuji, his grandfather Kele, his father Tang, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wangzheng, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed sixty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 325th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Ting, registered in Boluo County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yufu, and he ranked fourth in his family. He was thirty-one years old, born on the sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Chuan, his grandfather Ji, his father Kui, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ye, Yue, Lie, Mei, Jiong, and Xie; his younger brothers were Jie and Xun. His wife was née Che, and his subsequent wife was née Zhou. He placed sixty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Yunzhang, registered in Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Boqing, and he ranked third in his family. He was twenty-four years old, born on the ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather Rang was posthumously granted the title of Right Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; his father Shun was formerly Chief Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs. His mother, née Fan, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yundong and Yunyu; his younger brothers were Yunxia, Yunjiao, Yunxian, Yunxi, and Yunshi. His wife was née Wang. He placed third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhiye, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Keda, and he ranked second in his family. He was thirty-five years old, born on the seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather Yuan was an Associate Prefect [?; the transcription reads 同知府]; his father An was a Prefect. His mother, née Zhou, was granted the title of Lady of Respect (gongren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhizhong and Zhide; his younger brothers were Zhihe, Zhihong, Zhiyi, and Zhili. His wife was née Shen. He placed fifty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

甯鈳〔貫直隸廣德州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字大受，行八，年三十四，十一月二十九日生〕。曾祖世爵，祖奎，父顯貴，母鄭氏。嚴侍下，兄鍁〔監生〕，娶步氏。應天府鄉試第五十七名，會試第一百一名。

楊時喬〔貫江西廣信府上饒縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字宜遷，行六十二，年三十五，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖傑〔醫學正科〕，祖錫，父一芳，母宋氏。慈侍下，兄時秀、時用、時化，弟時泰、時景，娶鄭氏。江西鄉試第十三名，會試第九十一名。

邵元哲〔貫貴州普安衛，軍籍，應天府上元縣人，普安州學生，治禮記，字晦之，行六，年三十六，二月二十八日生〕。曾祖璇，祖昇〔贈知縣〕，父華譜〔府同知〕，母金氏〔封太孺人〕。慈侍下，兄元吉〔貢士〕、元善〔按察司僉事〕、元高〔知縣〕，娶董氏。貴州鄉試第二名，會試第八十三名。

范伋〔貫江西瑞州府高安縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字汝希，行一，年四十七，九月初九日生〕。曾祖孔傑，祖日補，父豪，母陳氏，繼母周氏。慈侍下，弟催、僭、僎，娶高氏，繼娶王氏。江西鄉試第二十三名，會試第二百九十九名。
translation_en:
Ning Ke, courtesy name Dashou, was registered in a civilian household in Guangde Subprefecture, Zhili; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked eighth in his family, and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijue, his grandfather Kui, his father Xiangui, and his mother née Zheng; his father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother Xian was an Imperial University student, and his wife was née Bu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shiqiao, courtesy name Yiqian, was registered in a civilian household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked sixty-second in his family, and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Jie was a Chief Medical Officer; his grandfather was Xi, his father Yifang, and his mother née Song. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shixiu, Shiyong, and Shihua, and his younger brothers Shitai and Shijing; his wife was née Zheng. He placed thirteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Yuanzhe, courtesy name Huizhi, was registered in a military household in Pu’an Guard, Guizhou, and was originally from Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture; he was a student of the Pu’an subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, ranked sixth in his family, and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather Sheng was posthumously granted the title of County Magistrate; his father Huapu was a Prefectural Vice Prefect; and his mother, née Jin, was granted the title of Grand Dowager Ru Ren. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanji, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Yuanshan, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Yuangao, a County Magistrate. His wife was née Dong. He placed second in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Ji, courtesy name Ruxi, was registered in a civilian household in Gao’an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first in his family, and was aged forty-seven, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongjie, his grandfather Ribu, his father Hao, his mother née Chen, and his stepmother née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Cui, Jian, and Zhuan; he married a woman née Gao and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張明正〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字大中，行二，年三十三，四月十二日生〕。曾祖瓛，祖宗義，父士毅，母陸氏。慈侍下，兄明德，弟明治、明化、明善、明道、明教，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第八名，會試第一百八十九名。

顧褒〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字惟忠，行十九，年二十七，七月二十六日生〕。曾祖駿〔累贈右副都御史〕，祖蘭〔府同知，累贈右副都御史〕，父遂〔南京刑部右侍郎〕，嫡母嚴氏〔封淑人〕，生母呂氏。永感下，兄亷〔監生〕、䛒〔監生〕、京〔監生〕、庶、章、奕〔貢士〕、應、燮〔貢士〕，娶謝氏。應天府鄉試第八十二名，會試第一百五十三名。

韓楫〔貫山西平陽府蒲州守禦千戶所官籍，直隸揚州府泰州人，蒲州學生，治春秋，字伯通，行三，年三十五，八月初三日生〕。曾祖澤，祖霐〔義官〕，父玻〔義官〕，母薛氏。永感下，兄柟、棟，弟梅〔貢士〕、松、栻、模、權，娶傅氏，繼娶祁氏。山西鄉試第二十四名，會試第四名。
translation_en:
Gu Yangqian 顧養謙, courtesy name Yiqing, was registered in a military household in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An auxiliary student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Neng and grandfather Shan held honorary official status; his father Yao was a student of the Imperial University. His father’s former wife was Lady Qian, and his mother was Lady Shan. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Yangheng was a student of the Imperial University; his younger brothers were Yangyi, Yangguan, Yangxun, and Yanglu. He married Lady Li. He placed 103rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mingzheng 張明正, courtesy name Dazhong, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was second in family order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Zongyi, his father Shiyi, and his mother Lady Lu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Mingde; his younger brothers were Mingzhi, Minghua, Mingshan, Mingdao, and Mingjiao. He married Lady Yang. He placed eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Bao 顧褒, courtesy name Weizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He was nineteenth in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Jun received successive posthumous honors culminating in Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; his grandfather Lan was a prefectural vice prefect and likewise received successive posthumous honors culminating in Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His father Sui was Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing. His legal mother, Lady Yan, was granted the title Lady of Virtue; his birth mother was Lady Lü. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Lian, Bian 䛒, and Jing, all students of the Imperial University; Shu; Zhang; Yi, a tribute scholar; Ying; and Xie, a tribute scholar [division of the unannotated names is uncertain]. He married Lady Xie. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Ji 韓楫, courtesy name Botong, was registered in an official household of the Puzhou Guard Chiliad, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a native of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A Puzhou school student, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was third in family order, aged thirty-five, and born on the third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ze; his grandfather Hong 霐 and father Bo held honorary official status. His mother was Lady Xue. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Nan and Dong; his younger brothers were Mei, a tribute scholar, and Song, Shi, Mo, and Quan. He married Lady Fu and subsequently Lady Qi. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Guang, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in a civilian household in Nanyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, and was a native of Shunyi County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Nanyang County school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirtieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Yue; and his father was Xue. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Jiong and Yao. He married a woman née Luo. He placed twenty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xingjian, courtesy name Tiqian, was registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Qi; and his father was Geng. His mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Xingjian (行簡), Xingxiao, and Xingdao. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Ni. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Yangzhong, courtesy name Zhongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Sizhe; his grandfather was Mingshan, posthumously granted the title of Registrar; and his father was Ai. His mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yangmeng, Yanghao, and Yangchun; his younger brothers were Yangzheng, Yangyuan, Yangda, Yanglian, and Yangcai. He married a woman née Du. He placed sixty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Jujin, courtesy name Kanghou, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Gongqing; his grandfather was Guang, a Prefectural Judge; and his father was Ming. His mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Tianlun, and his younger brother was Jutai. He married a woman née Sun. He placed ninety-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

許評〔貫河南南陽府內鄉縣民籍，山西平陽府曲沃縣人，內鄉縣學生，治詩經，字公甫，行十，年三十二，閏二月二十八日生〕。曾祖貴〔壽官〕，祖曜，父存仁，母馮氏。嚴侍下，兄誠諫諒認言齡誠訓謹誌，弟謙、讓，娶李氏。河南鄉試第四十三名，會試第一百八名。

楊珂〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字士佩，行一，年三十五，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖瑩〔教諭〕，祖宜，父忠，母蔡氏。永感下，弟瓊，娶莊氏。福建鄉試第八名，會試第一百四十一名。

楊惟喬〔貫四川叙州府富順縣軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字幼植，行一，年二十九，二月十六日生〕。曾祖斌，祖東曙，父𤇍，前母陽氏，母陽氏。慈侍下，兄惟塾、惟基，弟惟藩、惟芳、惟達，娶熊氏。四川鄉試第十六名，會試第一百六十五名。

王子蕙〔貫山東濟南府武定州陽信縣民籍，直隸鳳陽府定遠縣人，國子生，治詩經，字樂秋，行二，年三十七，九月初十日生〕。曾祖侃，祖鏞，父紹先，母張氏。具慶下，兄子芹、子蘭，弟聲、子梅、子勛、子才〔進士〕、子進〔省祭官〕、子德、子實、子省、子極、子會、子通，娶李氏，繼娶郭氏。山東鄉試第五十八名，會試第三百三十六名。
translation_en:
Xu Ping 許評, registered in a civilian household in Neixiang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, was originally from Quwo County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Neixiang County School specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Gongfu and ranked tenth in birth order; he was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the intercalary second month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Yao; his father was Cunren; and his mother was née Feng. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers’ names are recorded as 誠諫諒認言齡誠訓謹誌 [division into individual names uncertain]; his younger brothers were Qian and Rang. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ke 楊珂 was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shipei and ranked first in birth order; he was thirty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a Director of Studies; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Zhong; and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Qiong, and he married a woman née Zhuang. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Weiqiao 楊惟喬 was registered in a military household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Youzhi and ranked first in birth order; he was twenty-nine years old, born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather was Dongshu; and his father was 𤇍 [reading uncertain]. His father’s former wife and his mother were both née Yang 陽. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Weishu and Weiji; his younger brothers were Weifan, Weifang, and Weida. He married a woman née Xiong. He placed sixteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zihui 王子蕙, registered in a civilian household in Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was originally from Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Leqiu and ranked second in birth order; he was thirty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Kan; his grandfather was Yong; his father was Shaoxian; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ziqin and Zilan; his younger brothers were Sheng, Zimei, Zixun, Zicai (a metropolitan graduate, jinshi), Zijin (a provincial sacrificial official [shengjiguan]), Zide, Zishi, Zixing, Ziji, Zihui 子會, and Zitong. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Guo. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 336th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Ruyi, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Junyu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cai; his grandfather, Fu; his father, Yong, a tribute scholar; and his mother, née Ding. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Rudai, Ruzhen, Ruji, and Rusi, and his wife was née Fan. He placed forty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan, registered in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county government school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Linqing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather, Jingsheng; his father, Shiguan, a titular official; and his mother, née Jia. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ji, his younger brothers were Zhe and Shi, and his wife was née Fan. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yu, registered in Meizhou, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a department government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuxiang, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Shanghe; his father, Wenyou, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Feng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers are listed as Qian, Da, and Di, and his wife was née Wu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Gao, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was Instructor at the Fengyang County government school in the Metropolitan Region, specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shouxun, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongzhu, posthumously appointed Censor-in-chief; his grandfather, Yue, posthumously appointed Registrar; and his father, Kuizong, a Registrar. His legal mother, née Wu, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his birth mother was also née Wu. His parents were deceased. The annotation lists elder brothers Shan, Shuo, Jian, and Xu, and younger brothers Feng, Qian, Zan, Shen, Cheng, Xiao, Tai, Jing, Mi, An, Jin, Jiu [?], Bao, Zhun, Dang, and Lun. His wife was née Zheng. He placed seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dai Dali, registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ziyong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Rong, his father Jing, and his mother née Ding; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dabu, Daxiang, Dazhen, and Dazhi, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xinde, registered in a civilian household in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and originally from Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, was an expanded-quota student at the Deqing County school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanjing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, a Magistrate; his grandfather was Fenglai, an Imperial University student; his father was Ruyi, and his mother née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xinzheng, Xincun, and Xinxue, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Ce, registered in a civilian household in Yanling County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Duizhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen; his grandfather Shiwan and father Jin both held honorary official status for acts of public beneficence; his mother was née Lang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living, and his wife was née Chang. He placed seventy-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Yingqian, registered in a military household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shunzhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhitong, his grandfather Yixun, his father Jisheng, his mother née Ye, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huo Weijin, registered in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Aifu; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather Jun and father Guangxian were county magistrates. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Weihan, Weifan (a registrar), and Weiyuan; his younger brother was Weijian. His wife was née Wei. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Luowen, registered in Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Qitu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the first day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xin received the honorary title of Secretariat Drafter; his grandfather Jingming was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant; his father Li was a prefectural vice prefect. His mother was née Dai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Luoshu and Luoying, and his wife was née Gao. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Ruchu, registered in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Daoqiao; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-two, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ruhe was posthumously awarded the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather Chun ze was a prefect; his father Yingliang was Right Vice Minister of Revenue. His mother, née Zheng, received the title of Lady of Peace (anren). His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brothers were Ruyue and Ruqian, and his wife was née Gong. He placed thirteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lai Tinggui, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Erzhou; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanchou, his grandfather Chaoxun, and his father Jimei; his mother was née Zhuang. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brother was Tingpian, and his wife was née Tu. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃才敏〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣，民籍，府學附學生，治禮記，字爾懋，行五，年三十，九月十二日生〕。曾祖敷道，祖重堅，父瑄，前母盧氏，母許氏，繼母許氏、張氏。永感下，兄懷仁、懷禮、懷智、士敏，弟學敏，娶田氏。福建鄉試第一名，會試第十名。

戴洵〔貫浙江寧波府奉化縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字汝誠，行一，年三十二，八月十二日生〕。曾祖儼，祖珏，父𪐔，母竺氏。具慶下，娶嚴氏。浙江鄉試第七十八名，會試第九十五名。
translation_en:
Shi Guanmin, courtesy name Yuwo, was a registered native of Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, of civilian household registration, and an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. He ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wenquan, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Jimao; his father was Jianke; and his mother was née He. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guanlan, and his younger brothers were Guangui, Guanfa, Guanshan, Guanzhi, and Guanchao. He married a woman née He. He placed ninetieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Dashun, courtesy name Jingxi, was a registered native of Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, of civilian household registration, and a student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked twenty-fourth among his brothers, was aged forty-three, and was born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Zao, was granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works and posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, Left Vice Minister of War, and concurrently Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Xie, was Left Vice Minister of War and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of War. His father, Shixian, was Registrar of the Court of State Ceremonial and was granted the title of Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. His mother, née Han, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (Ruren). His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Dalin, a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy, and Daheng, an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Caimin, courtesy name Ermao, was a registered native of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, of civilian household registration, and a supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites. He ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Fudao; his grandfather was Zhongjian; and his father was Xuan. His father's former wife was née Lu, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmothers were née Xu and née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Huairen, Huaili, Huaizhi, and Shimin, and his younger brother was Xuemin. He married a woman née Tian. He placed first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Xun, courtesy name Rucheng, was a registered native of Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, of military household registration, and a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather was Jue; his father's name is written 𪐔 [reading uncertain]; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Yan. He placed seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳學詩〔貫江西瑞州府上高縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字伯興，行八，年三十二，十月初六日生〕。曾祖鐔，祖治邦，父詔，前母李氏，母王氏。慈侍下，兄興書，弟興禮，娶況氏。江西鄉試第八名，會試第五十五名。

喬懋敬〔貫直隸松江府上海縣，軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字允德，行一，年三十一，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖嶽，祖積〔州判官〕，父訓〔縣丞〕，嫡母顧氏，生母胡氏。慈侍下，兄維翰〔如京，監生〕，弟如陵、如阜、如隄、允胤、如斗，娶陳氏，繼娶張氏。應天府鄉試第九十名，會試第七十名。

徐時可〔貫湖廣黃州府黃岡縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治禮記，字惟易，行四，年三十二，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖大成，祖榮，父尚義，母萬氏。具慶下，兄時中〔縣丞〕，弟時同，娶袁氏，繼娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第二十八名，會試第三百十七名。
translation_en:
Zhang Chun 張純, registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuoheng; he ranked eighth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xingyuan, who held an honorary office for longevity; his grandfather was Jusheng; his father was Min; and his mother was née Chen. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun, Hongqi, Qiaoqi, and Huiqi; his younger brothers were Keqi, Guanqi, Tingqi, Chuqi, Cai, Ao, Song, and Yizi [the division of the final names is uncertain]. His wife was née Huang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Xueshi 吳學詩, registered in Shanggao County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boxing; he ranked eighth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tan; his grandfather was Zhibang; his father was Zhao; his father's former wife was née Li; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Xingshu, and his younger brother was Xingli. His wife was née Kuang. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Maojing 喬懋敬, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yunde; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yue; his grandfather was Ji, a subprefectural assistant judge; and his father was Xun, a county vice magistrate. His legal mother was née Gu, and his birth mother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Weihan; the accompanying annotation reads “Rujing, Imperial University student” [?]. His younger brothers were Ruling, Rufu, Rudi, Yunyin, and Rudou. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed ninetieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shike 徐時可, registered in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Weiyi; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Dacheng; his grandfather was Rong; his father was Shangyi; and his mother was née Wan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shizhong, a county vice magistrate, and his younger brother was Shitong. He married a woman née Yuan and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Youyuan, registered in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuchu. First in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuo, his grandfather Ji, and his father Liangdong; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Youyue, Yourui, Youying, and Youjie. His wife was née Xu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Weicheng, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an added student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Banghan. First in birth order, he was thirty-nine years old and was born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren, his grandfather Mao, and his father Shiyong, an Assistant Prefect; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Yang. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Shixi, Weining, Weicong, Weiming, Weiying, and Weishi. His wife was née Zheng. He placed fifty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third Class: 314 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Sheng Dangshi, courtesy name Mingfu, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Song, his grandfather Wei, his father Chi, and his mother née Yao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Yushi and his younger brother Yaoshi. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Lu. He placed thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Guoning, courtesy name Ziqing, was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was tenth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Qinheng received the honorary title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Cheng was a Prefect; and his father Bocong was an Usher. His mother was née Nie and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guoshen, Guolan, Guocai, Guochao, Guolai, Guoxun, and Guoshu. He married a woman née Xu. He placed forty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Li, courtesy name Zhonghua, was registered in a military household of Guide Guard, Henan, and was a native of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An expanded-quota student of the Guide prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Zhong was officially honored as a filial son and posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Rites. His grandfather Han was a Prefect and was advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master of the Second Rank (Yazhong dafu). His father was Du and his mother née Song; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guang, Can, Yao, Xi, and Lie; his younger brothers were Lin, Gu, Luo, an unclear name transcribed as “I” [?], and Lu. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tu Menggui, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shifang; he ranked ninth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue kui (Yuekui 曰逵), his grandfather Qingzhi, his father Jia, and his mother née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mengyan and Mengyang, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed seventy-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Guangpan, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the county government school, specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jizhao; he ranked ninth in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuxia, his grandfather Jing, his father Wencui, and his mother née Guo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Guangjin, Guangyu, Guangdian, Guanghan, Guangshi, Guangyao (a tribute scholar), Guangyu (光虞, an Imperial University student), and Guangzhou; his younger brothers were Guangxue, Guangye, and Guangtai. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Quanneng, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Rucai; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin (濦); his grandfather Shi held the conferred title of Secretary in the Ministry of War; his father Kan was a prefect; and his mother, née Huang, held the conferred title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother Quanxian was an Imperial University student, and his younger brothers were Quanlian, Quanliang, Quancheng, and Quanhe. His wife was née Song. He placed 103rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Shixu, registered in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zishu; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Ang, and his father Xie, who held the honorary designation of Righteous Official. His legal mother was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Tao. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His wife was née Pang; he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He placed one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Zhi, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yijing; he ranked thirtieth in his family’s birth order, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Fuhua, was Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Jiansu; his grandfather, Wei, was Investigating Censor for the Sichuan Circuit; and his father, Aoshan, was Censor of Education. His father’s former wife, née Ouyang, had been granted the title Lady (Ruren); his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone survived. His elder brother Zhi was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his younger brother Cheng was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Peng. He placed fortieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shichen, registered in an official household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruxian; he ranked first in his family’s birth order, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongmei; his grandfather, Li, held the honorary designation Official for Righteous Conduct; his father, Yao, was a Clerk; and his mother was née Zhao. His father alone survived. His younger brothers were Shichang, Shinan, and Shike. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Yilin, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked first in his family’s birth order, was forty-three years old, and was born on the eleventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhen; his grandfather, Fu, was a School Instructor; his father, Yin, was a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yi’e, Yifeng, Yikui, and Yiqi. He married a woman née Chu. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wenhuan, registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruzhao; he ranked fourth in his family’s birth order, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuchu; his grandfather was Ji; his father was Lian; and his mother was née Wan. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Wenchang, Wenhe, Wensui, a Messenger, and Wenhuang; his younger brothers were Wenzhuo and Wenxiu. He married a woman née He. He placed seventy-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Liangzuo, registered in Wanzai County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shouzhong; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qichun, his grandfather Xiang, his father Yi 頣, and his mother née Xin. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zhong. He placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Wanzhong, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional-quota student at the prefectural school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanliang; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-four, and was born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, posthumously appointed Prefectural Judge; his grandfather was Yingyin, Prefectural Judge; his father was Congyuan, and his mother née Gu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wanyan, Wanli, and Wanji; his wife was née Cai. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Daheng, registered in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenfu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Lin, his father Jingxian, and his mother née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Dachao and his younger brother Daji; his wife was née Yin. He placed thirteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Xizhou, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Sijian; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Changning, his father Jin, and his mother née Wei. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Xiyuan, Xizhong, and Xixiao; his wife was née Jin. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.
