translation_en:
Xu Shouqian, registered in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Zishou, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Zan; his father, Jin, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Su, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shouyue, and his younger brothers were Shoulu and Shoucheng; his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Zhe, registered in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Zidong, ranked seventh among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Song, a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; his grandfather, Chou; and his father, Can. His father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Bian, an Instructor, and his younger brothers were Huai and Han; he married a woman née Jiang, then successively women née Huang and née Wang. He placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Yance, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Tingchen, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bozheng; his grandfather, Weiliang, an honorary official; his father, Bangning; and his mother, née Jin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yanshu and Yanshu (言書 and 言疏); his wife was née Yang. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yunzhong, registered in Zunhua County, Jizhou Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Zuyao, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather, Chong; his father, Wenjian; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shizhong, Jianzhong, and Shouzhong, the last a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Yongzhong, Qizhong, Shangzhong, Lizhong, and Zhizhong. His wife was née Ju. He placed fifty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 322nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Bangqi, courtesy name Juncai, was registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiao, his grandfather Ruxiu, his father Hua, and his mother née Shen; his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Bangyan, and his younger brothers were Bangjun, Bangyong, Bangzai, Bangchong, Bangliang, Bangcai, and Bangzhi. He married a woman née Mao and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 382nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Shiqiao, courtesy name Yingwang, was registered in a civilian household in Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a native of Xinyu County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ketai; his grandfather, Can, held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father was Jiugao, his mother née Yang, and his stepmother née Zeng; his father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Pi and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed forty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Gong, courtesy name Duqing, was registered in a military household of the Liu'ao Battalion under the Zhenhai Guard, Fujian. An annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Lu, held an honorary official title awarded for longevity; his grandfather was Yong, his father Tingxian, and his mother née Cai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhongzheng, Sijing, and Zhongqin, and his younger brothers were Sizhong, Sicong, Siyi, and Zhongren. He married a woman née Chen. He placed 130th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 355th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanxi, courtesy name Huaiguo, was registered in a civilian household in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qiong, held an honorary official title awarded for longevity; his grandfather, Zhong, was an annual tribute student. His father was Fang and his mother née Feng; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zimei, Director of a School of Yin and Yang, Yiyang, Rugao, Ru'an, and Ruyong. His younger brothers were Sanmei, Sanpin, Sanjie, Sanzhai, Zikuan, Yi, and Shiyi [the division of the final names is uncertain]. He married a woman née Jin and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed thirteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guang Mao, courtesy name Ziying, was registered in Yangxin County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jing held an honorary office for longevity; his grandfather Xiang was a Magistrate; his father was Xiezhi, and his mother was née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Enrong, a Registrar, Rujia, and Fuhua; his younger brothers were Yu and Xian. His wife was née Tian. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mengnan, courtesy name Yuansi, was registered in Zhongmou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Song held prestige rank; his grandfather Jizu was an Adjudicator; his father was Wenjiao, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Mengru and Mengxian. His wife was née Zhu. He placed seventy-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhili, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Gu was granted the title of Magistrate; his grandfather Zhi was a Provincial Administration Commissioner; his father Keda was an Imperial University student, and his mother was née Gu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhiyu and Zhizhong; his younger brothers were Zhijing, Zhizhang, Zhibi, Zhifa, Zhice, and Zhimao. His wife was née Sheng. He placed 132nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Fengchun, courtesy name Shuren, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shirong; his grandfather Jingxian was granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father Xuan was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works; and his mother, née Luo, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brother Fengyang was an Imperial University student, and his younger brother was Fenghuai. His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cui Xingke, courtesy name Shifu, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Tianjing; his grandfather, Shiyong; his father, Yi, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; and his mother, née Peng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiuke, Dake, Jike, Sike, Yuke, Qike, and Shuke. He married a woman née Li. He placed tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Xuan, courtesy name Bangding, was registered in a civilian household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was originally from Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Zhangzhou prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Qing; his father, Luan, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhong, Jing, and Yue. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Tingchen, courtesy name Jinchen, was registered in a civilian household in Dehua County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Zhigang; his father, Feng; and his mother, née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingfu. He married a woman née Dai. He placed sixty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sui Fu, courtesy name Zixiu, was registered in a civilian household in Yutai County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Shi; his father, Ou, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née Han. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yin, Lin, Wan, Yan, and Ye; his younger brothers were Fang, Ju, and Mai. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently women née Li and née Kan. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Fen, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yongqing; he ranked fourth in birth order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Wenji, and his father Ji; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bi, a tribute scholar, and Shijie. He married a woman née Lin. He placed forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qu Cong, registered in Dianjiang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Fengting; he ranked fifth in birth order, was aged forty, and was born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather was Zigang; and his father was Heling, a Professor. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, Chong, Qiao, Fei, and Fan; his younger brother was Gong. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Jiying, registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Lehua; he ranked eighth in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongliang, his grandfather Zhichen, and his father Bencheng, who held an honorary official title granted for longevity. His father's former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Liu. His mother survived, but his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Mei, Zuo, Jie, Wei, Kan, Yan, and Chuan, a Registry Manager. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed tenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Jiugong, registered in Nanyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yunzhi; he ranked second in birth order, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Sicong, and his father Zhi; his mother was née Ning, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His father survived, but his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Jiude, Jiujing, and Jiushao; his younger brothers were Jiuxu, Jiufa, and Jiuguan. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Xiechun, courtesy name Fuyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; fourth in family order, he was aged twenty-nine and born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongqi, his grandfather Hu, his father Wengong, and his mother née Xie; his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Dafu, Jianchun, and Changchun, and his younger brothers Xuchun and Hongchun; he married a woman née Fang. He ranked eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Liangchen, courtesy name Xiangsheng, was registered in a civilian household in Gong'an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; first in family order, he was aged thirty-one and born on the first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Youxin, his father Lin, a County Vice Magistrate, and his mother née Chen; his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Liangcai and Lianggui; he married a woman née Lan. He ranked tenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Jugen, courtesy name Bocheng, was registered in a civilian household in Xiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; first in family order, he was aged thirty-five and born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Jun was a County Vice Magistrate, his grandfather Xiang a Registrar, and his father Zhen a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate; his mother was née Yan and his stepmother née Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Juzhen, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Jukun, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, and Jujing; he married a woman née Li. He ranked eighteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yingyuan, courtesy name Wenzong, was registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Jingyang County; he was an added-quota student at the Sanyuan county school specializing in the Book of Changes. Second in family order, he was aged thirty-five and born on the first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui, his grandfather Qing, and his father Jiaxing, who held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father's former wife was née Dong and his mother née Liu. Both his parents were living. His elder brother Yingkui was an Imperial University student, and his younger brother was Yingqi; he married a woman née Li. He ranked sixty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Dalie, registered in a military household in Daye County, Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanzuo, he ranked ninth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ji was a County Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather Zongzhi was a Prefect granted advancement to the privilege of wearing third-rank official dress; his father Nan was a County Magistrate; his father's former wife and his mother were both née Liu. Both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Daxun, and his wife was née Yin. He placed twenty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Rulin, registered in a civilian household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and originally from Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziren, he ranked sixteenth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jing was a Salt Transport Commissioner; his grandfather Bin was a County Vice Magistrate granted the honorary title of Commandant of Military Police; his father Jie was a Judicial Examiner; his father's principal wife was née Bao, and his birth mother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Yingshi, a Recorder in the Directorate of Imperial Parks, Ying'en, Yingxiao, and Ruqi, an Imperial University student; his younger brother Yingming was also an Imperial University student, and his wife was née Shen. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Zhihan, registered in a civilian household in Wu'an County, Ci Subprefecture, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuanqing, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather Zhao was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Fei, and his mother was née Shi. His parents and grandparents were living; his elder brother was Peng, his younger brothers were He, Zhifan, Zhifu, E, and Zhi'ou, and his wife was née Sun. He placed twenty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wangdao, registered in a civilian household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Mengfu, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hou, his grandfather was Hong, his father was Wan, and his mother was née Tao. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Wangyan and Wangjiao, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wei Timing, registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and a native of Fuqing County, was an additional student of the Houguan County School specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yonghui; he ranked first in family birth order, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the thirtieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather, Shirang; his father, Dexiang; and his mother, née Lin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Chaoyu, Chaoying, Chaojue, Chaozan, Chaoke, and Chaokun. He married a woman née Yang. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dalan, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Guanfu; he ranked fifth in family birth order, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Xuan, and grandfather, Zhi, both held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; his father was Shijie, and his mother was née Fu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Shicai, Dajin, and Dachen; his younger brothers were Dalu, Dahao, Dahong, Dahuai, and Dashen. He married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ziqi, registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shiqing; he ranked 146th in family birth order, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Chu; his grandfather, Zhen; his father, Fa, a Registrar; and his mother, née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ziye 子業 and Ziye 子葉. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiangkun, registered in an artisan household in Xincheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was an added student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zihou; he ranked second in family birth order, was twenty years old, and was born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Lin, was a Professor, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Chongguang, was an Assistant Administration Commissioner, posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his father, Zhihan, was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Yu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Xiangqian; his younger brothers were Xiangmeng, Xiangtai, Xiangzhen, Xiangben, Xiangjin, and Xiangli. He married a woman née Tian. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Shirun, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Weide, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the eleventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Fu, and his father Jing; his mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Wu, his parents were living, his younger brothers were Shiqian and Shichun, his wife was née Hong, and he placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yaoqing, registered in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zongshun, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Qi, and his father Haichao, a prestige official; his mother was née Li, and both parents were living; his younger brothers were Yuqing, Wenqing, and Wuqing, his wife was née Geng, and he placed ninety-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 377th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Minmu, registered in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Naixi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mei, his grandfather Dang, and his father Shi, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his mother was née Duan, and both parents were living; his elder brother was Minwang, his younger brothers were Minkun and Minhua, his wife was née Li, and he placed sixty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Ji, registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shanqing. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shangzhong, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Juqi, a County Magistrate; his father was Liuxue, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xu, and his wife was née Jin. He placed sixty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundred fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nie Tingbi, registered in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zuyong. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Mu, who held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather was Man, an Instructor in the Nanjing Directorate of Education; his father was Jian, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingjin, Tingyu, and Tingluan. His wife was née Hu; he subsequently married a woman née Zheng. He placed twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhixue, registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shengchu. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Xian; his father was Kui, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Ge. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhili, and his wife was née Gao. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Yangbi, registered in Anxi County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruqin. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jing, a Department Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Gui, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; and his father was Yuan, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His legal mother was née Wu, and his birth mother was née Huang. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yanggao, a student of the Directorate of Education; Bin, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and Yangtai. His younger brother was Yangcheng, and his wife was née Huang. He placed one hundred sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guan Daxun, courtesy name Shichen, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in the civilian registration category. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Fu; and his father, Zhi. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Daxi, and his younger brothers were Datao and Dazhao. His wife was née Yu. He ranked second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dao, courtesy name Yizhong, was registered in Hukou County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in the civilian registration category. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Hao; and his father, Shishan, who held an honorary official title for longevity. His mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shan, Yi, and Kui, and his younger brothers were Yun and Su. His wife was née Ke. He ranked fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 359th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jiaxiang, courtesy name Junqing, was registered in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, in the civilian registration category, and was originally from Kelan Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, a prefectural adjutant; his grandfather, Chou; and his father, Feng. His mother was née Zou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bai and Cai. His wife was née Kang. He ranked forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Chun, courtesy name Shuwen, was registered in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in the civilian registration category. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mian; his grandfather, Huai; and his father, Chaofeng, who held an honorary official title for longevity. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Bian. His wife was née Li. He ranked first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 351st in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
徐維楫〔貫錦衣衛旗籍，山東濟南府武定州人，順天府學生，治春秋，字汝進，行四，年三十三，四月二十九日生〕。曾祖廣，祖政〔贈工部郎中〕，父淮〔戶部郎中〕，前母谷氏，母范氏。永感下。兄良棟〔錦衣衛總旗〕、維榦〔貢士〕、維梅、維霖。娶李氏。順天府鄉試第六十七名，會試第七十六名。

佘嘉詔〔貫廣東廣州府順德縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字彥綸，行三，年二十七，九月十七日生〕。曾祖安，祖直，父記亨，嫡母陶氏，生母張氏。慈侍下。兄嘉謨〔監生〕、嘉謀，弟嘉誥。娶霍氏。廣東鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百三十五名。

姚繼可〔貫河南開封府許州襄城縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字光父，行一，年三十二，八月初三日生〕。曾祖偉，祖澤〔贈兵部主事〕，父汝皐〔布政司參議〕，前母黃氏〔封安人〕，母白氏。慈侍下。弟繼大、繼久。娶趙氏。河南鄉試第十八名，會試第三百九十八名。

丁應賓〔貫湖廣常德府龍陽縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字聘之，行二，年三十二，閏二月十三日生〕。曾祖鑰，祖永成〔壽官〕，父奎〔訓導〕，母熊氏。重慶下。弟應宿、應宸、應寮、應寀、應宦、應寵、應宇、應宣、應宙。娶杜氏。湖廣鄉試第十三名，會試第三百八十六名。
translation_en:
Xu Weiji, courtesy name Rujin, was registered in a banner household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Shuntian prefectural school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked fourth in his family, was thirty-three sui, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather, Zheng, was posthumously appointed a bureau director in the Ministry of Works; and his father, Huai, was a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father's former wife was née Gu, and his mother was née Fan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Liangdong, a platoon commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; Weigan, a tribute scholar; Weimei; and Weilin. His wife was née Li. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

She Jiazhao, courtesy name Yanlun, was registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county-school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked third in his family, was twenty-seven sui, and was born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather was Zhi, and his father was Jiheng. His legal mother was née Tao, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Jiamo, a student of the Imperial University, and Jiamou; his younger brother was Jiagao. His wife was née Huo. He placed thirty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Jike, courtesy name Guangfu, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangcheng County, Xu Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county-school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first in his family, was thirty-two sui, and was born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei; his grandfather, Ze, was posthumously appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War; and his father, Rugao, was an administration assistant in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father's former wife, née Huang, had been granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother was née Bai. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Jida and Jijiu. His wife was née Zhao. He placed eighteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 398th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Yingbin, courtesy name Pinzhi, was registered in a military household in Longyang County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang. An added student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked second in his family, was thirty-two sui, and was born on the thirteenth day of the intercalary second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue; his grandfather, Yongcheng, held an honorary longevity title; and his father, Kui, was an assistant instructor. His mother was née Xiong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yingsu, Yingchen, Yingliao, Yingcai, Yinghuan, Yingchong, Yingyu, Yingxuan, and Yingzhou. His wife was née Du. He placed thirteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 386th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shu Ao, of Dexing County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zihua; he ranked forty-ninth in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huang; his grandfather, Ze, was a Registrar; his father was Gai, and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jie, Xu, and Mo, and his wife was née Ye. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Ruhan, of Wanquan County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an expanded-quota student of the school of the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhaofu; he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather was Jun; his father, Dan, held an honorary official rank; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Rujun, an Imperial University student, Rujian, Ruhong, Ruwei, and Ruhuan; his younger brothers were Rucheng, Rujia, Rubing, and Ruwu. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently another woman née Chen. He placed thirtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 326th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shenxiu, of Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jingsi; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ben, was an annual tribute student; his grandfather, Conglong, received the honorary title of Prefectural Vice Prefect; and his father, Wanbi, was a Prefectural Vice Prefect promoted to the prestige title Grand Master for Administrative Service. His mother, née Gao, received the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mengheng, and his younger brothers were Shenji and Shendong. His wife was née Jiang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Yunzhe, of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Boming; he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qing, was posthumously awarded the title Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather, Kui, received successive posthumous honors culminating in that title; and his father, En, was retired Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father's former wife, née Bao, was posthumously awarded the title Lady (furen), and his mother, née Cao, received the same title. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yunduan, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; Yunmu; Yunxiu, an Imperial University student; Yunliang, a Recorder in the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent; Yunzang; Yunzheng; Yunda, an Imperial University student; Yunsu; Yunzhong; Yunhe, an Imperial University student; and Yunjia. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Xiang. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐元太〔貫直隸寧國府宣城縣，儒籍，府學生，治易經，字汝賢，行七，年二十九，閏十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖愈〔歲貢生〕，祖訪〔將仕郎〕，父衢〔主簿〕，母劉氏。具慶下，兄元策〔貢士〕、元氣〔南京兵部郎中〕、元朗、元第、元釋、元遵，弟元祉、元則、元禋、元禎、元禮、元祝，娶劉氏。應天府鄉試第二名，會試第二十七名。
translation_en:
Tan Yingyuan 覃應元, courtesy name Defang, was registered in a military household of the Mayi Defense Battalion under the Shanxi Regional Military Commission. A student of the Datong prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Biao; and his father, Huan. His father's principal wife was née Liu, and his birth mother was née Cao. His parents and grandparents were deceased. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Tun 趙焞, courtesy name Ziming, was registered in a military household in Pingyuan County, Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather, Jian; his father, Hui; and his mother, née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hui, Ye, Yi, and Ran. He married a woman née Cai. He placed sixty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Zichen 熊子臣, courtesy name Guoshi, was registered in a military household in Xinchang County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student on the expanded quota of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dongqi; his grandfather, Tian; his father, Yizhuang; and his mother, née Zou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Erchen, and his younger brothers were Qichen and Sichen. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 373rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yuantai 徐元太, courtesy name Ruxian, was registered in a scholarly household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was seventh in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-first day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Fang, Gentleman for Attending Service; his father was Qu, a Registrar; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuance, a Metropolitan Examination graduate; Yuanqi, a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of War; Yuanlang; Yuandi; Yuanshi; and Yuanzun. His younger brothers were Yuanzhi, Yuanze, Yuanyin, Yuanzhen, Yuanli, and Yuanzhu. He married a woman née Liu. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Fang, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shucheng, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bogui, his grandfather Jiang, and his father Xiang; his father's principal wife was née Hu, and his birth mother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Fuhui, and his wife was née Wang. He placed eighty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Ruqi, registered in a civilian household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Renqing, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-one, born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather Xiang, his father Yongping, and his mother née Han. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Ruji and Rucan. He placed seventy-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 305th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Yingyuan, registered in a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yunqing, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Rong, his father Gang, and his mother née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Yingshi, and he married a woman née Qin and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed forty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Fa, registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Cuizhang, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hu, his grandfather Chuan, his father Pian, and his mother née Deng. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Qi, Han, and Tao, and his younger brothers Man, Yi, and Bian; he was betrothed to a woman née Liang. He placed third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 335th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xiong Wei 熊煒, registered in Jianchang County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tiankui, he ranked eighth in family birth order, and he was thirty-three sui, born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zilin; his grandfather, Xuan, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Dong, and his mother was née Yue. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Huan, and his younger brothers were Lang, Zhuo, Tun, Jiong, and Kun. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed thirty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Weining 丁惟寧, registered in Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yangjing, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was twenty-four sui, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongben; his grandfather was Zhen; his father, Chun, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu, and his younger brother was Weiyi. He married a woman née Ji. He placed thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xi 王璽, registered in Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuxin, he ranked eleventh in family birth order, and he was forty sui, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yukuan; his grandfather was Tingliang; his father was Shao, and his mother was née Qiu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bi, Bao, Ying, and Kui. He married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 379th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Yizheng 龔以正 was registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household, and was a native of Nanchang County. He was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dezhen, he ranked fourth in family birth order, and he was thirty-eight sui, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maosheng; his grandfather, Jin, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Mu, and his mother was née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Yicong. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed thirty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xiang Cheng, courtesy name Zongluo, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked thirty-fifth in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Shizheng, and his father En; his father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Lu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Chou and Zhu. He married a woman née Yang. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yuan, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in a civilian household in Xincheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Hong, and his father Yunyan; his legal mother was née Zhou, and his birth mother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yuan 源 and Tan, and his younger brother was Lan. He married a woman née Jing. He placed twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Menglong, courtesy name Zizheng, was registered in a military household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked eleventh in family order and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian, his grandfather Huan, and his father Lin; his mother was née Tang, and his stepmother was née Yu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jing, Hou (a subprefectural assistant magistrate), Yao, Ji, and Ping; his younger brothers were Yichun, Shan, and Jia. He married a woman née Shen. He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 393rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zi, courtesy name Guoqi, was registered in a civilian household in Shiping Subprefecture, Lin'an Prefecture, Yunnan. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third in family order and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Shi, and his father Ying; his mother was née Duan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qin and Quan. He married a woman née Sun. He placed first in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yue Weihua, registered in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruxi; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather was Ling, a Recorder of Good Deeds; his father was Ke, and his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brothers were Weihuo, Weisong, Weikun, and Weilun. His wife was née Li. He placed thirtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gongda, registered in Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Deqian; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the intercalary tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zan, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Zhengqi; his father was Chongben, a Judicial Officer; his mother was née Pang, and his stepmothers were née Liu and née Ren. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brothers were Gonggao, an Assistant Administration Commissioner, and Gongheng; his younger brothers were Gongjin and Gongqing. His wife was née Zhou. He placed twelfth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tianzeng, registered in Yi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wenyi, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Jiong, an Instructor; his father was Shi, and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tianci, Tianfu, and Tianze. His wife was née Shu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Keda, registered with the Qinzhou Defense Battalion in Shanxi, belonged to an official household and was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yefu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wu, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Tingchong, a Registrar; his father was Fengchun, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kejiu. His first wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Wei. He placed eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 397th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Lun, registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zida; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zuo, an Assistant Prefect; his grandfather was Lü; his father was Xiao; and his mother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tong, Dai, Xun, and Jun. He married a woman née Tong and subsequently a woman née Pei. He placed fifty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Honghui, registered in Ding'an County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an附生 additional student at the county school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaochuan; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zeng; his grandfather was Xi; his father was Yunsheng; and his mother was née Mo. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Hongmo, Hongzhao, and Honggao; his younger brother was Hong'e. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shuling, registered in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhiyi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Ding and grandfather Wei both held honorary official status for longevity. His father was Yan; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Tian. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shuqiao, Shutong, Shuzeng, Shudan, Shujin, Shucan, and Shuji. He married a woman née Yu. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 360th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Huan, registered in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenguang; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the fifteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xiu; his grandfather Hui held honorary official status for public beneficence; his father Meng was a Prefectural School Instructor; and his mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yao, and his younger brother was Can. He married a woman née Qian. He placed fifty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Bo 張博, courtesy name Ziyue, was registered in a military household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Shanyin County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang Qi, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; his grandfather was Zhang Ci, granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Zhang Qia, an Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Niu, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Bo 愽, and his wife was née Chen. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Mu 楊沐, courtesy name Zixin, was registered in a civilian household in Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Yang Siming, and grandfather, Yang Yongning, both held honorary official status granted for longevity. His father was Yang Zhong, a Ceremonial Usher; his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Huai. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Qing, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence, and Run, a student of the Directorate of Education. His wife was née Li. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yitong 張一通, courtesy name Ruda, was registered in a military household in Ningjin County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang Lian, a Prefect; his grandfather was Zhang Sheng; his father was Zhang Cunxing; his mother was née Lu; and his stepmother was née Yang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Yiguan and Yile, and his younger brother was Yibian. His wife was née Duan. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 394th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shi 程實, courtesy name Shizhang, was registered in a military household in Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Cheng Ci; his grandfather was Cheng Kan, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; his father was Cheng Zhou, a Food Service Officer; and his mother was née Yang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Yin. He married a woman née Wei and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xie Shiyan, registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruxin, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Kezan, his grandfather Yu, and his father Mingzhi (an annual tribute student); his mother was née Xu, and his father alone was living. His elder brother was Shicheng (a tribute scholar), and his younger brothers were Shizeng, Shiyin, Shifu, Shidan, and Shiqi; he married a woman née Zhu and ranked thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fengzheng, registered in a military household in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shunfu, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirtieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shihong, his grandfather Xun (an Instructor), and his father Xilian; his mother was née Wang, and his parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Fengbiao, Fengqi, Fengzhu, and Fengtu; he married a woman née Cai and ranked forty-fifth in both the Fujian Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shi, registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student at the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Mengjing, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yugao (posthumously granted the title of Minister of War at Nanjing), his grandfather Wanping (additionally granted that title posthumously), and his father Sui (Minister of War at Nanjing, participating in the direction of military affairs); his mother was née Lai (additionally granted the title of Lady posthumously), and his stepmother was née Yan (granted the title of Lady). His father and stepmother were living. His elder brothers were Shu (a student admitted by imperial grace), Ge (an Assistant Commander), Hang (a tribute student), and Xiang (a District Magistrate); his younger brothers were Cai (a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice), Pu (a National University student), Jing, Cheng, Zhen, Yue, and Rong. He married a woman née Xiong and ranked ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yide, registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou Subprefecture, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shiyu, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ji (a Registrar), his grandfather Bi, and his father Mi; his mother was née Zhao, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Junde (a sacrificial attendant, shengjiguan) and Xuande; he married a woman née Qin and ranked forty-fourth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

潘仲徽〔貫福建福州府侯官縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字克典，行二，年三十，四月三十日生〕。曾祖裕〔壽官〕，祖景，父積中，母吳氏。慈侍下，兄伯徵，弟叔衡、季德、季循、季復，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第六名，會試第三百六十五名。
translation_en:
Li Zhizhen, registered in Shifang County, Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xiqing; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Bencong; his grandfather, Yi; and his father, Shu. His father's principal wife was née Zhu, and his birth mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingzheng, and his younger brothers were Zhongzhen and Shuzhen. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wenzhu, registered in Mianyang Subprefecture, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yushu; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather, Pan, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of War; and his father, Bai, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Ren, was granted the title Lady of Tranquility. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wenbing, an Imperial University student, and Wenxie; his younger brothers were Wenwei, Wenyang, Wenjiong, Wenkuang, and Wenxuan. He married a woman née Tong. He placed seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 342nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Zhao, registered in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maoqing; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Xue; and his father, □□ [name illegible]. His mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Desheng and Deci. He married a woman née Xu. He placed fifty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Zhonghui, registered in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kedian; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the thirtieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Jizhong. His mother was née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Bozheng, and his younger brothers were Shuheng, Jide, Jixun, and Jifu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 365th in the Metropolitan Examination.

駱問禮〔貫浙江紹興府諸暨縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字子本，行五十九，年三十九，十二月十三日生〕。曾祖進，祖鳳韶，父驂，母鄭氏。具慶下，娶樓氏。浙江鄉試第十名，會試第六十五名。

陶允淳〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字懋初，行十四，年二十五，十月十九日生〕。曾祖諧〔兵部左侍郎，贈兵部尚書〕，祖師賢〔鴻臚寺主簿，封翰林院編修〕，父大順〔同科進士〕，母諸氏。重慶下，弟允端、允嘉，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第八十三名，會試第九十名。
translation_en:
Zheng Yixin, courtesy name Junyun, was registered in a civilian household in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanlang; his grandfather was Chen, a School Instructor; his father was Jingshan; his mother was née Guo, and his successive stepmothers were née Wang, Hu, and Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yiqian, and his younger brothers were Yiwei, Yijun, Yilian, Ju [?], Yizuo, and Yiluan. He married a woman née Zhuang and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Pingshan, courtesy name Minwang, was registered in a civilian household in Zitong County, Jian Subprefecture, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was forty-six years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather was Shiying, his father was Yue, and his mother was née Tao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Weishan, and he married a woman née Peng. He placed forty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 327th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Wenli, courtesy name Ziben, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked fifty-ninth in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather was Fengshao, his father was Can, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Lou. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Yunchun, courtesy name Maochu, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fourteenth in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xie, Left Vice Minister of War, posthumously granted the title Minister of War; his grandfather was Shixian, Registrar of the Court of State Ceremonial, granted the honorary title Compiler in the Hanlin Academy; his father was Dashun, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of this same examination cohort; and his mother was née Zhu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yunduan and Yunjia, and he married a woman née Wang. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Guo, courtesy name Weizhen, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Ruxian, his father Fu, and his mother née Wang; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Yi and Si, and his younger brothers Pang, Yuan, Chong, Pan, and Huai; he married a woman née Wang and placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chongshi, courtesy name Zhongxu, was registered in an official household of the Xingzhou Left Agricultural Garrison Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region; a Yutian County school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei, a Company Commander; his grandfather was Jing, his father Pinyang, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Chongwei, Chongmei, Chongyang, Chongrong, Chongzhou, and Chongda; he married a woman née Liu and placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Wenjia, courtesy name Shiwang, was registered in a military household in Jingling County, Mianyang Subprefecture, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang; an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiong, his grandfather Zhengchao, his father Jun, his mother née Ding, and his stepmother née Wang; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Wenhua, Wenshi, Wenren, Wenbing, and Wenwei; he married a woman née Cui and subsequently a woman née Li, and placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiang, courtesy name Daqing, was registered in a military household of Jining Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ning, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Xin; his father's former wife was née Li and his mother née Liu; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Han and Cang, and his younger brothers Jiang and Wei; he married a woman née Jiang and placed sixty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Shude, courtesy name Yucheng, was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was forty-four years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tingxun; his grandfather, Lan; and his father, Hu, who received the honorary title of Hanlin Academy Compiler. His mother, née Shen, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shufang and Shusheng, the latter serving as Left Admonisher in the Left Spring Office and concurrently as Hanlin Academy Reader-in-waiting. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Mo. He placed twenty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Xiru, courtesy name Chongbo, was registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Yao; his father, Tian; and his mother, née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuru, and his younger brother was Shiru. He married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Geng, courtesy name Caishu, was registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twelfth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shi, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his grandfather was Jian, an Usher; and his father was Jin, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of State Ceremonial. His mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Mingqian, courtesy name Deqing, was registered in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather, Wenguan; and his father, Zong. His mother was née Hu, and his stepmother was née Zhong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Laoqian, and his younger brothers were Huiqian and Yiqian. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Meng Xueyi, courtesy name Yushi, was from Lingtai County, Jingzhou, Pingliang Prefecture, Shaanxi, and belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Shaoxian, an annual tribute student; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xueshu, Xueshi, and Xueli. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Yuzhao, courtesy name Zongdu, was from Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Xi, held an honorary longevity title; and his father, Duo, was a Steward. His father's principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yulu, an Usher, and Yuchu; his younger brother was Yusong. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Zigui, courtesy name Gongpan, was from Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather, Di; and his father, Dashao. His father's principal wife was née Gao, and his birth mother was née Meng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ziying, a provincial sacrificial official (shengjiguan), and Zicai. He married a woman née Jia and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Mengchun, courtesy name Tiyuan, was from Gao'an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and belonged to a military household. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Chongsheng; his grandfather, Cheng, held an honorary longevity title; his father was Shun; and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. He married a woman née Liao. He placed eighty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.
