translation_en:
Hou Jukun 侯居坤, courtesy name Bosheng, was registered in Jie Department, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. An additional student of the departmental school specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fourth in family order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Jun was a county vice magistrate; his grandfather Xiang was a registrar; and his father Zhen was a departmental judge. His mother was née Yan and his stepmother née Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Jugen, a jinshi of the same examination year, and Juzhen, a tribute scholar; his younger brother was Jujing. His wife was née Sun. He placed forty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 345th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Jie 鄭傑, courtesy name Ruxing, was registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather Jing held the honorary designation “official for righteousness”; his grandfather Xian was a steward of provisions; and his father was Daji. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shen, Hui 儶 [?], and Guan. His wife was née Zhou. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yigui 賀一桂, courtesy name Qiufang, was registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in family order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Song; his grandfather Luan held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father Yi was a prefectural vice prefect. His mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yisong and Yiyang. His wife was née Xiao. He placed seventy-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kuang Duo 匡鐸, courtesy name Shujiao, was registered in an official household of the Jiaozhou Defense Battalion, Shandong, and was a native of Ganyu County, Hai Department, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Mao had been honorifically invested as Gentleman of the Cultivated Forest and Investigating Censor; his grandfather Yizhi was a provincial surveillance commissioner; and his father was Yunding. His mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Quan. His first wife was née Luan, and his subsequent wife née Zhai. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 331st in the Metropolitan Examination.

治易經字公昂行九年三十九十月二十六日生

===
胡溽
貫直隷常州府無錫縣軍籍　縣學附學生
曾祖樸　祖良珮　父觀　母闞氏
治書經字原荆行一年三十二十一月二十二日生

應天府鄉試第六十二名　會試第七十四名
李良臣
貫貴州普安衛軍籍應天府江寧縣人　普安州學生
曾祖豫　祖崇道　父時〔教諭〕　母金氏
治易經字直甫行二年三十十一月初二日生
永感下　兄純臣　弟明臣　娶戴氏
貴州鄉試第八名　會試第二百名
punctuated:
楊松〔貫河南河南衞軍籍，浙江杭州府海鹽縣人，洛陽縣學增廣生，治易經，字惟喬，行一，年三十七，三月二十八日生〕。曾祖萱〔散官〕，祖鴻，父珩，前母劉氏，母沈氏，繼母朱氏。具慶下，弟栟、楨，娶張氏。河南鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百七十四名。

陳錡〔貫河南河南衞官籍，直隸滁州來安縣人，洛陽縣學附學生，治易經，字公鼎，行九，年三十九，十月二十六日生〕。曾祖林，祖羔〔散官〕，父垠，母李氏，繼母張氏。慈侍下，兄泓〔指揮僉事〕、鑰、鎮，弟銓〔貢士〕、鑄、錫、鏘，娶李氏，繼娶虞氏。河南鄉試第二十四名，會試第三十五名。

胡孝〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字原荆，行一，年三十二，十二月二十二日生〕。曾祖樸，祖良珮，父觀，母闞氏。慈侍下，娶浦氏。應天府鄉試第六十二名，會試第七十四名。

李良臣〔貫貴州普安衞軍籍，應天府江寧縣人，普安州學生，治易經，字直甫，行二，年三十，十一月初二日生〕。曾祖豫，祖崇道，父時〔教諭〕，母金氏。永感下，兄純臣，弟明臣，娶戴氏。貴州鄉試第八名，會試第二百名。
translation_en:
Yang Song, courtesy name Weiqiao, was registered in a military household of Henan Guard in Henan and was originally from Haiyan County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was an additional student at the Luoyang County school, specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, holder of a prestige title; his grandfather was Hong, and his father was Heng; his father's former wife was née Liu, his mother née Shen, and his stepmother née Zhu; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Bing and Zhen; his wife was née Zhang; he placed thirty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qi, courtesy name Gongding, was registered in an official household of Henan Guard in Henan and was originally from Lai'an County, Chuzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an attached student at the Luoyang County school, specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked ninth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather was Gao, holder of a prestige title, and his father was Yin; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Zhang; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Hong, an Assistant Commander, Yue, and Zhen, and his younger brothers were Quan, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Zhu, Xi, and Qiang; his wife was née Li, and he subsequently married a woman née Yu; he placed twenty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xiao, courtesy name Yuanjing, was registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an attached student at the county school, specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather Liangpei, his father Guan, and his mother née Kan; his father was deceased and his mother living; his wife was née Pu; he placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Liangchen, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a military household of Pu'an Guard in Guizhou and was originally from Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture; he was a student at the Pu'an Subprefectural school, specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Chongdao, his father Shi, an Instructor, and his mother née Jin; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Chunchen and his younger brother Mingchen; his wife was née Dai; he placed eighth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

===
董三遷〔貫山東萊州府昌邑縣軍籍縣學生治詩經字汝孟行五年三十五十月初六日生〕
曾祖迪祖春〔壽官〕父瑂母李氏
慈侍下兄三策〔省祭官〕三槐三省三聘娶宋氏

===

貫山東萊州府昌邑縣軍籍　縣學生

曾祖迪　祖春壽官　父珵　母李氏

曾祖堯誼〔贈刑部主〕〔事〕　祖守誠〔布政司參議進〕〔階中憲大夫〕　父允恭　母周氏
嚴侍下　兄執器〔執藝　執禮〕〔執經　執御〕〔執玉　弟執〕〔執政〕　娶岑氏
浙江鄉試第四十名　會試第三十名
punctuated:
李日強〔貫山西平陽府曲沃縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字元莊，行四，年三十一，正月十二日生〕。曾祖錄，祖瓚，父廷舉，母衛氏，繼母王氏、龔氏。具慶下，兄日休、曰躋、日新，弟日明、日智、日章、日瞻、日中、日熙，娶鞏氏。山西鄉試第一名，會試第二百三十名。

王元賓〔貫山東兖州府滕縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字國賢，行二，年二十七，十月初八日生〕。曾祖峻，祖美，父天敘，母程氏。具慶下，兄嘉賓〔知縣〕，弟利賓，娶神氏。山東鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百二十一名。

董三遷〔貫山東萊州府昌邑縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字汝孟，行五，年三十五，十月初六日生〕。曾祖迪，祖春〔壽官〕，父瑂，母李氏。慈侍下，兄三策〔省祭官〕、三槐、三省、三聘，娶宋氏。山東鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百二十四名。

徐執策〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字以獻，行二十，年三十五，九月初五日生〕。曾祖克誼〔贈刑部主事〕，祖守誠〔布政司參議，進階中憲大夫〕，父允恭，母周氏。嚴侍下，兄執器、執藝、執禮、執經、執御、執玉，弟執政，娶岑氏。浙江鄉試第四十名，會試第三十名。
translation_en:
Li Riqiang, registered in a military household in Quwo County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was an added student of the county school who specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuanzhuang; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather Zan, and his father Tingju; his mother was née Wei, and his stepmothers were née Wang and née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rixiu, Yueji, and Rixin; his younger brothers were Riming, Rizhi, Rizhang, Rizhan, Rizhong, and Rixi. His wife was née Gong. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuanbin, registered in a military household in Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an added student of the county school who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guoxian; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Mei, and his father Tianxu; his mother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother Jiabin was a District Magistrate, and his younger brother was Libin. His wife was née Shen. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Sanqian, registered in a military household in Changyi County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the county school who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rumeng; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Chun held an honorary rank for longevity, and his father was Mei; his mother was née Li. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Sance, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan), Sanhuai, Sanxing, and Sanpin. His wife was née Song. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhice, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school who specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yixian; he ranked twentieth in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Keyi was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Shoucheng was an Assistant Administration Commissioner, advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Exemplary Service (Zhongxian dafu). His father was Yungong, and his mother was née Zhou. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhiqi, Zhiyi, Zhili, Zhijing, Zhiyu (執御), and Zhiyu (執玉); his younger brother was Zhizheng. His wife was née Cen. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

貫江西撫州府臨川縣民籍　縣學附學生

曹慎
貫直隸鎮江衛軍籍山西平陽府解州人　丹徒縣學生
治易經字思永行七年三十六六月二十五日生
曾祖榮　祖綬〔贈監察御史〕父倣〔南京太僕寺少卿〕嫡母余氏〔封孺人〕生母金氏
慈侍下　兄忠〔縣丞〕恕〔知州同知〕恒悅〔知縣〕忱〔知縣〕恬〔知縣〕懷　娶金氏
應天府鄉試第四十名　會試第九十四名
punctuated:
成憲〔貫直隸薊州衛官籍，國子生，治詩經，字君迪，行二，年二十七，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖鵬〔百戶，贈都督同知〕，祖用〔百戶，封都督同知〕，父勳〔鎮守總兵官、都督同知〕，嫡母黃氏〔封夫人〕，生母楊氏。慈侍下，兄恩，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百名，會試第一百十二名。

葉夢熊〔貫廣東惠州府歸善縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字男兆，行四，年三十五，正月二十七日生〕。曾祖巒，祖標，父春芳〔縣丞〕，前母嚴氏，母石氏。慈侍下，兄夢麟〔主簿〕、夢奎、夢陽，弟夢桂，娶廖氏。廣東鄉試第四名，會試第一百二十名。

徐儒〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字邦珍，行九，年三十二，九月初十日生〕。曾祖福，祖濬，父汝乾，母饒氏。具慶下，兄化〔貢士〕，弟伊、位，娶朱氏。江西鄉試第五十四名，會試第三百三十四名。

曹慎〔貫直隸鎮江衛軍籍，山西平陽府解州人，丹徒縣學生，治易經，字思永，行七，年三十六，六月二十五日生〕。曾祖榮，祖綬〔贈監察御史〕，父倣〔南京太僕寺少卿〕，嫡母余氏〔封孺人〕，生母金氏。慈侍下，兄忠〔縣丞〕、恕〔州同知〕、恒、恱〔知縣〕、忱、恬〔知縣〕、懷，娶金氏。應天府鄉試第四十名，會試第九十四名。
translation_en:
Cheng Xian, courtesy name Jundi, was registered in an official household of Jizhou Guard in Zhili. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked second in birth order, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Peng was a Company Commander posthumously granted the title of Vice Commissioner-in-chief; his grandfather Yong was a Company Commander granted the title of Vice Commissioner-in-chief; and his father Xun was a Regional Commander and Vice Commissioner-in-chief. His legal mother, née Huang, was granted the title of Lady; his birth mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was En, and his wife was née Li. He placed one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Mengxiong, courtesy name Nanzhao, was registered in a civilian household of Guishan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong. He was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, ranked fourth in birth order, and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Luan, his grandfather was Biao, and his father, Chunfang, was an Assistant Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Yan, and his mother was née Shi. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Menglin, a Registrar, Mengkui, and Mengyang; his younger brother was Menggui. His wife was née Liao. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ru, courtesy name Bangzhen, was registered in a civilian household of Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked ninth in birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather was Jun, his father was Ruqian, and his mother was née Rao. Both parents were living. His elder brother Hua was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Yi and Wei. His wife was née Zhu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Shen, courtesy name Siyong, was registered in a military household of Zhenjiang Guard in Zhili and was a native of Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a student of Dantu County School specializing in the Classic of Changes, ranked seventh in birth order, and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather Shou was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father Fang was Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing. His legal mother, née Yu, was granted the title of Ru ren (Lady); his birth mother was née Jin. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zhong, an Assistant Magistrate; Shu, a Department Vice Magistrate; Heng; Yue, a District Magistrate; Chen; Tian, a District Magistrate; and Huai. His wife was née Jin. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Defu, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked nineteenth among his male relatives of the same generation and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyou, his grandfather Xi, and his father Lie; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Dai. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Shufu and Ganfu, and his wife was née Shi. He placed forty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Ying, courtesy name Yuanfu, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his male relatives of the same generation and was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bing, his grandfather Hao, and his father Jin; his mother was née Tang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His wife was née Jiang. He placed thirteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Kejiu, courtesy name Deqing, was registered in a civilian household in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twenty-ninth among his male relatives of the same generation and was aged twenty, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunlu, his grandfather Zhaohe, and his father Ti; his mother was née Yang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Kele, and his younger brothers were Keda, Kezhan, Keyang, Keshi, Kefu, and Kexue. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née He. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan, courtesy name Maowen, was registered in a military artisan household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his male relatives of the same generation and was aged thirty, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan, his grandfather Qi, and his father Liangchen; his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wei, and his younger brothers were Can and Hui. He married a woman née Mu and subsequently women née Chen and née Qiao. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Keda, registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a salt-producing household, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dezhou, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong (an honorary official recognized for longevity), his grandfather was Tang (a sacrificial official, shengjiguan), his father was Jiayan, and his mother was née Zhao; both parents were living, his elder brother was Kejiu, his younger brothers were Keli, Kexing, Keshi, Keren, and Kechuan, his wife was née Zhou, and he placed sixty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Guihe, registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in an artisan household, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zizhong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-four years old, born on the eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ru, his grandfather was Yun, his father was Xun, his legal mother was née Gao, his stepmothers were née Fan and née Yang, and his birth mother was née Wang; his father was deceased and his mother living, his younger brothers were Guizhong and Guijing, his wife was née Wang, and he placed sixty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gui Youguang, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xifu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was forty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng (a County Magistrate), his grandfather was Shen, his father was Zheng, his mother was née Zhou, and his stepmother was née Xue; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brother was Youjia, his younger brothers were Youqing, Yougong, and Youdao, he married a woman née Wei and subsequently women née Wang and née Fei, and he placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Chong, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junxi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight years old, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daxing, his grandfather was Zhongguan, his father was Xianbang, his father's former wife was née Yin, and his mother was née Zhu; both parents were living, his elder brother was Zongshun, his younger brothers were Xuanbin and Yinxuan, his wife was née Hao, and he placed forty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Rong 楊鎔, registered in a civilian household in Rong County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Defu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guishan; his grandfather, Tao, was a subprefect; his father was Dizai, and his mother was née Cheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ding, Quan, and Yue, and his younger brother was also recorded as Yue [?]. He married a woman née Xu. He placed sixty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Mao 黃茂, registered in an officer household of Wuchang Guard, Huguang, and a native of Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shucai, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yu, was a commander; his grandfather, Fu, was a magistrate; his father, Zhou, was a vice magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Hua and Fang, and his younger brother was Zhi. He married a woman née Luo and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed fifty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ze 李澤, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenfu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maoguang, his grandfather was Qianliang, his father was Jingfu, and his mother was née Zeng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qing and Chun, and his younger brother was Ye. He married a woman née Wu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and three hundred sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yixiu 王以修, registered in a civilian household in Dazhou, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jingfu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Gengji, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his grandfather, Zongyi, was an assistant instructor; his father was Yanzhong, and his mother was née Tang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Yidi, and his younger brothers were Yifu, Yijing, Yiguang, Yining, Yixin, Yishang, and Yiwei. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Xiong. He placed twelfth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Xin, registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Kerong, he ranked ninth in his family, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhuo, his grandfather Zhen, his father Zuo, and his mother née Chen; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, Tian, Xun, and Ying, and his wife was née Peng. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Deyang, registered in a military household in Guangde Subprefecture in the Metropolitan Region, was an additional student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Boying, he ranked first in his family, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Zhao, a Subprefectural Assistant Judge, his father Chongqian, a District Magistrate, and his mother née Sun; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qingyang and Fengyang, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qi, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and originally from Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, was a student of the Shanghai county school specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Yuanhan, he ranked first in his family, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Huai, his father Yi, a Medical Instructor, and his mother née Ma; both parents were living. His elder brother was Chi, his younger brothers Bi and Zhong, and his wife was née Chen. He placed 112th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Jian, registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongzhen, he ranked seventh in his family, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, a Prefect, his grandfather Zhuo, his father Xian, and his mother née Sun; both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Jin and Hai, his younger brothers Zhi, Tong, Han, Qia, and Zhang, and his wife was née Huang. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

熊汝器〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字國用，行八，年三十二，八月十二日生〕。曾祖守信，祖津，父蓋，母秦氏。具慶下，兄汝弼，弟汝相、汝賓、汝嘉，娶胡氏。江西鄉試第九十四名，會試第三百六十九名。

楊守仁〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣，軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字嘉復，行一，年二十二，六月二十二日生〕。曾祖正章，祖廷選，父國岐，母黃氏。具慶下，弟守義、守備、偉、侃、守禮、儔、守智、僎、健、信、佐、傑，娶戴氏。福建鄉試第七十三名，會試第二百三十七名。

張學顏〔貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子的，行一，年四十一，五月十一日生〕。曾祖實，祖受，父儼，母林氏。慈侍下，弟學曾、學孔、學孟，娶周氏。廣東鄉試第二十六名，會試第八十二名。
translation_en:
Wei Li 魏澧 was registered in Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Ruheng and ranked second in family order. He was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Duan, an Honorary Official; his grandfather was Xiao, posthumously granted the title of Prefect; his father was Tingxuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Song, had received the additional title of Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Pan, a County Vice Magistrate, Guang, Ji, Zi, Hun, Jin, Zhi, and Ji; his younger brothers were Pu, Yan, and Yong. His wife was née Du. He placed fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Ruqi 熊汝器 was registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Guoyong and ranked eighth in family order. He was thirty-two years old, born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shouxin, his grandfather Jin, his father Gai, and his mother née Qin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rubi; his younger brothers were Ruxiang, Rubin, and Rujia. His wife was née Hu. He placed ninety-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 369th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shouren 楊守仁 was registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Jiafu and ranked first in family order. He was twenty-two years old, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhengzhang, his grandfather Tingxuan, his father Guoqi, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shouyi, Shoubei, Wei, Kan, Shouli, Chou, Shouzhi, Zhuan, Jian, Xin, Zuo, and Jie. His wife was née Dai. He placed seventy-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xueyan 張學顏 was registered in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zidi and ranked first in family order. He was forty-one years old, born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shi, his grandfather Shou, his father Yan, and his mother née Lin. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Xuezeng, Xuekong, and Xuemeng. His wife was née Zhou. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

蕭復陽〔貫福建泉州府同安縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字道長，行一，年三十五，十一月二十三日生〕。曾祖萬慶，祖廷舉，父國用，母張氏。慈侍下，弟復春，娶張氏。福建鄉試第十五名，會試第三百二十八名。
translation_en:
Feng Yixiang 酆一相, courtesy name Fuzhi, was registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household; he was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked tenth among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Yuanzan, his father Mingqi, and his mother née Xiong; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Yizhen, Yicheng, and Yicai, his younger brothers Yizheng and Yisong, and his wife née Xu; he placed forty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xueshi 李學詩, courtesy name Zixing, was registered in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household; he was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Xian, his father Tingchen, his father's former wife née Du, and his mother née Qiao; his father alone was living; his younger brothers were Xueli, Xueyi, Xueshu, and Xuekong, and his wife née Han; he placed sixty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yingdeng 張應登, courtesy name Zhongyong, was registered in Xianyang County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household; he was a student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Yue, his father Chongde, a prefectural vice prefect, and his mother née Shi; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Yingju, his younger brothers Yingzhao and Yingpin, and his wife née Zhao; he placed sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Fuyang 蕭復陽, courtesy name Daozhang, was registered in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household; he was a student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wanqing, his grandfather Tingju, his father Guoyong, and his mother née Zhang; his mother alone was living; his younger brother was Fuchun, and his wife née Zhang; he placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and three hundred twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Bosheng, courtesy name Yu’ai, was registered in a civilian household in Xiaogan County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang, and was originally from Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangyou. A student of the De’an prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benmin; his grandfather, Kuande; his father, Tingxiang; and his mother, née Fang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother Boxie was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gui Tianxiang, courtesy name Zixing, was registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An auxiliary student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked eighth in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengyu; his grandfather, Hong; his father, Lian; and his mother, née Luo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Tianxi, and his younger brothers were Tianqing, Tianmin, and Tianwen. He married a woman née Duan. He placed sixty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Tingshi, courtesy name Wenqing, was registered in a military household in Chenliu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Jin; and his father, Lu, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations. His father's principal wife was née Zhu, and his birth mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and three hundred seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zang Weiyi, courtesy name Shouzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An added-quota student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-four, born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, posthumously granted the title of Registrar; his grandfather, Fei, was a Department Vice Magistrate; and his father was Jie. His father's principal wife was née Meng, and his birth mother was née Jiao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Weijing, and his younger brothers were Weishi, Weiji, Weijing, Weixiao, and Weizhong. He married a woman née Chang. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Xueshi, courtesy name Shuyan, was registered in a civilian household in Dong'e County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather, Wan; and his father, Ying, held an honorary title for charitable service; his father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Wang, who alone of his parents was living; his elder brothers were Xuezhou and Xueyi, his younger brothers were Xuezhong and Xueshu, and his wife was née Zhang; he placed twenty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Bai, courtesy name Zixiu, was registered in a military household in Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and served as Instructor at the county school of Tangyi, Shandong, specializing in the Book of Documents; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-six, and was born on the twenty-first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Bi; his grandfather, Dawu; his father, Zhou, was a Steward of Provisions; and his mother, née Fan, alone of his parents was living; his younger brothers were Feng and Xing, he married a woman née Tao and subsequently a woman née Wu, and he placed fifty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Tingwu, courtesy name Zicai, was registered in a civilian household in Xinxiang County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, and was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Lan; his grandfather, Rujing, was a Professor; his father, Congke, was an Instructor; and his mother was née Zhao; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Tinggui and Tinghui, his wife was née Meng, and he placed seventy-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 346th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Xiang, courtesy name Yunli, was registered in a civilian household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a subprefectural-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Ming; and his father, He, held an honorary title for longevity; his father's former wife was née Gao, and his mother was née Xu, who alone of his parents was living; his elder brothers were Mei, a Steward of Provisions, and Guo, a Pacification Officer, his younger brothers were Zi and Ge, his wife was née Ren, and he placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 363rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Shao, courtesy name Wenxiao, was from Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and registered in a civilian household. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Biao, a Prefect; his grandfather was Ben; and his father was Xiao, a Registrar. His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wan, and his wife was née Huang. He placed eighty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenyu, courtesy name Tingji, was from Pinghe County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and registered in a military household. A student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Benzhang; his grandfather was Zongmian, an honorary official for longevity; and his father was Shihao, a Professor, honorifically invested as Archivist of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. His father’s former wife, née Lin, was posthumously granted the title Lady (Ruren); his mother, née Yan, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Wenshu, an Assistant Instructor; Wencha, a Prefectural Vice Prefect; and Wentian. His younger brother was Wenbing, and his wife was née Yan. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ju Shou, courtesy name Ziyue, was from Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a military household. A supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Zhang; his father was Xian; and his mother was née Zhu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Guan and Shi; his younger brother was Xian (憲). His wife was née Xu. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Sheng, courtesy name Xianqing, was registered in an officer household of the Xi’an Front Guard, Shaanxi. A student of the Xi’an prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a Regional Military Commissioner; his grandfather was Ming, a Brigade Commander; and his father was Hao, a Regional Military Commissioner. His father’s former wife was née Liang, and his mother was née Ji. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zhi, a Guard Commander, and his wife was née Jia. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊一魁〔貫山西平陽府安邑縣民籍，河東運司學生，治禮記，字子選，行四，年三十一，十二月三十日生〕。曾祖景山，祖昭，父琯〔知縣〕，母景氏。永感下，兄一源、一科、一才，弟一舉、一棟，娶張氏。山西鄉試第五十七名，會試第一百六十七名。
translation_en:
Gao Qiyu, registered in a civilian household in Tongliang County, Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Minfu; he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Zongxiang, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Mao, an Administration Vice Commissioner in the Provincial Administration Commission. His father's principal wife, née Wang, had been granted the title of Lady (Ruren); his birth mother was née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Qikui and Qihan, and his younger brothers Qixin and Qiren. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Mingzhang, registered in a civilian household in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yonghui; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ning, his grandfather Cen, his father Xiang, and his mother née Pan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Mingjiao. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Sikao, registered in a military household of Pu'an Guard, Guizhou, and originally from Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Tingbi, a College Supervisor in the Imperial University, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Zonglu, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate. His mother, née Pan, had been granted the title of Lady of Peace (Anren). His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Sizhong, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Siyuan. He married a woman née Jin. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 343rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yikui, registered in a civilian household in Anyi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the school of the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission, specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zixuan; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingshan, his grandfather Zhao, his father Guan, a County Magistrate, and his mother née Jing. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yiyuan, Yike, and Yicai, and his younger brothers Yiju and Yidong. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zha Duo, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in a civilian household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen; his grandfather, Shilun; and his father, Jingming. His mother was née Cui, and his stepmothers were née Zhang and née Su. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tianmin, a District Magistrate; his younger brothers were Kai, Zhen, Jin, Jian, Xian, Zhong, and Tang. His wife was née Xie. He placed forty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Qian, courtesy name Bozhen, was registered in an officer household of Henan Guard, Henan, and was a native of Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Tong and grandfather Luan were both Company Commanders. His father was Yao; his mother was née Chang, and his stepmother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kun, Shouhe (a Company Commander), Shouyi, Shouheng, and Shouxing. His wife was née Yan. He placed sixty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yuyan, courtesy name Zhifen, was registered in a civilian household in Dapu County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenming; his grandfather, Kongyuan; and his father, Dabin, a Prefectural School Professor. His mother was née Wu. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Yuhui and Yutai; his younger brothers were Yuwen, Yucheng, and Yuqi. His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fuduan, courtesy name Zixiang, was registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Quan had been granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather Qi was a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His father was Maochen, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fuxu; his younger brothers were Fuqing and Fuguan. His wife was née Cao. He placed ninety-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳三謨〔貫浙江杭州府仁和縣民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字汝明，行二，年二十七，十一月初四日生〕。曾祖琳，祖衡，父魯，前母葉氏、顧氏、童氏，母姚氏。具慶下，兄三策、天曆、堯曆，弟舜曆、三才，娶冷氏。浙江鄉試第六十六名，會試第三百十三名。

張克家〔貫直隸寧國府宣城縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字有光，行六，年二十九，八月十九日生〕。曾祖侗，祖柯，父烈，前母邵氏，母楊氏。具慶下，弟克愼、克效、克己、克勤、克敬、克寛、克復、克盛、克靜、克敏，娶戚氏，繼娶姜氏。應天府鄉試第七名，會試第一百三名。
translation_en:
Wang Yao, courtesy name Minhao, was registered in a civilian household in Shifang County, Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaorong; his grandfather, Xiang; and his father, Benjian, a Registrar. His father's principal wife was Lady Liu, and his birth mother was Lady Jie. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Yong, and his younger brothers were Cheng, Shi, Mou, Xu, and Xie. He married Lady Dai. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jianjia, courtesy name Boshou, was registered in a military household of Yingchuan Guard, Henan, and was a native of Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, an Honorary Official; his grandfather, Qi, an Assistant Magistrate; and his father, Jimei, a student of the Imperial University. His mother was Lady Wang. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Jianliang, Jiancheng, Jianbin, Jiangao, Jianshi, Jianyuan, and Jiankai. He married Lady Wang. He ranked sixty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 368th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Sanmo, courtesy name Ruming, was registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Heng; and his father, Lu. His father's former wives were Lady Ye, Lady Gu, and Lady Tong; his mother was Lady Yao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sance, Tianli, and Yaoli, and his younger brothers were Shunli and Sancai. He married Lady Leng. He ranked sixty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Kejia, courtesy name Youguang, was registered in a military household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Ke; and his father, Lie. His father's former wife was Lady Shao; his mother was Lady Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Keshen, Kexiao, Keji, Keqin, Kejing, Kekuan, Kefu, Kesheng, Kejing, and Kemin. He married Lady Qi and subsequently Lady Jiang. He ranked seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

朱光宇〔貫河南開封府祥符縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字德明，行二，年四十，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖璘，祖弘〔壽官〕，父鎰，前母高氏，母許氏。慈侍下。兄光先，弟光遠、光夏，娶王氏，繼娶楚氏。河南鄉試第十二名，會試第五十一名。

萬幾〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字汝思，行六，年二十七，閏十二月初十日生〕。曾祖欽時，祖明高〔壽官〕，父文化，母章氏。具慶下。兄恭〔兵部左侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史〕，弟思迪、思建，娶周氏。江西鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百四十六名。

錢楷〔貫山東東昌府冠縣，匠籍，府學生，治易經，字範之，行七，年三十，九月初二日生〕。曾祖臻，祖輅，父繼先，前母龐氏、劉氏，母張氏，繼母康氏。嚴侍下。兄朴、梧、松、棟，弟權、梯、梓，娶王氏。山東鄉試第二名，會試第一百九名。
translation_en:
Qiu Qiyun, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was an auxiliary student at the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ruqian; he ranked first in family order and was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Wanxiu, and his father Liang, a tribute student; his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qingyun, Langyun, Qingyun, and Canyun; his younger brother was Shengyun. His wife was née Wan. He placed twenty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Guangyu, registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Deming; he ranked second in family order and was forty years old, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Hong, who held an honorary official title for longevity, and his father Yi. His father's former wife was née Gao, and his mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Guangxian; his younger brothers were Guangyuan and Guangxia. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Chu. He placed twelfth in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Ji, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an auxiliary student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rusi; he ranked sixth in family order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qinshi, his grandfather Minggao, who held an honorary official title for longevity, and his father Wenhua; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Gong was Left Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His younger brothers were Sidi and Sijian. His wife was née Zhou. He placed forty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Kai, registered in Guan County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to an artisan household and was a student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Fanzhi; he ranked seventh in family order and was thirty years old, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Lu, and his father Jixian. His father's former wives were née Pang and née Liu; his mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother née Kang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Pu, Wu, Song, and Dong; his younger brothers were Quan, Ti, and Zi. His wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Shouyu, registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shengchi, he ranked seventy-sixth in his family, and he was twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War; his grandfather was Xu, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his father was Hongde, and his mother was née Cheng. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Shouyue, Shoujing, and Shouren, and his wife was née Yu. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ximeng, registered in a civilian household in Gushi County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was an supplementary student of the county school who specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shikong, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ze, his grandfather Guang, his father Chu, and his mother née Qi. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Xizhou; he married a woman née Zhao and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventy-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yigui, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a supplementary student of the prefectural school who specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenfang, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weiduan, posthumously appointed Assistant Magistrate of a subprefecture; his grandfather was Yongkuan; his father was Li, a County Vice Magistrate; his mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother née Luo. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Yilin, Yikui, Yiwenming, Yi'e, Yibao, and Yi'ao, an Usher; his younger brothers were Yiqi, Yiluan, Yiwenmei, Y /iw en xiu [?], Yiwenwei, Yiwensheng, Yiwu, and Yiyingnan. His wife was née Yu. He placed seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Liangjian, registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yixin, he ranked seventh in his family, and he was thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangyu, his grandfather Ke, his father 𤇍 [reading uncertain], and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Liangyan, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his wife was née Rao. He placed seventy-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
李謨〔貫直隸廣德州民籍，國子生，治易經，字顯卿，行九，年二十九，正月二十八日生〕。曾祖洪〔縣丞〕，祖康，父淳，母葛氏。具慶下，兄棟、栱，弟梧，娶楊氏，繼娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第八十二名，會試第三百三十七名。

陳惟直〔貫四川嘉定州洪雅縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字伯生，行二，年二十六，十月二十日生〕。曾祖永道，祖孟舉〔壽官〕，父誥〔學正〕，嫡母譚氏，繼母楊氏，生母周氏。慈侍下，兄惟重、惟勤，娶張氏。四川鄉試第一名，會試第一百二十九名。

朱學顏〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣竈籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字子愚，行一，年二十八，八月十五日生〕。曾祖桂〔壽官〕，祖玭〔監生〕，父陳範，母密氏。重慶下，弟學儒、學臯、學忠、學斌、學聖、學純、學藎，娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第三十二名，會試第三百七十一名。

鄭繼之〔貫湖廣襄陽儀衛司旗籍，襄陽府學生，治詩經，字伯孝，行一，年三十一，十二月初四日生〕。曾祖鏞，祖璽，父時中〔歲貢生〕，母陳氏。具慶下，弟緝之、綸之，娶胡氏，繼娶李氏。湖廣鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百五十二名。
translation_en:
Li Mo, courtesy name Xianqing, was registered in a civilian household in Guangde Subprefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked ninth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Kang; his father was Chun; and his mother was née Ge. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dong and Gong, and his younger brother was Wu. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 337th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Weizhi, courtesy name Bosheng, was registered in a civilian household in Hongya County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongdao; his grandfather was Mengju, who held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father was Gao, a School Instructor. His father's principal wife was née Tan, his stepmother was née Yang, and his birth mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Weizhong and Weiqin. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xueyan, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a salt-producing household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Pin, a student of the Directorate of Education; his father was Chenfan; and his mother was née Mi. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xueru, Xuegao, Xuezhong, Xuebin, Xuesheng, Xuechun, and Xuejin. He married a woman née Huang. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 371st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Jizhi, courtesy name Boxiao, was registered in a banner household of the Xiangyang Ceremonial Guard Office in Huguang. A student of the Xiangyang prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather was Xi; his father was Shizhong, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jizhi (緝之) and Lunzhi. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed fifty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

羅惟垣〔貫四川嘉定州竈籍，州學生，治易經，字少辰，行三，年三十一，七月二十四日生〕。曾祖厚〔封經歷〕，祖仕用，父綬〔典史〕，母劉氏，繼母葛氏、陳氏。嚴侍下，兄惟和、惟順，弟惟翰，娶任氏，繼娶陳氏。四川鄉試第三十二名，會試第二百三十一名。
translation_en:
Zhao Kehuai, courtesy name Dezhong, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Yang, his father Zhibi, and his mother née Li; his grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Kezong, and his younger brothers were Kejin, Keshi, Kebin, Kexue, Kexuan, and Kecheng. He married a woman née Zou. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Sanle, courtesy name Kexing, was registered in a civilian household in Yangxin County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Zhang, his father Bian, and his mother née Zhu; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sanyi, Sanjian, and Sangang. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yinglan, courtesy name Fangqing, was registered in a civilian household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Guanbao, his grandfather Shichang, his father Chuan, his mother née Xie, and his stepmother née Liu; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingzhao, Yinghuan, Yingzhen, and Yingying. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li (黎). He placed thirty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Weiyuan, courtesy name Shaochen, was registered in a salt-producing household in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hou, granted the title of Registrar; his grandfather was Shiyong; his father was Shou, a Clerk; his mother was née Liu, and his successive stepmothers were née Ge and née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Weihe and Weishun, and his younger brother was Weihan. He married a woman née Ren and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

李巳〔貫河南彰德府磁州民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子復，行二，年三十，正月十八日生〕。曾祖雄，祖聰〔教諭〕，父百之〔歲貢生〕，前母武氏，母楊氏。具慶下，兄乙，弟庚、辛、壬，娶任氏。河南鄉試第八名，會試第一百三十名。

李采菲〔貫直隸瀋陽中屯衛軍籍，江西臨江府新喻縣人，國子生，治易經，字君采，行一，年二十九，三月二十八日生〕。曾祖瓊〔贈昭勇將軍都指揮僉事〕，祖銳〔知州，贈昭勇將軍都指揮僉事〕，父涵〔義官〕，母樊氏。具慶下，弟采蘋、采蘩，娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第八名，會試第二百二十五名。

笪東光〔貫江西饒州府德興縣民籍，縣學附學生，治禮記，字景陽，行七十三，年三十五，十一月二十一日生〕。曾祖元吉，祖棠，父𨊬，母汪氏。永感下，兄東芬、東杲，娶祝氏。江西鄉試第五名，會試第二百六十四名。
translation_en:
Gu Zhixian 古之賢, courtesy name Shixi, was registered in a civilian household in Liangshan County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third in family birth order and was twenty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xiao; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Shu. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Tu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhiyu and Zhizhong; his younger brothers were Zhiru, Zhizhen, Zhidao, Zhiwen, Zhixue, Zhicai, and Zhizhi. His wife was née Gao. He placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Si 李巳, courtesy name Zifu, was registered in a civilian household in Cizhou, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family birth order and was thirty, born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xiong; his grandfather, Cong, was a School Instructor; and his father, Baizhi, was an annual tribute student. His father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yi; his younger brothers were Geng, Xin, and Ren. His wife was née Ren. He placed eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Caifei 李采菲, courtesy name Juncai, was registered in a military household of the Shenyang Central Garrison Guard in Zhili and was a native of Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family birth order and was twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Qiong, was posthumously granted the titles General of Illustrious Courage and Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His grandfather, Rui, was a Department Magistrate and was posthumously granted the same two titles. His father, Han, was an honorary official; his mother was née Fan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Caipin and Caifan. His wife was née Zhao. He placed eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Da Dongguang 笪東光, courtesy name Jingyang, was registered in a civilian household in Dexing County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked seventy-third in family birth order and was thirty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuanji; his grandfather, Tang; and his father, 𨊬 [name reading uncertain]. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dongfen and Donggao. His wife was née Zhu. He placed fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

朱一松〔貫直隸寧國府寧國縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字應秀，行二，年三十二，八月初九日生〕。曾祖文榮，祖鳳〔縣丞〕，父大有〔貢士〕，母段氏。慈侍下，兄一桂，弟一柏〔貢士〕、一梧。娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第一百九名，會試第五十名。

translation_en:
Bao Qian, courtesy name Yuanfu, was registered in a military household of Mianyang Guard, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Mianyang Subprefecture. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxian; his grandfather, Tong; his father, Derong; and his mother, née Yan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Meng, Shun, Kun, Sheng, Guan, Jie, and Cui. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Tong. He placed seventy-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 332nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Qianheng, courtesy name Guangfu, was registered in a civilian household of Maping County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi. A student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zi; his grandfather, Zongwen; his father, Jiabang, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother, née Fang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Kunheng, an Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and Lüheng; his younger brothers were Zhenheng, Yuheng, Jiheng, Taiheng, Jinheng, and Zhenheng. He married a woman née Ge. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 341st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Yisong, courtesy name Yingxiu, was registered in a civilian household of Ningguo County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenrong; his grandfather, Feng, an Assistant Magistrate; his father, Dayou, a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother, née Duan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yigui; his younger brothers were Yibai, a tribute student (gongshi), and Yiwu. He married a woman née Wu. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Hao, courtesy name Zuqin, was registered in a civilian household of Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather, Zhenqi; his father, Hankui; and his mother, née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Gao and Jing. He married a woman née Luo. He placed thirty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

鄭金〔貫直隸河間府滄州南皮縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字伯純，行一，年三十九，四月初八日生〕。曾祖喜，祖富，父宗學，母李氏，繼母孫氏。慈侍下，弟鍾、銘、錡、釴、錢，娶崔氏，繼娶徐氏。順天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第一百九十一名。

translation_en:
Yan Zhang, registered in a civilian household in Penglai County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruqing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Cong, a prefect; his grandfather was Ao; his father was Fengchong, a prefectural school instructor; and his mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Du and Zhuo, and his wife was née Liang. He placed forty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 366th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Shou, registered in a civilian household in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyin, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Mengyong, his grandfather was Sheng, and his father was Jingming; his father's principal wife was née Shen, and his birth mother was née Zeng. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jin, Si, and Fu. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently women née Wang and Zheng. He placed forty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 311th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Jin, registered in a civilian household in Nanpi County, Cangzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bochun, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xi, his grandfather was Fu, his father was Zongxue, his mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Zhong, Ming, Qi, Yi, and Qian. He married a woman née Cui and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Youlan, registered in a civilian household in Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Huaqing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jingzong, his grandfather was Mao, his father was Lingshu, his mother was née Song, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Youke, his younger brother was Yougui, and his wife was née Yang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Yilong, courtesy name Ruhua, was registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenke; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Shiying; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yide, Yiyuan, and Yiru; his younger brothers were Yigui, Yipeng, Yikui, Yihe, Yikun, and Yihong. His wife was née Dai. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Weidai, courtesy name Guozhen, was registered with the Zunhua Guard in Zhili, in an official household. A student of the Zunhua County school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xuan, was an Assistant Commander and was posthumously granted the title General of Manifest Might; his grandfather, Dajie, was an Assistant Regional Commander and was posthumously granted the title General Who Guards the State; his father, Yuanxun, was a Supreme Commander and was posthumously granted the title General of Manifest Courage. His mother, née Liu, was granted the title Respectful Lady. His mother alone was living. His elder brother, Weiyue, was an Assistant Regional Commander. He married a woman née Gan and subsequently women née Zhang and née Zhu. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 395th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Yingzheng, courtesy name Maode, was registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a military household. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Wei; his father, Yue; his mother, née Gao; and his stepmother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shanzheng, and his younger brother was Hezheng. His wife was née Gu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 354th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yinglong, courtesy name Shihua, was registered in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Che; his grandfather, Yong, was a Commissioner; his father, Wenxi, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yingfeng. His wife was née Guo. He placed thirtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.
