蕭敏道〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字曰遜，行五，年三十六，十月二十六日生〕。曾祖盛安，祖元紹，父時信，母古氏。具慶下，兄琛、濟道，弟言道、教道、淑道、鍊道、鑑道、敦道、膠道、脈道，娶郭氏。江西鄉試第八十一名，會試第三百九名。

殷渠〔貫直隸大名府開州長垣縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字伯清，行四，年三十九，二月初一日生〕。曾祖蓊，祖富〔七品散官〕，父軾〔巡檢〕，母楊氏。永感下，兄桓〔省祭官〕、楹、采〔訓導〕，弟格〔監生〕、鶴齡，娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第九十九名，會試第八十一名。

左熈〔貫陝西西安府耀州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字夏伯，行一，年四十七，九月初三日生〕。曾祖進〔封大理寺右寺副〕，祖經〔按察司僉事〕，父思忠〔吏部員外郎〕，前母王氏〔贈安人〕，母忽氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，弟煦、原、黙、黌，娶李氏。陝西鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百四十九名。
translation_en:
Yu Yiguan, courtesy name Yuandao, was registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Shi; and his father was Lianggui. His father's principal wife was née Wang 汪, and his birth mother was née Wang 王. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Yijian, and his wife was née Wang 汪. He placed forty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Mindao, courtesy name Yuexun, was registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng'an; his grandfather was Yuanshao; his father was Shixin; and his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chen and Jidao, and his younger brothers were Yandao, Jiaodao, Shudao, Liandao, Jiandao, Dundao, Jiaodao 膠道, and Maidao. His wife was née Guo. He placed eighty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Qu, courtesy name Boqing, was registered in Changyuan County, Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weng; his grandfather was Fu, who held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Shi, a Police Chief; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Huan, a ceremonial official (shengjiguan), Ying, and Cai, an Assistant Instructor. His younger brothers were Ge, an Imperial University student, and Heling. His wife was née Zhao. He placed ninety-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Xi, courtesy name Xiabo, was registered in Yao Subprefecture, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, honorifically appointed Right Assistant Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather was Jing, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his father was Sizhong, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel. His father's former wife, née Wang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother, née Hu, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Xu, Yuan, Mo, and Hong, and his wife was née Li. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gong Tingbi, registered in a civilian household in Jianshui Subprefecture, Lin’an Prefecture, Yunnan, was a native of Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruochun, and he ranked second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yongzeng, his grandfather Jie, his father Yanwen, and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Tingxun, and he married a woman née Hu. He placed ninth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wude, registered in a civilian household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Maoxiu, and he ranked first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Lie, his grandfather Mengxun, his father Wenfeng, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yide, and his younger brothers were Xiande, Jingde, and Chengde. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Wenyao, registered in a military household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county government school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Qiwei, and he ranked first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zunxian, his grandfather Zirui (holder of an honorary official title awarded for longevity), his father Miyu, his mother née Huang, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wenyuan (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Wenqiao, Wenjia, Wenlong, Wenzi, Wenbao, and Wenshi; he married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pu Ningzhong, registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was Instructor at the county government school of Shimen, Huguang. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhenzhi, and he ranked second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Chang (holder of an honorary official title awarded for longevity), his grandfather Sui, his father Weizhan, his father’s former wife née Li, and his mother née Huang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Ningfang, his younger brother Ningbi, and he married a woman née Lin. He placed eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Zhi, registered in a civilian household in Rongcheng County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Sizhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Shi’ang; his father, Wende, a student of the Imperial University; and his mother, née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Qi, was also a student of the Imperial University, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yilong, registered in a civilian household in Gaoyao County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jianfu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, a Sacrificial Attendant; his grandfather, Peng; his father, Shangyin, a Police Chief; and his mother, née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Dide, Yijing, Yikui, and Yijiao, and his wife was née Su. He placed twenty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xuanhua, registered in an officer household of the Longjiang Left Guard in Nanjing and a native of Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xingyi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi, a Company Commander; his grandfather, Deng; his father, Wen; and his mother, née Qiao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hong, his younger brothers were Yi, Wan, and Zunhua, and his wife was née Ma. He placed sixty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Yingmeng, registered in a military household in Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shizheng, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Ao; his father, Wenju; and his mother, née Fan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yingyang and Yingxian, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Shouyue, registered in Yongfu County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, in a civilian household, was Instructor in the county school of Xindu, Sichuan. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Xizeng. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and born on the tenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qiong, his grandfather Jizong, and his father Bai; his mother was née Zeng. His mother was living, and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Su, a Clerk, and Xuan, an annual tribute student; his younger brothers were Shoujing and Shougang. His wife was née Liang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Cunren, registered in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, in a civilian household, was an additional student in the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingfu. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Chi, and his father Mao; his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His wife was née Guo; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed fortieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Shi'ao, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household, was a native of Changzhou County and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Juqing. First in birth order, he was aged forty and born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Mei, and his father Shaozong; his mother was née Wu, and his stepmother née An. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shijing, Shili, and Shizun. His wife was née Xu. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Shi, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household, was an additional student in the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shuzhi. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and born on the eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Shiyi and grandfather Xing both served as Department Magistrates. His father was Zizhu, and his mother was née Xiong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bi and Yan. His wife was née Cai. He placed ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Siyu was registered in a civilian household in Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, and served as Instructor at the county school of Pujiang, Zhejiang. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zixi. He ranked second in birth order, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, Liang, was a Professor, posthumously granted successive honors culminating in Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of War; his grandfather, Hongmo, was Left Vice Minister of War. His father was Yiben, and his mother was née Yuan. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Silu and Sixun, and his younger brothers were Sizhong, Sile, Yi, Ying, Qi, Xiu, and Xun. His wife was née Pan. He placed fiftieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yingji was registered in a civilian household in Xiangling County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Boxiu. He ranked first in birth order, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Huan, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Tianxiang; and his father, Yongzhong, was an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Liang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Lu. He placed nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tiqian was registered as a bannerman in the Right Battalion of Zhending Guard, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Fenzhou, Shanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weijian. He ranked first in birth order, was thirty-nine years old, and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Long, his grandfather was Zan, and his father was Zhichun. His father's former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Tizhen, Tizhuang, Tiguan, and Tijie. His wife was née Lü. He placed sixty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 352nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Liangbi was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Laiqing. He ranked second in birth order, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengchun, his grandfather was Dan, and his father was Lin. His mother was née Xiong. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Lianghan, Liangwang, Liangzuo, Liangjian, Liangrui, and Liangyan. His wife was née Yu. He placed fifteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yuanli, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongjie; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-four sui, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kegang; his grandfather was Yunda, a tribute scholar; his father was Tingxian; and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanhao, Yinglei (a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice), and Yuangao; his younger brothers were Yuanheng, Yuanliang, Yuanchong, and Yuangun. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 387th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yicong, registered in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jianzhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-one sui, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Zhongde; and his mother was née Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yizhi, and his wife was née Pan. He placed forty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Kongxiu, registered in Daming County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yunzhi; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-five sui, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, a Prefect; his grandfather was Ke, a Proofreader; his father was Xixian; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Konghui, Kongshi (an Assistant Instructor), and Kongshuo; his younger brother was Kongming. His wife was née Wang. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xuan, registered in Taiping County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruhua; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-six sui, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang; his grandfather was Lu; his father was Jing; and his mother was née Jiao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jian; his younger brothers were Yong, Mo, and Xiang. His wife was née Cheng. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Ruhui; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Shao; and his father was Shi. His father's principal wife was née Su, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Ziqin, Zixian, and Chengmao; his younger brothers were Zigong, Zijing, and Ziyi. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Lin, registered in a civilian household in Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kefa; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Qianyuan, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his father was Yang, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Peng, and his stepmother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother was Bao, an Imperial University student, and his younger brother was Ji. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née Ouyang. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Dagang, registered in a civilian household in Wen'an County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunli; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, a Right Administrator promoted to rank 4a; his grandfather was Chang, a Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his father was Jie, Chief Messenger in the Office of Transmission. His mother was née Li. Both his parents were living. His elder brother was Datong, an Office Assistant in the Court of State Ceremonial; his younger brothers were Dajing, Dalun, Daji, Dawei, and Dayun. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Yue, registered in a civilian household in Daizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xizhun; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, a District Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Duan, an honorary official by virtue of longevity; and his father was Ruyu. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brother was Jian, and his wife was née Liu. He placed twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Teng, his grandfather Zhigao, and his father Xue; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Tian. He had living grandparents and parents. His younger brother was Dahua, and his wife was née Sun. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 390th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xiaocai, courtesy name Yongfu, was registered in an artisan household in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-seven years old, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonghe, his grandfather Bang (an honorary official recognized for longevity), and his father Qicong; his mother was née Huang and his stepmother née Wu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Xiaoliang and Xiaoxian; he married a woman née Peng and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Run, courtesy name Tianze, was registered in a military household of the Nanyang Central Princely Guard, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng, his grandfather Lun, and his father Chen; his mother was née Sun and his stepmother née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Yingyuan and Yingheng, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Huncheng, courtesy name Lianqing, was registered in a civilian household in Queshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather Fu was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel; his father Dashi was formerly Left Vice Minister of Revenue; and his mother, née Chen, held the title Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sucheng and Youcheng, his younger brothers Mocheng, Yuncheng, and Lincheng, and his wife was née Lin. He placed twenty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 376th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Ti 許倜, courtesy name Wenfu, was registered in a civilian household in Lingbao County, Shanzhou, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the thirtieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ju was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Library. His grandfather Jin was Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel, and was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Library, with the posthumous name Xiangyi. His father Zan was Junior Mentor concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. His mother was née Li and his stepmother née Wang; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Kang and his younger brother Dai. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed forty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Zun 雒遵, courtesy name Daoxing, was registered in a military household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Shou held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Wei and his father Ang. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmothers were née Huang and née Sun; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yuan and Xia. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chongkui 李冲奎, courtesy name Gongbei, was registered in a civilian household in Luancheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather Chun, and his father Mei; his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chongxiao and Chonghan, a District Magistrate; his younger brother Chongdou was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently a woman née Guo. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chonggong 張崇功, courtesy name Weizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Daming County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Guan was a School Instructor, and his father was Zidong; his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chongxian, Chongsu, Chongjian, and Chongqing; his younger brothers were Chongzhi and Chongya. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Qian. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qi Jie 戚杰 was registered in Sizhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shixiu; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was You; his grandfather, Jing, received the honorary title of Registrar; and his father, Ang, was a Registrar. His father's principal wife, née Li, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his stepmother, née Zhang, was granted the same title; and his birth mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun, Xu, Zhao, and Xi, and his younger brothers were Lie and Mo. He was betrothed to a woman née Hua. He placed ninety-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Maoru 丁懋儒 was registered in Liaocheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Pinqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Lian, was a County Magistrate; his grandfather, Kongzhang, was a Prefect; and his father, Yaozuo, was a Subprefectural Clerk. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Deng. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Maoguan, Maoshang, and Maoqing. He married a woman née Geng. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 378th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Pan 張磐 was registered in a military household of the Daning Front Guard and was a native of Pinggu County, Shuntian Prefecture. An added-quota student of the Shuntian prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Hongjian; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather was Yong, and his father was Ju. His father's former wife was née Feng, and his mother was née Xing. His mother alone was living. His younger brother, Yan, was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Zhou. He placed 105th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chu Fu 褚鈇 was registered in Yuci County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Minwei; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fuyuan, his grandfather was Kuang, and his father was Daquan. His father's former wife was née Li, his mother was née Qin, and his stepmother was née Jia. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Cheng and Ding, and his younger brothers were Yue and Tang. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

杜其萌〔貫山東濟南府濱州民籍，國子生，治書經，字子先，行一，年三十九，四月十二日生。〕曾祖鏞，祖景和〔壽官〕，父勑，母侯氏。永感下，娶袁氏。山東鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百十四名。

王家卿〔貫河南南陽衛官籍，國子生，治春秋，字應忠，行一，年四十四，八月初七日生。〕曾祖銳，祖繡，父稷，母杜氏，繼母汪氏。具慶下，弟家民、家仁、家慶、家胤，娶李氏，繼娶陳氏。河南鄉試第四名，會試第三百七十二名。
translation_en:
Dai Yanrong, registered in a military household of the Defense Battalion of Weihui Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zihan; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Gui, was posthumously appointed Magistrate; and his father, Ying, was Associate Commissioner of the Salt Distribution Commission. His father's former wife, Lady You, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Courtesy; his mother was Lady Cao, and his stepmothers were Lady Zhang and Lady Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yanshao and Yanshou. He married Lady Chen and subsequently Lady Xu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 384th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Ruchun, registered in a civilian household of Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Renxiang; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shiliang; his grandfather, Ang, was Assistant Magistrate and was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father, Shi, was a National University student; and his mother was Lady Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rujing, a National University student, and Ruqu, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Ru[?] (如𫨺), Rufu, Ruwei (如衛), Rutai, Ruwei (如闈), and Ruhai. He married Lady Xu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Qimeng, registered in a civilian household of Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixian; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Jinghe, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his father was Chi; and his mother was Lady Hou. Both parents were deceased. He married Lady Yuan. He placed fifty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiaqing, registered in an officer household of the Nanyang Guard, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yingzhong; he ranked first in his family and was forty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather was Xiu; his father was Ji; his mother was Lady Du; and his stepmother was Lady Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiamin, Jiaren, Jiaqing (家慶), and Jiayin. He married Lady Li and subsequently Lady Chen. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 372nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
程文〔貫江西撫州府東鄉縣軍籍，安仁縣人，東鄉縣學增廣生，治春秋，字載道，行十五，年三十六，七月二十一日生〕。曾祖瑩，祖瓊，父九萬〔壽官〕，母何氏。具慶下，兄度，弟京，娶王氏。江西鄉試第十九名，會試第一百八十七名。

劉世亨〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字以進，行八，年三十四，六月二十四日生〕。曾祖繼宏〔贈知州〕，祖瓛，父貢，母李氏。具慶下，娶羅氏。江西鄉試第八十三名，會試第一百四十九名。

薛志義〔貫山東濟南府濱州軍籍，州學增廣生，治書經，字民服，行五，年三十五，十二月初十日生〕。曾祖能，祖啓，父梅，母郭氏，繼母田氏。永感下，兄志道〔省祭官〕、志德、志學、志忠，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第二十名，會試第三百十八名。

王三錫〔貫四川成都府內江縣軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字用懷，行一，年二十四，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖加茂，祖登雲，父一陽，母趙氏。重慶下，弟廷錫、永錫、申錫，娶胡氏。四川鄉試第十九名，會試第三百二十九名。
translation_en:
Cheng Wen 程文, courtesy name Zaidao, was registered in a military household in Dongxiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a native of Anren County. An additional student at the Dongxiang County Confucian school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked fifteenth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Qiong; his father, Jiuwan, held the honorary title of Longevity Official; and his mother was née He. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Du, and his younger brother was Jing. His wife was née Wang. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shiheng 劉世亨, courtesy name Yijin, was registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student at the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked eighth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jihong, posthumously granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather, Huan; his father, Gong; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His wife was née Luo. He placed eighty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Zhiyi 薛志義, courtesy name Minfu, was registered in a military household in Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An additional student at the subprefectural Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather, Qi; his father, Mei; his mother, née Guo; and his stepmother, née Tian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhidao, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan), Zhide, Zhixue, and Zhizhong. His wife was née Liu. He placed twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanxi 王三錫, courtesy name Yonghuai, was registered in a military household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student at the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-four, and was born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiamao; his grandfather, Dengyun; his father, Yiyang; and his mother, née Zhao. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Tingxi, Yongxi, and Shenxi. His wife was née Hu. He placed nineteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 329th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王用章〔貫河南開封府祥符縣民籍，浙江衢州府龍游縣人，開封府學生，治易經，字汝平，行二，年三十四，七月十五日生〕。曾祖善忠，祖俊，父綱，前母徐氏，母張氏。永感下，兄用化〔儀賓〕，娶于氏。河南鄉試第三十七名，會試第二百六十七名。

translation_en:
Li Siyin, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An additional student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked second in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dashou, granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Chunfan, a Steward; and his father was Yizhuang, an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Chi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sizhong; his younger brothers were Sizhe, Siyue (a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue), Sidun, Sicheng, Sizhen, and Siyong. His wife was née Chen. He placed fiftieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 350th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Linqiao, courtesy name Zizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, a Steward; his grandfather was Jiurong, a District Magistrate; and his father was Hui. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhong (a county-school Instructor); his younger brothers were Lincai (a Prefectural Judge), Linsong, Lindong, Lin[?] (林𬃷, a metropolitan graduate), Linshu, Linyuan, Linlong, Linbiao, Linchong, Lingui, Linchun, and Linzhang. His wife was née Yu. He placed thirtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yongzhang, courtesy name Ruping, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and was originally from Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Kaifeng prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shanzhong, his grandfather was Jun, and his father was Gang. His father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yonghua, a Ceremonial Son-in-law. His wife was née Yu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shizhang, courtesy name Shang'an, was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked tenth in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyou, his grandfather was Hong, and his father was Zhongfu. His father's former wives were both née Zheng, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shihe, Shizhe, and Shizhao. His wife was née Huang. He placed eighty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qin Jishi, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in a civilian household in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in family order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, a County Office Manager; his grandfather was Lin; and his father was Ying, an honorary official awarded the title for public benefactions. His mother was née Zhou. His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Bangyan, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Shanshi; his younger brother was Guoshi. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Ziqi, courtesy name Ruzhen, was registered in a civilian household in Shouzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A department government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in family order and was aged thirty-nine, born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Kai; and his father was Huan, a Registrar. His father's former wife was née Pan, and his mother was née Yang. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Zijin, Zibi, Zizhuo, Ziqiong, and Zizhang; his younger brothers were Ziyu, Zifan, Zixuan, Zigui, and Ziying. His wife was née Yao. He placed ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 338th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Guangda, courtesy name Ziqian, was registered in a civilian household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. An added-quota student at the prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Huai, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of War; and his father was Fuli, Secretary in the Ministry of War. His mother, née Zhao, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren); his stepmother, née Jiao, was granted the same title. His mother alone survived. His younger brothers were Guangzu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Guangyu. His wife was née Li. He placed sixty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Yonghe, courtesy name Liheng, was registered in a military household of the Hangzhou Front Guard in Zhejiang and was a native of Huai'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Zongsheng; and his father was Bao. His father's former wife was née Ding, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents survived. His elder brother was Yongxiang, and his younger brother was Yongnan. His wife was née Li. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Mingshi, registered in an artisan household in Guang Prefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yiqi; he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Xiu, and his father Xin; his father's former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mingru and his younger brother Mingyan. His wife was née Xie. He placed eleventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Guan, registered in a military household in Shan County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziye; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Xi, his father Tianjue, and his mother née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Shu and Zhu. His wife was née Li. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bangzuo, registered in a military household in Chenliu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhiqing; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Nai, his grandfather Dao, his father Ju, and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Bangda and Bangwei, the latter holding a seventh-rank prestige title. His wife was née Chang; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lan, registered in a military household in Guan County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingzhong; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather Zhou was posthumously awarded the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites. His father was Rui and his mother née Feng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother Dong was a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Fa and Wo. His wife was née Xu. He placed thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ou Xiji, registered in a military household in Hengyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziwen; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhicong, his grandfather Junyi, his father Shixiang, and his mother Lady Huang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Xiyan, and his younger brothers were Xikui, Xifan, Xiqi, Xiding, Xiyin, and Xihan. He married Lady Xiao. He placed eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chaoyang, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yangming; he ranked fourth in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Shi, his father Kai, and his mother Lady Gui. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Chaochen and Chaoyue. He married Lady Shen. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yuchun, registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zifu; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hu, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Xian, a student of the Directorate of Education; his father was Gu, a Director of a county school; and his mother was Lady Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuqi and Yushi, and his younger brothers were Yuju, Yuzhu, Yuke, Yushun, Yujun, Yulin, and Yugeng. He married Lady Chen. He placed sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Daoming, registered in a civilian household in Yuancheng County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xingfu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Yue, his father Min, an annual tribute student, and his mother Lady Cheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Daoheng, a student of the Directorate of Education, and his younger brothers were Daogong, Daotong, Daodong, Daoli, Daozhi, Han [?; the division of these last two names is uncertain], Daoshun, and Daohong. He married Lady Liu. He placed one hundred fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Xibi, registered in a civilian household in Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Demao; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Quan and grandfather Ting both held honorary offices for longevity; his father Yi was a Registrar, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xian, Assistant Instructor at Qufu, and Xiyin; his younger brothers were Xigao and Xishen. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 394th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Xun, registered in a civilian household in Linqu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was originally from Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youcai, his grandfather Wang, his father Yongtai, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jie, and his wife was née Yin. He placed seventy-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 344th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tingshi, registered in a civilian household in Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yanqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Chaochen held an honorary office awarded for charitable contributions; his grandfather was Shanshu, his father Shiyuan was an annual tribute student, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xingshi, Songshi, and Zhishi, and his wife was née Dong. He placed forty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 361st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chi Yude, registered in a military household in Tong’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shijue; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongbao, his grandfather Min, his father Yang, and his mother née Lü. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuri; his younger brothers were Yuyi and Yuyun. His wife was née Fu. He placed twenty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Liangbin, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yishang, and he ranked second among his brothers. His age and birth month are missing or garbled [?]; his birthday was the ninth day. His great-grandfather was 𫎸 [?], an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather, Cong, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Chang, his mother was née Gu, and his stepmother was née Zhuang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Liangbao and his younger brother was Liangshi; his wife was née Yang. He placed fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Bian, registered in Mianyang Guard, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to an official household and was an added-quota student of the Mianyang subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenming, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was 𧦬 [?], his grandfather was Huan, and his father was Xuan; his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Tang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Tong, a Battalion Commander, Jin, Ying, and Sui; his younger brothers were Di, Mai, Yi, and Qian. His wife was née Li. He placed forty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dou Rulan, registered in Daming County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zihua, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-eight years old, born on the eleventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather was Shao, and his father was Bao; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Fan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rugui, an Imperial University student, and Ruzhi; his wife was née Qian. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wenhui, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dechong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yufu, his grandfather was Cheng, his father was Chu, and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wenyao; his wife was née You. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 381st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Hongyou, courtesy name Yongzhong, was registered in a military household of the Fuzhou Left Guard in Fujian and was a native of Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Ce held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather was Ang, his father was Zhu, and his mother was née Lin. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Hongxun, Hongxiu, Hongmo, Hongpan, Honglie, Hongtu, Hongzhang, Hongfan, and Hongji; his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Bolong, courtesy name Yunqing, was registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Ang held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather Qiong was a titular official; and his father Dali was a School Instructor. His father's former wife was née Zhou, his mother was née Xiang, and his stepmother was née Tu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Menghong, Zhonghe, Shulin, Menghu, Jifeng, and Jipeng; his wife was née Yang. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Pu, courtesy name Gongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Dingzhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather was Luan, his father was Mei, and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Zhen, Ji, and Huan; his wife was née Mu. He placed eighty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 367th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yue Lingshuang, courtesy name Zisu, was registered in a civilian household in Gaoyi County, Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhu, his grandfather was He, his father was Shan, and his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Lingyun and Linghan; his wife was née Zhang. He placed 107th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 357th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bao Mengqi, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a civilian household in Tunliu County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather, Jinggang; his father, Lian, held an honorary office for longevity; and his mother was née Wang. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Mengchun, Menghe (Gentleman for General Service and a princely household’s Director of Foodstuffs), Mengrui (a princely household’s Director of Foodstuffs), and Mengzhu (Physician in the Imperial Medical Service). His younger brothers were Mengyi, Mengli, Mengyan (sacrificial attendant, shengjiguan [?]), Mengxun, and Mengxian. His wife was née Wang. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhiping, courtesy name Rufan, was registered in a civilian household in Yingzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the sixth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather, Huan; his father, Chongru; his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were still living. His elder brothers were Zhimin and Zhiju; his younger brothers were Zhizhen and Zhifeng. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Ruoyu, courtesy name Keming, was registered in a civilian household in Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the thirtieth day of the intercalary sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Jing, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Shengzong. His father’s former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Wu. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Ruoqi and Ruoren. His wife was née He. He placed 124th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Ai, courtesy name Yuzhou, was registered in an officer household of Fuzhou Left Guard, Fujian, and was a native of Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Fuzhou prefectural school in Fujian specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked eleventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Lun, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Shiqi, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Shiheng, and his mother was née Chen. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Que and Keshi; his younger brothers were Kexue (Instructor), Kewei, Mao, Lü, Xiao, and Xian. His wife was née Gao. He placed fifty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chunpu, courtesy name Wenbo, was registered in a civilian household in Dingyuan County, He Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A county government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in family order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Yongning was a Prefect; his grandfather Gang was posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father Bangbiao was a Transport Commissioner. His father's principal wife, Lady Cao, held the title of Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was Lady Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Kun, Mo, Chunyi, and Shouyi, and his younger brother was Chunjian. He married Lady Gong. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Fu, courtesy name Fanglai, was registered in a civilian household in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in family order, aged thirty-five, and born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zan, his grandfather Qi, his father Yu, and his mother Lady Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shou, and he married Lady Ju. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 391st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yun, courtesy name Yongxin, was registered in a civilian household in Jingling County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Nanchang County, Chang Prefecture [?], Jiangxi. An added-quota student at the Jingling County government school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Tiande, his grandfather Wanyu, and his father Yi. His father's principal wife was Lady Tao, and his birth mother was Lady Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ming and Fan, and he married Lady Zhu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yude, courtesy name Yangui, was registered in a civilian household in Xiong County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather Lu was an Assistant Prefect and was granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father Si was Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate. His mother, Lady Su, held the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuming, and his younger brothers were Yuzhen, Yuzhuo, Yuxuan, and Yujie. He married Lady Yuan. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖讓〔知縣〕　祖洪　父綱〔府同知誥封朝列大夫〕　嫡母劉氏生母劉氏

劉自存〔貫河南開封府扶溝縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字體仁，行一，年三十五，五月二十七日生〕。曾祖憲〔義官〕，祖瑞〔知縣〕，父東〔府同知〕，母曹氏，繼母安氏。永感下，兄自修〔知州〕、自任〔序班〕、自強〔都察院右副都御史〕、自考〔監生〕，弟自養〔廩生〕、自見〔監生〕、自樂、自薦、自警，娶馬氏。河南鄉試第三十六名，會試第十二名。

杜化中〔貫河南開封府扶溝縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字民孚，行一，年二十七，十一月初二日生〕。曾祖紹〔戶部主事〕，祖孟乾〔經歷〕，父漸〔監生〕，母范氏。具慶下，弟化醇、化光，娶劉氏。河南鄉試第七十八名，會試第七十二名。

孫濟遠〔貫直隸太平府當塗縣民籍，府學生，治書經，字承澤，行二，年三十二，六月初八日生〕。曾祖讓〔知縣〕，祖洪，父綱〔府同知，進階朝列大夫〕，嫡母劉氏，生母劉氏。慈侍下，兄濟美〔知縣〕，娶端氏，繼娶黃氏、楊氏。應天府鄉試第四十二名，會試第三百八十名。
translation_en:
Liang Wenmeng, courtesy name Shangxian, was registered in a military household in Xincheng County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was listed as first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather, Jingfang; and his father, Dachao. His father’s former wife was née Zheng, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother also née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Pinmeng and Binmeng. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zicun, courtesy name Tiren, was registered in a civilian household in Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Poetry, he was listed as first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his grandfather, Rui, a county magistrate; and his father, Dong, a prefectural vice prefect. His mother was née Cao and his stepmother née An. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zixiu, a department magistrate; Ziren, an usher; Ziqiang, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; and Zikao, an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Ziyang, a government-stipend student; Zijian, an Imperial University student; Zile; Zijian; and Zijing. He married a woman née Ma. He placed thirty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Huazhong, courtesy name Minfu, was registered in a military household in Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Poetry, he was listed as first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shao, a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Mengqian, a registrar; and his father, Jian, an Imperial University student. His mother was née Fan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Huachun and Huaguang. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jiyuan, courtesy name Chengze, was registered in a civilian household in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was listed as second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, a county magistrate; his grandfather, Hong; and his father, Gang, a prefectural vice prefect promoted to the prestige rank of Chaolie dafu. His legal mother and birth mother were both née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Jimei, a county magistrate. He married a woman née Duan and subsequently women née Huang and née Yang. He placed forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 380th in the Metropolitan Examination.

戢汝止〔貫四川成都府簡州，民籍，州學生，治書經，字敬之，行一，年三十八，九月初五日生〕。曾祖漢陽，祖治安，父文宗，母張氏。具慶下，兄汝學〔教授〕、汝礪，弟汝聰、汝謙、汝選、汝逵、汝咸、汝信〔典膳〕，娶曽氏。四川鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百五名。

translation_en:
Zhao Sicheng, registered in a military household in Leping County, Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruxiao; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zihua, an honorary longevity official; his grandfather was Zan, a Police Chief; his father was Wenyuan, and his mother was née Chang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Siming, and his younger brothers were Siwen, Sigong, and Sizhong. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Yongji, registered in a military household of the Right Battalion of Qingyang Guard, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Bozhen; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Delin; his grandfather was Biao; his father was Zhi, an official holding prestige rank; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yongshi, Yongfeng, Yongheng, and Yongyu, and his younger brothers were Yongnian, Yongxiang, and Yongzhen. He married a woman née Chen. He placed second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Ruzhi, registered in a civilian household in Jian Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingzhi; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hanyang; his grandfather was Zhi'an; his father was Wenzong, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruxue, a Professor, and Ruli; his younger brothers were Rucong, Ruqian, Ruxuan, Rukui, Ruxian, and Ruxin, a Dietary Steward. He married a woman née Zeng. He placed thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Weiqing, registered in a civilian household in Jie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was an additional student of the subprefectural school, specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhongzhi; he ranked third in birth order and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather was Xiao; his father was Li, and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Weihou and Weiming. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Yingjian, registered in a civilian household in Qingcheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weixian; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Zhi; and his father, Tingzuo, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Cao; both parents were living. His younger brother was Yingzhen, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Ji, registered in a military household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yizhou; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, a Registrar; his grandfather, Sheng, received the honorary title of Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Rites; and his father, Xian, was an Investigating Censor. His mother, née Yuan, received the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his mother alone was living. His elder brother was Li, and his younger brothers were Xie and Bo. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventy-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Lian, registered in a civilian household in Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xuzhi; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongjie; his grandfather, Tingjian; and his father, Mingqing. His father's former wife was née Jie, and his mother was née Wang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Ben, and his wife was née Hu. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Keqian, registered in a salt-producing household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingyi; he ranked twenty-fifth in his family and was aged forty-three, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengduan; his grandfather, Luan; and his father, Wenxian. His mother was née Yu; both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Kecheng, and his wife was née Shao. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Qiao, registered in a civilian household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixing; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong, his grandfather Zongwu, and his father Ying, a Registrar; his mother was née Gao and his stepmother née Lu. His father was still living, and his mother was deceased. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yizhi, registered in a civilian household in Chaoyi County, Tongzhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyong; he ranked first in birth order and was aged forty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Yong, a Registrar, and his father Chaopin; his mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Dazhi. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhaolin, registered in a civilian household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Meifang; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhe, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Cong, a Recorder in the Directorate of Imperial Parks; his father was Du, an Associate Prefect; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shanglin, a Prefectural School Professor; Wenlin, an Administrator; and Rulin, an Assistant Instructor. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕聞治天
下者審所尚夏尚
忠殷尚質周尚文
皆聖人所以捄弊
之政也周之末文
日以勝當漢盛時
論治者已謂宜損
周之文致用夏之
忠况今去古益遠
文之弊其可弗捄

===

忠況今去古益遠
文之弊其可弗捄
punctuated: 皇帝制曰：「朕聞治天下者審所尚。夏尚忠，殷尚質，周尚文，皆聖人所以捄弊之政也。周之末，文日以勝。當漢盛時，論治者已謂宜損周之文，致用夏之忠。况今去古益遠，文之弊其可弗捄……」
translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: “I have heard that those who govern all under Heaven carefully consider what they should esteem. The Xia esteemed loyalty, the Yin simplicity, and the Zhou refinement: these were all policies by which the sages remedied prevailing abuses. Toward the end of the Zhou, refinement increasingly predominated. Even at the height of the Han, those who discussed government already held that Zhou refinement should be curtailed and Xia loyalty put into practice. How much more so now, when we are ever further removed from antiquity: can the abuses of refinement be left unremedied…”

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
哉然人情之趨於
偽也猶水之趨於
下也今欲使損文
而用忠其道何繇
士大夫者民之表
===
也朕於百司屢詔
以實為謂庶幾有
副朕意者徐而察
之則脩政者或徒
美觀聽而未能建
alt_text:
哉然人情之趨於
僞也猶水之趨於
下也今欲使㨗文
而用忠其道何繇
士大夫者民之表
===
也朕於百司屢詔
以實為謂庶幾有
副朕意者徐而察
之則修政者或徒
美觀聽而未能建
punctuated: 哉！然人情之趨於偽也，猶水之趨於下也。今欲使損文而用忠，其道何繇？士大夫者，民之表也。朕於百司屢詔，以實為謂，庶幾有副朕意者。徐而察之，則脩政者或徒美觀聽，而未能建
translation_en: …! Yet human inclinations tend toward falsity just as water flows downward. If we now wish to reduce outward embellishment and put sincerity into practice, by what path can this be achieved? Scholar-officials are exemplars for the people. I have repeatedly issued edicts to the various offices, calling for substance [?], in the hope that some would fulfill my intentions. Yet upon observing them over time, I find that those who attend to government sometimes merely make an impressive show to the eyes and ears, without being able to establish…

或徒工詞說而未
能效濟時之猷稱
愛民者或飾甘言
而乏一體之心名
任事者或張虛聲
而罕特立之節致
身之義非不知也
而鮮克盡瘁於蹇
蹇愼獨之訓非不

translation_en: …the work of securing the realm. Those who submit proposals may merely excel at verbal argument, yet fail to offer plans that meet the needs of the times. Those who profess to love the people may embellish sweet words, yet lack the heart that regards the people as one body with themselves. They are not ignorant of the duty to devote themselves to service, yet few can expend their utmost strength in steadfast loyalty. As for the teaching to be watchful over oneself when alone, it is not that they have not…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
聞也而率多惰行
於冥冥然則欲望
民之還於忠也不
亦難乎夫古之民
不賞而勸不怒而
威於鈇鉞乃今士
大夫且不能然其
故何也爾諸士上
下古今必有慨於
茲矣其為朕根極

translation_en: …heard it, yet most are lax in their conduct when unseen. If this is so, is it not difficult to hope that the people will return to loyalty? The people of antiquity were encouraged without rewards and, without any display of anger, stood in awe as before the executioner's axe. Yet today even scholar-officials cannot conduct themselves thus. Why is this? You scholars, surveying past and present, must surely feel deeply concerned about this. For Us, trace to their very roots…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
臣范應期
臣對臣聞帝王之致治也法天道以經時政
而後有以啓天下用忠之化肅臣紀以一衆
志而後可以鼓天下效忠之心盖君猶天也
臣與民皆覆冒于天而惟君所率者也天道
默運於上而化育流行之實未始不隨時令
以順其施人君端拱于上而化民成俗之方
未始不隨世運以善其治然君也者主宰化
機于上者也臣也者所以行君之令而致之
民者也欲有以更天下之化而不先之於臣
===
以肅其紀則上有崇本之心而或窒于承宣
之未至上有勵化之術而或阻于賛襄之無
良雖日以其令布諸天下而庶官百職之近
且有泥焉而弗行者其何以達諸四海九州
之遠而妙夫推準動化之機也哉故必法天
道以運夫因時之政而變通損益獨得夫神
化之微權肅臣紀以端夫道揆之本而倡導
率先尤得夫馭下之大體則綱維立而運化
有機紀法嚴而宣化有地鼓舞于上而百官
庶職咸篤夫忠貞不貳之心風行于下而四
