臣對：臣聞帝王之致治也，法天道以經時政，而後有以啓天下用忠之化；肅臣紀以一衆志，而後可以鼓天下效忠之心。盖君猶天也，臣與民皆覆冒于天，而惟君所率者也。天道默運於上，而化育流行之實，未始不隨時令以順其施；人君端拱于上，而化民成俗之方，未始不隨世運以善其治。然君也者，主宰化機于上者也；臣也者，所以行君之令而致之民者也。欲有以更天下之化，而不先之於臣以肅其紀，則上有崇本之心，而或窒于承宣之未至；上有勵化之術，而或阻于賛襄之無良。雖日以其令布諸天下，而庶官百職之近，且有泥焉而弗行者，其何以達諸四海九州之遠，而妙夫推準動化之機也哉？故必法天道以運夫因時之政，而變通損益，獨得夫神化之微權；肅臣紀以端夫道揆之本，而倡導率先，尤得夫馭下之大體。則綱維立而運化有機，紀法嚴而宣化有地，鼓舞于上，而百官庶職咸篤夫忠貞不貳之心；風行于下，而四
translation_en:
Your servant, Fan Yingqi.

Your servant replies: I have heard that, in bringing about good government, emperors and kings model themselves on the Way of Heaven to order the affairs of their age; only then can they initiate a transformation throughout the realm that puts loyalty into practice. They enforce discipline among their ministers to unite the intentions of all; only then can they inspire throughout the realm the desire to render loyal service. For the ruler is like Heaven. Ministers and people alike live beneath Heaven’s covering, and all follow the ruler’s lead. The Way of Heaven operates silently above, yet its actual work of nurturing and transforming all things invariably follows the seasons, so that its influences are fittingly bestowed. The ruler sits upright with hands folded above, yet his methods for transforming the people and shaping their customs invariably follow the course of the age, so as to perfect his government. The ruler presides above over the workings of transformation; ministers carry out his commands and convey them to the people.

If he wishes to renew the moral transformation of the realm but does not begin with his ministers by enforcing their discipline, then, although he desires to honor the foundations of government, that purpose may be thwarted by failures in receiving and promulgating his commands. Although he possesses methods for encouraging transformation, they may be obstructed by the lack of worthy assistance. Even if his commands are proclaimed throughout the realm every day, some among the many officials and officeholders close at hand will become mired and fail to act. How, then, can those commands reach the distant reaches of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, and bring to perfection the process by which his example is extended and transformation set in motion?

Thus he must model himself on the Way of Heaven in conducting government suited to the times, adapting, reducing, and augmenting as circumstances require, and himself grasping the subtle discretion underlying wondrous transformation. He must enforce discipline among his ministers to rectify the foundations of government’s guiding moral standards, taking the lead and setting an example, and thereby fully grasping the essential principles of governing his subordinates. Then the framework of order will be established, and transformation will have a means of operation; discipline and laws will be strict, and the spread of transforming influence will have a foundation. Inspired and encouraged from above, all officials and officeholders will strengthen their resolve to remain loyal, steadfast, and undivided in allegiance; as that influence sweeps like the wind among those below, throughout the Four …

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
海九州咸效夫忠順不渝之節奠國祚于久
安長治之盛升世道于時雍風動之庥唐虞
三代之治不可復見於
今日也哉欽惟
皇帝陛下
稟聖神間出之資
建帝王中興之業際
乾元統天之運膺
壽考作人之符秉一誠以格
帝而
===
帝祉申錫于無疆崇四德以通
玄而
玄貺荐加于有永然猶
周察吏治
洞燭民隱
心運而化行如馳
令發而威動萬里蓋誠登三咸五而極千載一
時之盛者臣愚竊伏草茅有懷欲獻久矣廼
者叨有司之薦得與
大廷之對

punctuated:
海九州咸效夫忠順不渝之節，奠國祚于久安長治之盛，升世道于時雍風動之庥，唐虞三代之治不可復見於今日也哉？
欽惟皇帝陛下，稟聖神間出之資，建帝王中興之業，際乾元統天之運，膺壽考作人之符，秉一誠以格帝，而帝祉申錫于無疆；崇四德以通玄，而玄貺荐加于有永。然猶周察吏治，洞燭民隱，心運而化行如馳，令發而威動萬里，蓋誠登三咸五而極千載一時之盛者。
臣愚竊伏草茅，有懷欲獻久矣。廼者叨有司之薦，得與大廷之對
translation_en:
…throughout the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, all display unwavering loyalty and obedience, securing the dynasty’s fortunes in the flourishing condition of enduring peace and lasting good government, and bringing the world into blessed concord under the transforming influence of virtue. Could the good government of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties not be seen again today?
Reverently I consider that Your Majesty the Emperor possesses the qualities of a sage of divine understanding, such as appears only rarely, and has established the achievement of a sovereign who restores his dynasty’s greatness. You have encountered the auspicious workings of the Creative Origin that governs Heaven, and received the tokens of longevity and the nurturing of worthy men. Through undivided sincerity you reach the Lord on High, whose blessings are repeatedly bestowed without limit; by exalting the four virtues, you commune with the Mysterious, whose gifts are renewed for all eternity. Yet you still scrutinize the administration of officials comprehensively and perceive the people’s hidden sufferings clearly. Your mind moves, and your transforming influence spreads swiftly; your commands issue, and your might stirs ten thousand li. Truly, you stand alongside the Three Sovereigns and equal the Five Emperors, attaining the utmost splendor of an age encountered only once in a thousand years.
Your foolish servant, dwelling humbly among the common people, has long cherished thoughts he wished to present. Recently, undeservedly favored with the recommendation of the responsible officials, I have been permitted to take part in answering the policy question at the great court…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
聖問所及特惓惓焉首舉三代迭尚之宜次及臣
民尚文之弊而欲臣等深察夫捄弊之源條
陳夫用忠之道大哉
皇言更化善治之心見乎詞矣敢不殫竭愚衷以
對揚
休命于萬一耶臣嘗聞之書曰惟天聰明惟聖
時憲又曰道有升降政由俗革蓋言天之立
君所以代天而施因時之政也又曰惟臣欽
若惟民從乂蓋言君之得臣所以助君而敷
化民之猷者也君代天而為之子當以天之
===
心為心臣體君而為之用當以君之心為心
君以天之心為心其道法天而不私臣以君
之心為心其道從君而不貳此自有天地以
来未之有改者也粵稽諸古夏后氏之王天
下其道尚忠矣所以承唐虞之後法天道而
以忠為教也而當時文命四敷聲教四訖以
成一代尚忠之化者豈神禹以一人之聰明
獨運于上哉惟其迪知忱恂之臣有以體君
心而協贊于下爾至于忠弊而為野亦其勢
之使然而聖人不能逆觀其變也有殷氏之

民尚文之弊而欲臣等深察夫捄弊之源條
陳夫用忠之道大哉
皇言更化善治之心見乎詞矣敢不殫竭愚衷以
對揚
休命于萬一耶臣嘗聞之書曰惟天聰明惟聖
時憲又曰道有升降政由俗革盖言天之立
君所以代天而施因時之政也又曰惟臣欽
若惟民從乂盖言君之得臣所以助君而敷
化民之猷者也君代天而為之子當以天之
心為心臣體君而為之用當以君之心為心
===
君以天之心為心其道法天而不私臣以君
之心為心其道從君而不貳此自有天地以
來未之有改者也粤稽古夏后氏之王天
下其道尚忠矣所以承唐虞之後法天道而
以忠為教也而當時文命四敷聲教四訖以
成一代尚忠之化者豈神禹以一人之聰明
獨運于上哉惟其迪知忱恂之臣有以體君
心而協贊于下爾至于忠弊而為野亦其勢
之使然而聖人不能逆覩其變也有殷氏之
punctuated:
聖問所及，特惓惓焉，首舉三代迭尚之宜，次及臣民尚文之弊，而欲臣等深察夫捄弊之源，條陳夫用忠之道。大哉，皇言！更化善治之心見乎詞矣。敢不殫竭愚衷，以對揚休命于萬一耶？
臣嘗聞之，《書》曰：「惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。」又曰：「道有升降，政由俗革。」蓋言天之立君，所以代天而施因時之政也。又曰：「惟臣欽若，惟民從乂。」蓋言君之得臣，所以助君而敷化民之猷者也。君代天而為之子，當以天之心為心；臣體君而為之用，當以君之心為心。君以天之心為心，其道法天而不私；臣以君之心為心，其道從君而不貳。此自有天地以來未之有改者也。
粵稽諸古，夏后氏之王天下，其道尚忠矣，所以承唐虞之後，法天道而以忠為教也。而當時文命四敷，聲教四訖，以成一代尚忠之化者，豈神禹以一人之聰明獨運于上哉？惟其迪知忱恂之臣，有以體君心而協贊于下爾。至于忠弊而為野，亦其勢之使然，而聖人不能逆觀其變也。有殷氏之
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s questions show particular solicitude in the matters they address. They first raise the appropriateness of the successive values upheld by the Three Dynasties, then turn to the abuses arising from officials’ and commoners’ preference for outward refinement. You wish us, your servants, to examine deeply the fundamental means of remedying these abuses and to set forth, point by point, the way to employ wholehearted sincerity. How great are Your Majesty’s words! Your desire to transform governance and govern well is manifest in them. Dare I fail to exhaust my humble thoughts in answering and extolling even a ten-thousandth part of your gracious charge?
I have heard these words in the Book of Documents: “Heaven is discerning; the sage takes this as his model.” It also says: “The Way rises and declines; government changes with customs.” This means that Heaven establishes rulers to act on its behalf and administer government suited to the times. It also says: “Ministers reverently comply; the people follow and are well governed.” This means that a ruler obtains ministers to assist him in carrying out plans for transforming the people. The ruler acts for Heaven and is its son; he should therefore take Heaven’s heart as his own. Ministers embody the ruler’s intentions and serve as his instruments; they should therefore take the ruler’s heart as their own. When the ruler takes Heaven’s heart as his own, his way is to model himself on Heaven without selfishness. When ministers take the ruler’s heart as their own, their way is to follow the ruler without divided allegiance. This has never changed since Heaven and Earth came into being.
Examining antiquity, when the house of Xia ruled All under Heaven, its way esteemed wholehearted sincerity. Thus, succeeding Tang and Yu, it modeled itself on Heaven’s Way and made sincerity the basis of its teaching. At that time, its civilizing commands spread in all directions and its moral influence reached everywhere, bringing about an entire dynasty’s transformation through esteem for sincerity. Could this have been accomplished by the divine Yu exercising one man’s discernment alone above? It was only because his enlightened, wise, earnest, and faithful ministers could embody the ruler’s heart and assist him below. When sincerity deteriorated into crudeness, this too resulted from the tendency of circumstances; even the sage could not foresee the change. As for the house of Yin’s…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
王天下其道尚質矣所以救忠之弊法天道
而以質為教也而當時商邑用協四方丕式
所以成一代尚質之化者豈成湯以一人之
勇智獨運於上哉惟其克宅克俊之臣體君
心而協賛于下爾至于質弊而為鬼亦其勢
之使然而聖人不能逆為之慮也周文武之
王天下也其道尚文矣所以救質之弊法天
道而以文為教也而當時有夏脩和天下大
定以成一代尚文之化者豈文武以一人之
明聖獨運于上哉惟其四友五臣之賢體君
===
心而協賛于下爾至于文之弊而為靡亦其
勢之所趨而聖人不能預為之所也夫夏后
殷周之世天下之盛王也忠質文之迭尚天
下之至治也而補偏救弊之方不能不因時
以為之損益推行化導之術不能不待臣以
為之賛襄至若漢臣董仲舒損文用忠之論
盖有感於驕淫奢靡之習而欲得乎返朴還
淳之理可謂深識乎治體者也然則臣之所
謂法天道以經時政者庶幾萬世不易之常
道而所謂肅臣紀以一眾志者豈非一時宣

謂法天道以經時政者庶幾萬世不易之常

punctuated:
王天下，其道尚質矣，所以救忠之弊，法天道而以質為教也。而當時商邑用協，四方丕式，所以成一代尚質之化者，豈成湯以一人之勇智獨運於上哉？惟其克宅克俊之臣體君心而協賛于下爾。至于質弊而為鬼，亦其勢之使然，而聖人不能逆為之慮也。周文武之王天下也，其道尚文矣，所以救質之弊，法天道而以文為教也。而當時有夏脩和，天下大定，以成一代尚文之化者，豈文武以一人之明聖獨運于上哉？惟其四友五臣之賢體君心而協賛于下爾。至于文之弊而為靡，亦其勢之所趨，而聖人不能預為之所也。
夫夏后殷周之世，天下之盛王也；忠質文之迭尚，天下之至治也。而補偏救弊之方，不能不因時以為之損益；推行化導之術，不能不待臣以為之賛襄。至若漢臣董仲舒損文用忠之論，盖有感於驕淫奢靡之習，而欲得乎返朴還淳之理，可謂深識乎治體者也。然則臣之所謂法天道以經時政者，庶幾萬世不易之常道；而所謂肅臣紀以一眾志者，豈非一時宣
translation_en:
…in ruling All under Heaven, they esteemed simplicity. This was how they remedied the abuses of wholehearted sincerity, modeled themselves on the Way of Heaven, and made simplicity the basis of their teaching. At that time, the Shang capital was brought into harmony, and the four quarters took it as their great example. Was the transforming influence of an age that esteemed simplicity achieved by Cheng Tang exercising his courage and wisdom alone on high? It was only because his ministers, capable of holding office and displaying excellence, embodied their ruler’s intentions and assisted him below. When simplicity deteriorated into preoccupation with spirits, this too was brought about by the tendency of circumstances; even the sage could not anticipate it and devise precautions.
When Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou ruled All under Heaven, they esteemed cultural refinement. This was how they remedied the abuses of simplicity, modeled themselves on the Way of Heaven, and made cultural refinement the basis of their teaching. At that time, the lands of Xia were ordered and harmonious, and All under Heaven was firmly settled. Was the transforming influence of an age that esteemed cultural refinement achieved by Wen and Wu exercising their enlightened sagacity alone on high? It was only because their worthy Four Friends and Five Ministers embodied their ruler’s intentions and assisted him below. When cultural refinement deteriorated into extravagance, this too was the direction in which circumstances tended; even the sage could not make provision for it beforehand [?].
The rulers of the Xia, Yin, and Zhou eras were illustrious kings of All under Heaven. Their successive esteem for wholehearted sincerity, simplicity, and cultural refinement represented governance at its highest. Yet measures to correct imbalances and remedy abuses necessarily required adjustments to suit the times; methods of extending transforming instruction necessarily depended on ministers for assistance. As for the Han minister Dong Zhongshu’s argument for reducing cultural refinement and employing wholehearted sincerity, he was evidently moved by prevailing habits of arrogance, excess, luxury, and extravagance, and sought the principle of returning to simplicity and restoring purity. He may be said to have understood deeply the essentials of governance. Thus, what your servant calls modeling oneself on the Way of Heaven to regulate the affairs of the age is perhaps the constant Way, unchanging through ten thousand generations. And what I call tightening discipline among ministers to unite the wills of all—is this not, for the age, the crucial means of spreading…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
化之要機也哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝承天啓運立萬世之丕基
成祖文皇帝安内攘外纘百王之令緒其規模之
敦厚施為之忠實見於先民所傳者詳且悉
矣臣請舉其槩而言之紀綱不紊而中外有
相維之勢體統有序而大小有相制之權重
邦國之本原而
宗社先建謹郡縣之風化而庠序先立取周之八
法而内有
勅諭以勵九卿取唐之六典而外有
===
===
律令以布諸省羅賢才于館閣非隆師重道之
心乎書衍義于廡壁非稽古正學之事乎
大誥三編既有以新天下之耳目而示其勸懲
大明集禮一書又有以一天下之心志而端其
趨向以至啓忠萌賢之篇昭其度也稽制醒
貪之錄正其範也臥碑監規之條端其則也
資世教民之訓溥其化也孝順事實之書植
其本也為善陰隲之編發其良也以崇理學
而人才無不正以抑浮費而風俗無不淳其
所以議諸

punctuated: 化之要機也哉！洪惟我太祖高皇帝承天啓運，立萬世之丕基；成祖文皇帝安内攘外，纘百王之令緒。其規模之敦厚、施為之忠實，見於先民所傳者，詳且悉矣。臣請舉其槩而言之：紀綱不紊，而中外有相維之勢；體統有序，而大小有相制之權。重邦國之本原，而宗社先建；謹郡縣之風化，而庠序先立。取周之八法，而内有勅諭以勵九卿；取唐之六典，而外有律令以布諸省。羅賢才于館閣，非隆師重道之心乎？書衍義于廡壁，非稽古正學之事乎？《大誥》三編，既有以新天下之耳目，而示其勸懲；《大明集禮》一書，又有以一天下之心志，而端其趨向。以至啓忠萌賢之篇，昭其度也；稽制醒貪之錄，正其範也；臥碑監規之條，端其則也；資世教民之訓，溥其化也；孝順事實之書，植其本也；為善陰隲之編，發其良也。以崇理學，而人才無不正；以抑浮費，而風俗無不淳。其所以議諸
translation_en:
…the crucial means of spreading moral transformation at this time!

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s mandate and inaugurated the dynasty’s destiny, laying its grand foundation for ten thousand generations; Emperor Chengzu Wen secured the realm within and repelled threats from without, carrying forward the splendid legacy of the hundred kings. The magnanimity of their institutions and the sincerity of their actions are recorded fully and in detail in what our predecessors have transmitted. Your servant begs leave to outline them.

The governing order was free of confusion, so that the central and regional administrations sustained one another; the hierarchy was properly ordered, so that higher and lower authorities possessed powers of mutual restraint. Giving weight to the foundations of the state, they first established the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain. Attending carefully to moral instruction in the prefectures and counties, they first established schools. Drawing upon the Eight Regulations of Zhou, they issued imperial admonitions at court to spur on the Nine Ministers; drawing upon the Six Statutes of Tang, they promulgated laws and ordinances throughout the provinces. Was not their gathering of worthy and talented men in the literary offices an expression of their resolve to honor teachers and esteem the Way? Was not their inscription of the Extended Meaning on the walls of the side galleries an undertaking to examine antiquity and rectify learning?

The three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements refreshed the eyes and ears of all under Heaven and made clear their encouragements and punishments. The Collected Rituals of the Great Ming, in turn, unified the minds and aspirations of all under Heaven and set their aims aright. Furthermore, the writings on awakening loyalty and fostering worthiness [?] made their standards manifest; the records on examining institutions and awakening the avaricious [?] corrected their models; the provisions of the Recumbent Steles and the Directorate of Education’s regulations established proper rules; the instructions for aiding the world and teaching the people extended their transforming influence; the book of factual accounts of filial obedience planted the roots; and the compilation Doing Good and Hidden Merit brought forth innate goodness. By honoring the Learning of Principle, they ensured that all men of talent were upright; by curbing wasteful expenditure, they ensured that all customs were sound. The measures that they deliberated upon in…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
朝廷頒諸邦國而風行于天下者固皆確乎不
貳粹乎無疵有成周文質適中之美而本之
有夏忠信之孚盖信乎超越三代而陋有漢
於下風矣一時內外諸臣同心協德以成
一代光明之業交懽濟美而永貽萬世無疆之
庥固由我
二祖
天錫仁聖而馭臣之有方實亦一時諸臣慶知遇
之隆秉匪躬之節忠愛而不忍欺寅畏而不
敢欺也今我
===
皇上久道成化而殷憂愈切于日中
純心用賢而一念尤先于知恤一有微能則隨
材以授任而詔爵得器使之宜一有微勞則
因功以懋賞而賚予極寵綏之厚委任之專
也堅如金石而讒間不能携其情責成之篤
也假之便宜而進退得以行其志至於
恩禮之優渥盎乎如陽春之煦育而萬物咸被
其光華
德意之交孚藹然如父子之真切而羣工樂有
所怙恃真可謂推心置腹而相待一體者矣

punctuated:
朝廷，頒諸邦國，而風行于天下者，固皆確乎不貳，粹乎無疵，有成周文質適中之美，而本之有夏忠信之孚。盖信乎超越三代，而陋有漢於下風矣。一時內外諸臣，同心協德，以成一代光明之業，交懽濟美，而永貽萬世無疆之庥。固由我二祖天錫仁聖，而馭臣之有方，實亦一時諸臣慶知遇之隆，秉匪躬之節，忠愛而不忍欺，寅畏而不敢欺也。
今我皇上久道成化，而殷憂愈切于日中；純心用賢，而一念尤先于知恤。一有微能，則隨材以授任，而詔爵得器使之宜；一有微勞，則因功以懋賞，而賚予極寵綏之厚。委任之專也，堅如金石，而讒間不能携其情；責成之篤也，假之便宜，而進退得以行其志。至於恩禮之優渥，盎乎如陽春之煦育，而萬物咸被其光華；德意之交孚，藹然如父子之真切，而羣工樂有所怙恃。真可謂推心置腹，而相待一體者矣。
translation_en:
…at court, promulgated throughout the realm, and spread like the wind through all under Heaven: these were assuredly all firm and unwavering, pure and without blemish. They possessed the beauty of the perfected Zhou’s proper balance between refinement and substance, while being rooted in the trusted loyalty and good faith of the Xia. Indeed, they surpassed the Three Dynasties and relegated the Han to an inferior position. The officials then serving both at court and in the provinces united their hearts and joined their virtues to accomplish the glorious work of a dynasty. In mutual accord they furthered its excellence, bequeathing boundless blessings to ten thousand generations. This certainly arose from the Heaven-bestowed benevolence and sagacity of our two founding ancestors and their skill in governing their ministers. Yet it also arose because the ministers of that time rejoiced in the exceptional recognition and favor they received and maintained selfless integrity: their loyal devotion made them unable to bear deceiving their sovereigns, and their reverent awe made them dare not do so.
Now our Emperor has long upheld the Way and brought about moral transformation, yet his profound concern grows still more earnest at the sun’s zenith. With a pure heart he employs the worthy, giving foremost thought to understanding and caring for them. If someone possesses even a modest ability, he assigns responsibilities according to that person’s talents, and his decreed grants of rank fittingly employ each according to his capacity. If someone renders even a modest service, he bestows generous rewards according to the achievement, extending favor and reassurance through gifts of the utmost munificence. His wholehearted trust in those he appoints is firm as metal and stone; slander and efforts to sow discord cannot loosen this bond. So earnest is his expectation that they accomplish their tasks that he grants them discretion to act as circumstances require, allowing them to carry out their intentions in advancing or withdrawing. As for the abundance of his gracious favor and courtesy, it overflows like the nurturing warmth of spring sunshine, whose radiance reaches all things. The mutual trust inspired by his virtuous intentions is as warm and sincere as the affection between father and son, and all his officials rejoice in having someone upon whom they can rely. Truly, he may be said to open his heart to them in complete confidence, sovereign and ministers treating one another as members of one body.

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
而又屢
詔百司務崇實意凡茲臣庶咸宜以
陛下之心為心而今有不盡然者其在卿士僚佐
豈無分猷宣力以建保邦之業者乎而徒美

translation_en:
…Moreover, you have repeatedly commanded all offices to give priority to sincerity of intent. All these officials and common people ought to take Your Majesty’s heart as their own, yet some now fail to do so fully. Among the high officials and their subordinate officers, are there none who contribute counsel and exert their strength to secure the state? Yet there are still some who merely make a fine impression on the eyes and ears, without producing tangible results. Among the court attendants, censors, and remonstrance officials, are there none who deliberate and offer counsel to enlighten the sovereign, presenting plans to meet the needs of the age? Yet there are still some who merely excel at rhetoric, without achieving practical usefulness. Among the various offices and bureaus, are there none who courageously undertake responsibilities, faithfully discharge their duties, and work harmoniously with their colleagues? Yet there may be some who merely trumpet an empty reputation, displaying no integrity in taking an independent stand. Among the provincial administration and surveillance officials, prefects, and magistrates, are there none who circulate and proclaim the sovereign’s beneficent, harmonious governance and safeguard the common people? Yet there may be some who violate the Way to seek praise, fundamentally lacking any sense of forming one body with their sovereign. Who has not repeatedly heard of the duty to devote oneself to service upon first entering office? Yet, judging by their eventual conduct, few can exhaust their strength in steadfast loyalty. Who has not heard from the beginning of childhood study the injunction to be watchful over oneself even when alone? Yet, examining their actual conduct, most merely embellish their behavior where others can plainly see it. If officials are like this, how much more difficult must it be, throughout the vast realm and among its myriad people, to reverse the ill effects of outward refinement prevailing over substance and restore a spirit of loyalty and sincerity? Can this be achieved?
Your servant has reverently read the imperial composition, which says: “At the end of the Zhou dynasty, outward refinement increasingly prevailed. Now that we are still further removed from antiquity, can we leave the harmful effects of such refinement uncorrected?” Your servant has also reverently read the imperial composition, which says: “If we wish to diminish outward refinement and employ loyalty, by what way can this be accomplished? Scholar-officials are models for the people. I have repeatedly issued edicts to all offices, speaking of the need for substance, in the hope that there might be some who would fulfill…”

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
朕之意者乃今士大夫且不能然其故何也臣
甞目擊時弊而有槩於中久矣况今
清問下及敢不為
陛下陳之夫臣者君之輔也法之守也民之望也
世道之所以斡旋而轉運者也今
陛下燭弊之源炳如日月而諸臣不能奉宣
德意以弘倡導之機
陛下救弊之勇决如雷霆而諸臣不能奉揚
德威以成釐正之化玆欲使天下返薄而還忠敦
本而尚實抑豈無其道哉臣甞聞之陸贄曰
===
漢高稟大度故其時多瑰傑不羈之材漢武
好英風故其時富瓌詭立名之士漢宣精吏
治故其時萃循良核實之能言下之係乎所
率也漢之三君固非純乎王道之主然而御
臣有其道則天下之趨向隨之而况
聖明在上尤必有不疾而速不言而喻者乎是故
今日之治惟在
陛下一轉移之間爾蓋
陛下之於羣臣寵之以祿秩矣榮之以聲名矣忠
信以孚其心而疑貳不萌于念慮禮儀以重

punctuated: 朕之意者，乃今士大夫且不能然，其故何也？」臣甞目擊時弊，而有槩於中久矣。况今清問下及，敢不為陛下陳之？夫臣者，君之輔也，法之守也，民之望也，世道之所以斡旋而轉運者也。今陛下燭弊之源，炳如日月，而諸臣不能奉宣德意，以弘倡導之機；陛下救弊之勇，决如雷霆，而諸臣不能奉揚德威，以成釐正之化。玆欲使天下返薄而還忠，敦本而尚實，抑豈無其道哉？臣甞聞之，陸贄曰：「漢高稟大度，故其時多瑰傑不羈之材；漢武好英風，故其時富瓌詭立名之士；漢宣精吏治，故其時萃循良核實之能。」言下之係乎所率也。漢之三君，固非純乎王道之主，然而御臣有其道，則天下之趨向隨之，而况聖明在上，尤必有不疾而速、不言而喻者乎？是故今日之治，惟在陛下一轉移之間爾。蓋陛下之於羣臣，寵之以祿秩矣，榮之以聲名矣，忠信以孚其心，而疑貳不萌于念慮，禮儀以重
translation_en:
…my intentions; yet now even the scholar-officials cannot act thus. Why is this?” Your servant has personally witnessed the abuses of our time and has long felt indignation within. Now that your august inquiry has reached me, how could I dare not lay these matters before Your Majesty? Ministers assist the ruler, uphold the laws, and are those to whom the people look. They are the means by which the course of the age is redirected and transformed. Your Majesty illuminates the source of these abuses as brilliantly as the sun and moon, yet your ministers cannot proclaim your virtuous intentions so as to extend your guiding influence. Your Majesty’s resolve to remedy these abuses is as decisive as thunder, yet your ministers cannot uphold and spread your virtuous authority so as to bring about reform. If we now wish to make all under Heaven turn from shallowness back to sincerity, strengthen the foundations, and esteem substance, can there really be no way to do so?

Your servant has heard these words of Lu Zhi: “Gaozu of Han was endowed with magnanimity, and thus his age abounded in outstanding men of unfettered talent. Emperor Wu of Han admired heroic spirit, and thus his age was rich in extraordinary men who established reputations. Emperor Xuan of Han was expert in the administration of officials, and thus his age gathered capable men who governed conscientiously and verified actual performance.” This means that those below depend upon the leadership they receive. These three Han rulers were certainly not sovereigns who adhered wholly to the Kingly Way. Yet when they had a method for directing their ministers, the inclinations of all under Heaven followed them. How much more, with a sagely and enlightened ruler above, must there be results achieved swiftly without haste and understanding attained without words! Thus the good government of the present day depends solely upon a single change of direction by Your Majesty.

In your treatment of your ministers, Your Majesty has favored them with stipends and ranks and honored them with renown. Through sincerity and trustworthiness you have won their hearts, so that doubt and divided allegiance do not arise in their thoughts; through ritual propriety you give weight to…

其報而恩施毎溢于分涯其體之已無不至
而待之已無不厚矣然優養培植之後不可
無振揚飭勵之功而惇厚博大之餘不可無
精明果銳之氣盖一於慈惠則惠褻而不以
為恩過于寵榮則寵加而不以為德是故廷
臣之細過可弗詰也而忠邪之辨當嚴則不
可不稽其心迹之素言官之狂戇可弗懲也
而事理之原當審則不可徒徇其奏對之詞
事無首尾泛相沿及者弗槩坐焉可也其或
罔上以行私背公而徇黨則天討之彰非所
===
以正其欺歟所見不同本無意必者弗過求
焉可也其或陽非而陰是穿鑿以附會則殛
罰之典非所以懲其佞歟誠一不貳之臣委
之腹心非過也而
恩威恒主於獨斷則益以勵其秉德明恤之心
篤棐效忠之士晉之崇階匪僭也而
仁義毎見其並行則愈以堅其靖恭體國之念
臺省重任以待藩臬之良似矣若本無旬宣
之績而徒貽尸素之誚者豈宜使之溷跡于
朝端資格弗循以拔卓異之才似矣若外托

…their recompense, while your gracious favors constantly exceed their allotted bounds. Your consideration for them has been utterly thorough, and your treatment of them utterly generous. Yet, after generously nurturing and cultivating them, there must also be efforts to rouse, discipline, and encourage them; alongside magnanimity and broad generosity, there must also be clear discernment, resolution, and vigor. For if one relies solely on kindness, favors become commonplace and cease to be regarded as grace; if honors and distinctions are excessive, further favor ceases to be regarded as beneficence.

Thus, minor faults of court officials may be left unchallenged; but the distinction between loyalty and wickedness must be strict, so their habitual intentions and conduct must be examined. The rash bluntness of remonstrance officials may go unpunished; but the underlying principles of affairs must be carefully considered, so one must not simply follow the words of their memorials and replies. Those who played no initiating or concluding role in an affair and became implicated only through loose connections [?] may properly be spared indiscriminate punishment. But if any deceive their sovereign to advance private interests, turn their backs on public duty, and favor their factions, is not the manifestation of Heaven’s chastisement the means to correct their deceit? Those whose views differ, but who harbor neither preconceived judgments nor obstinate insistence, may properly be spared excessive demands. But if any outwardly condemn what they inwardly approve, twisting interpretations to force agreement, are not the statutes of punishment the means to chastise their flattery?

It is no error to entrust intimate responsibilities to ministers of single-minded sincerity and undivided loyalty. Yet if grace and authority remain subject to your sole decision, this will further encourage their resolve to uphold virtue and exercise discerning compassion. It is no unwarranted elevation to advance men who steadfastly assist you and render loyal service to exalted rank. Yet if benevolence and righteousness are always seen to operate together, this will further strengthen their commitment to devoted reverence and concern for the state.

Reserving weighty responsibilities in the Censorate and central ministries for worthy officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions seems fitting. But if they have no achievements in spreading imperial beneficence and have merely incurred the reproach of holding office idly and drawing unearned salaries, how could they properly be allowed to mingle among the leaders at court? text:
慎重之名而陰為鑽刺之術者豈可使之濫
塵乎名器又或間行不測之威以懾奸宄之
志時申核實之令以防文飾之奸某稱賢能
也必審其賢能之實而名浮于德者在所不
容某稱勞勩也必攷其勞勩之詳而祿浮于
功者在所必黜推而至於天下之大四海之
廣由大臣以督監司由監司以督守令申嚴
乎紀律而大起明作之功振肅乎綱維而痛
革虛浮之弊使天下洗心而滌志聚精而會
神一賞罰之施也若神明之降鑒而以勸以
===
懲凛然一天威之震懾一號令之布也若風
雨之適至而以鼓以舞靡然一神氣之流行
譬則玄樞默運而五緯之迭經者旋轉順逆
隨其躔度次舍而莫之違權衡在我而庶物
之錯綜者低昻輕重任吾之調劑均節而不
敢抗是其
總攬乾綱機制物則
威命靈爽侔乎造物而凡紛然羣生者皆熈然
其從欲者矣將見一心所向百辟爭先一人
所指群工效力利在一身而非以

punctuated: 慎重之名，而陰為鑽刺之術者，豈可使之濫塵乎名器？又或間行不測之威，以懾奸宄之志；時申核實之令，以防文飾之奸。某稱賢能也，必審其賢能之實，而名浮于德者在所不容；某稱勞勩也，必攷其勞勩之詳，而祿浮于功者在所必黜。推而至於天下之大、四海之廣，由大臣以督監司，由監司以督守令，申嚴乎紀律，而大起明作之功；振肅乎綱維，而痛革虛浮之弊。使天下洗心而滌志，聚精而會神。一賞罰之施也，若神明之降鑒，而以勸以懲，凛然一天威之震懾；一號令之布也，若風雨之適至，而以鼓以舞，靡然一神氣之流行。譬則玄樞默運，而五緯之迭經者，旋轉順逆，隨其躔度次舍而莫之違；權衡在我，而庶物之錯綜者，低昻輕重，任吾之調劑均節而不敢抗。是其總攬乾綱，機制物則，威命靈爽侔乎造物，而凡紛然羣生者，皆熈然其從欲者矣。將見一心所向，百辟爭先；一人所指，群工效力。利在一身而非以
translation_en: …the name of prudence, while secretly employing methods of unscrupulous advancement—how could such men be allowed to sully official rank and its insignia indiscriminately? At times, moreover, exercise unpredictable severity to intimidate those intent on wrongdoing; periodically reiterate orders to verify actual performance, to prevent the fraud of deceptive embellishment. If someone is acclaimed as worthy and capable, one must scrutinize the reality of his worth and ability; those whose reputation exceeds their virtue must not be tolerated. If someone is acclaimed for meritorious toil, one must examine the particulars of his service; those whose emoluments exceed their achievements must certainly be dismissed. Extend this throughout the vast realm and the broad lands within the Four Seas: have the great ministers supervise the surveillance officials, and the surveillance officials supervise the prefects and magistrates. Enforce discipline strictly and greatly advance the work of discerning governance; restore order to the governing framework and thoroughly eliminate the abuses of empty pretence. Make all under Heaven cleanse their hearts and purify their intentions, concentrate their energies and collect their minds. Each dispensation of reward or punishment will be like divine beings descending to scrutinize them: encouraged or chastened, all will stand in awe before the dread majesty of Heaven. Each proclamation of a command will be like wind and rain arriving at the proper time: stirred and inspired, all will yield as one to the circulation of divine vitality. It is like the celestial pivot revolving silently: the five planets, traversing their successive courses, move forward or backward, following their prescribed degrees and stations without deviation. With the scales and steelyard in our hands, the myriad things in all their complexity, whether high or low, light or heavy, submit to our adjustment and regulation and dare not resist. Thus, by holding comprehensive command of the sovereign’s guiding authority and directing the ordering of things [?], Your Majesty’s majestic commands and spiritual potency will equal the workings of creation, and all the teeming multitude of living beings will joyfully follow your wishes. We shall then see the hundred officials vying to lead wherever the sovereign’s mind inclines, and all officers exerting themselves wherever the One Man points. If a benefit concerns only oneself and is not for…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
君父也則不敢以私其身事在一家而非以
社稷也則不敢以私其家坐而論道者皆務調元
贊化之實而有虞庭師讓之風起而作事者
皆切奔走疏附之誠而有王人秉恤之義臺
諫之臣誠思匡弼而非徒炫直以沽名省寺
之臣誠竭賛襄而非徒虛張以飾聽位居藩
臬者竭力於旬宣而不負專城之托職司郡
邑者誠心於綏牧而足紓外顧之憂盖義以
維乎其恩則法行自近而
朝廷輦轂之下翕然成忠直之風威以克乎厥
===
愛則權不下移而邦國甸侯之間群然秉忠
藎之念由是而自上以達下自近以及遠辟
之手持而足行目視而耳聽莫不流貫於元
氣從令於天君而呼吸運動神化黙成有不
知其所以然者矣則夫儀刑觀感之際民之
同有是心者孰敢不回心而嚮化風行而草
偃也哉抑臣又有
獻焉
朝廷者風化之原也
心者運治之本也

朝廷者風化之原也

punctuated:
君父也，則不敢以私其身；事在一家而非以社稷也，則不敢以私其家。坐而論道者，皆務調元贊化之實，而有虞庭師讓之風；起而作事者，皆切奔走疏附之誠，而有王人秉恤之義。臺諫之臣，誠思匡弼，而非徒炫直以沽名；省寺之臣，誠竭賛襄，而非徒虛張以飾聽。位居藩臬者，竭力於旬宣，而不負專城之托；職司郡邑者，誠心於綏牧，而足紓外顧之憂。盖義以維乎其恩，則法行自近，而朝廷輦轂之下，翕然成忠直之風；威以克乎厥愛，則權不下移，而邦國甸侯之間，群然秉忠藎之念。由是而自上以達下，自近以及遠，辟之手持而足行，目視而耳聽，莫不流貫於元氣，從令於天君，而呼吸運動，神化黙成，有不知其所以然者矣。則夫儀刑觀感之際，民之同有是心者，孰敢不回心而嚮化，風行而草偃也哉？
抑臣又有獻焉：朝廷者，風化之原也；心者，運治之本也。
translation_en:
…their sovereign and father, they dare not pursue their own private interests; when a matter concerns their own family rather than the altars of soil and grain, they dare not pursue their family’s private interests. Those who sit and discuss the Way all strive for the actual achievement of harmonizing the primal forces and assisting the transforming work of Heaven and Earth, displaying the spirit of mutual deference among the officials at Shun’s court. Those who rise to undertake affairs are all earnest in hastening to serve and bringing the estranged into allegiance, displaying the dutiful solicitude of the king’s servants. Censors and remonstrance officials sincerely seek to correct and assist their ruler, rather than merely flaunting their forthrightness to purchase renown. Officials of the central departments and courts sincerely devote themselves to assisting him, rather than merely making empty displays to embellish what he hears. Those serving in the provincial administration and surveillance commissions exert themselves fully in disseminating imperial guidance, living up to the trust placed in them to govern their jurisdictions. Those responsible for prefectures and counties sincerely pacify and shepherd the people, sufficiently relieving the ruler’s concern for affairs beyond the court. For when righteousness regulates his graciousness, enforcement of the law begins with those nearest him, and a spirit of loyalty and uprightness arises in harmony throughout the court and capital. When authority restrains his affection, power does not pass into the hands of subordinates, and throughout the realm and its territories all cherish thoughts of devoted loyalty. Thus influence reaches from above to below and from near to far. It is like the hands grasping, the feet walking, the eyes seeing, and the ears hearing: all are permeated by the primal vital force and obey the commands of the mind, the lord of the body. Breathing and movement occur, and wondrous transformation is silently accomplished, without anyone knowing how it comes about. Then, as the people behold the exemplary model and are moved by it, sharing as they do this same moral mind, who would dare not turn their hearts toward transformation, bending like grass before the wind?
Yet your servant has a further proposal to offer: the court is the source of moral influence; the mind is the foundation for conducting government.

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
陛下欲使天下之作忠亦先之以訓臣而已爾欲
使臣民之式化亦本之以純心而已爾仰惟
陛下神明
天縱
聖學日新應帝王五百歲之昌期而
敬一發傳心之祕衍
祖宗億萬年之正曆而
綱維弘保治之規
禮樂明備而文明之化以宣
倫制兩全而太平之象以見蓋粹乎位斯道之
===
中而
建維皇之極者矣則夫化導臣民之機挽回風
化之本臣復何言也哉但臣聞之書曰慎厥
終惟其始蓋言天道順布于四時常運而不
息王者法天以行健純一而不已今
陛下剛健文明之德自昔有聞嚴恭寅畏之心於
今愈密固矣然一念之危微易汩而况
九重邃密之内天理之培養者甚難人心之出入
無時而况一日二日之間事幾之所關者有
萬向使作之以憂勤而或乘以一時之怠忽

無時而況一日二日之間事幾之所關者有
萬向使作之以憂勤而或乘以一時之怠惣
punctuated:
陛下欲使天下之作忠，亦先之以訓臣而已爾；欲使臣民之式化，亦本之以純心而已爾。仰惟陛下神明天縱，聖學日新，應帝王五百歲之昌期，而敬一發傳心之祕；衍祖宗億萬年之正曆，而綱維弘保治之規。禮樂明備，而文明之化以宣；倫制兩全，而太平之象以見。蓋粹乎位斯道之中，而建維皇之極者矣。則夫化導臣民之機、挽回風化之本，臣復何言也哉？

但臣聞之，《書》曰：「慎厥終，惟其始。」蓋言天道順布于四時，常運而不息；王者法天以行健，純一而不已。今陛下剛健文明之德，自昔有聞；嚴恭寅畏之心，於今愈密，固矣。然一念之危微易汩，而况九重邃密之内，天理之培養者甚難；人心之出入無時，而况一日二日之間，事幾之所關者有萬。向使作之以憂勤，而或乘以一時之怠忽，
translation_en:
If Your Majesty wishes to inspire loyalty throughout the realm, you need only begin by instructing your ministers; if you wish your ministers and people to follow your transforming influence, you need only make purity of heart its foundation. Looking reverently upward, I reflect that Your Majesty’s spiritual illumination is Heaven-endowed and your sagely learning advances daily. Answering the auspicious occasion for an emperor or king that comes once in five hundred years, through reverent oneness you reveal the secret of transmitting the heart’s teaching. Extending the legitimate succession of your ancestors for countless millions of years, through the guiding bonds you enlarge the principles for preserving good government. Rites and music are clearly established and complete, spreading the transforming influence of cultured enlightenment; human relationships and institutions are both perfected, displaying the signs of great peace. Indeed, you dwell with purity at the center of this Way [?] and establish the sovereign’s supreme standard. What more, then, can your servant say about the means of transforming and guiding ministers and people, or the foundation for restoring moral influence?

Yet your servant has heard the Documents say: “Be mindful of the end, as of the beginning.” This means that Heaven’s Way unfolds in due order through the four seasons, constantly moving without rest; the king models himself on Heaven in acting with vigor, remaining wholly single-minded without cease. Now Your Majesty’s virtues of strength, vigor, and cultured enlightenment have long been renowned, while your solemn reverence and vigilant awe have become still more assiduous today: this is assuredly so. Yet the precarious and subtle workings of a single thought are easily obscured; how much more difficult it is to nurture heavenly principle within the secluded depths of the palace. The human mind comes and goes at no fixed time; moreover, within a day or two, the incipient affairs demanding attention number ten thousand. If, having begun with anxious diligence, one should allow a moment of indolence and negligence to intrude…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
出之以誠篤而或雜以一息之虛文則本原
之地未免間隔而未融大化之行必有壅遏
而弗達者矣臣願
陛下終始惟一而不雜於二三動靜有常而無時
乎豫怠防閑於
深宮獨行之際而端莊靜一以凝其真致謹於
燕閒清暇之時而縝密緝熈以聯其間將使一
心之中虛靈洞徹感通之際誠意交流以此
照臨百官如懸鑑以待妍媸而忠邪之分自
別以此賞罰天下如執度以齊長短而勸懲
===
之道自明則
聖德已至而益至
治道已隆而益隆
紀綱已振而益振風俗已淳而益淳觀化在
朝而百工庶職莫敢不一於忠矣觀俗在野而
海隅蒼生莫敢不讓於忠矣有醇朴不漓之
意而典章經制之備曠三代而獨隆當文明
大著之時而惇龐渾噩之風追隆古而僅見
由是而天時人事交相契合治運氣化交相
流通馨香感格於

translation_en:
…and if what issues forth in sincerity and earnestness should be mingled with even a moment’s empty formalism, then the very source would inevitably suffer interruptions and fail to become fully integrated; the operation of your great transforming influence would surely encounter obstructions and fail to reach everywhere. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would remain single-minded from beginning to end, without divided or wavering purposes, and maintain constancy in activity and repose, never lapsing into indolence. Guard yourself when acting alone within the secluded palace, and through dignified composure and inward stillness and unity consolidate your genuine nature. Exercise care in moments of private leisure, and through meticulous attention and sustained cultivation of enlightenment maintain continuity without a break. Thus your mind will become receptive, numinously aware, and thoroughly lucid; in its responsive communion with things, sincerity will flow freely in both directions.
With this, oversee the officials as though suspending a mirror before beauty and ugliness: the distinction between loyalty and perversity will become apparent of itself. With this, reward and punish throughout the realm as though applying a measure to determine length: the way to encourage and chastise will become clear of itself. Then your sagely virtue, already consummate, will become still more consummate; the way of governance, already flourishing, will flourish still further; governing principles and discipline, already invigorated, will gain still greater vigor; and customs, already pure, will become still purer. Those at court will observe your transforming influence, and none among the many officials and functionaries will dare be other than single-minded in loyalty. Those outside the court will observe prevailing customs, and none among the common people, even at the sea’s farthest shores, will dare fail to show deference in loyalty [?].
An unadulterated spirit of simplicity will prevail, while the completeness of statutes, institutions, and established systems will attain a distinction unrivaled since the Three Dynasties. At a time when civilized accomplishment shines forth, a spirit of generous simplicity and uncontrived innocence will appear, scarcely seen since high antiquity. Through this, Heaven’s seasons and human affairs will accord with one another, while the course of governance and the transformations of vital energy will flow in mutual communion. The sweet fragrance of virtue will move and reach …

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
神明而諸福駢臻協氣上通於
皇穹而百嘉鬯遂
天德孚而王道成
天心享而至治永億萬年無疆之休端在是矣此
端本澄源之道臣愚之所拳拳效忠者也惟
陛下留神採納天下幸甚臣愚幸甚臣不識忌諱
干冒
天威不勝戰慄隕越之至臣謹對

punctuated: 神明，而諸福駢臻；協氣上通於皇穹，而百嘉鬯遂。天德孚而王道成，天心享而至治永，億萬年無疆之休端在是矣。此端本澄源之道，臣愚之所拳拳效忠者也。惟陛下留神採納，天下幸甚，臣愚幸甚。臣不識忌諱，干冒天威，不勝戰慄隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: …the spirits, and manifold blessings arrive together; harmonious vital energy reaches upward to august Heaven, and all auspicious things flourish and attain fulfillment. Heaven’s virtue inspires trust, and the Kingly Way is realized; Heaven’s heart is pleased, and consummate governance endures. Boundless blessings for countless millions of years lie precisely in this. This way of setting the root aright and clearing the source is what your foolish servant earnestly offers in loyal service. May Your Majesty give it attentive consideration and adopt it: all under Heaven would be most fortunate, and your foolish servant most fortunate. Your servant, ignorant of what must not be spoken, has presumed to offend your heavenly majesty. I am overcome with trembling fear and the utmost dread of falling into disgrace. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
臣李自華
臣對臣聞帝王之御天下也必民俗之歸於
厚而後可以稱化中之治必人臣之實其心
而後可以成化民之功何則臣者民之倡也
民者國之本也國以民為本民俗之淳漓國
治之盛衰係焉民以臣為倡臣道之誠偽民
俗之淳漓關焉故為臣者之居於位也有真
德實意以施之化理之間而不假外務以狥
人不飾虛名以竊禄存之有實心行之有實
政成之有實功矣夫然後為民者之居於下
===
也皆至情聯屬而日趨於淳厚之化上不務
外而下亦非徒外感上不狥名而下亦不以
名應所蒙者有實惠所尚者有實德所用者
有實情矣甚矣臣民之相為聯屬而為臣者
之責為甚重也夫苟不知其責之重而罔勵

臣對臣聞帝王之御天下也必民俗之歸於
厚而後可以稱化中之治必人臣之實其心

也皆至情聯屬而日趨於淳厚之化上不務
外而下亦非徒外感上不狥名而下亦不以
名應所蒙者有實惠所尚者有實德所用者

又何以成治化之隆又何以副君上之心哉
punctuated:
臣李自華。

臣對：臣聞帝王之御天下也，必民俗之歸於厚，而後可以稱化中之治；必人臣之實其心，而後可以成化民之功。何則？臣者，民之倡也；民者，國之本也。國以民為本，民俗之淳漓，國治之盛衰係焉；民以臣為倡，臣道之誠偽，民俗之淳漓關焉。故為臣者之居於位也，有真德實意以施之化理之間，而不假外務以狥人，不飾虛名以竊禄，存之有實心，行之有實政，成之有實功矣。夫然後為民者之居於下也，皆至情聯屬，而日趨於淳厚之化。上不務外，而下亦非徒外感；上不狥名，而下亦不以名應。所蒙者有實惠，所尚者有實德，所用者有實情矣。甚矣，臣民之相為聯屬，而為臣者之責為甚重也！夫苟不知其責之重，而罔勵其心之實，則是為煌煌眩美之術，而無肫肫厚下之仁；為庸庸苟禄之謀，而無蹇蹇匪躬之節。由是虛偽成風，淳朴盡散，而凡上下之間，率皆以文相徵逐，而忠實蕩乎其無存矣。又何以成治化之隆？又何以副君上之心哉？
translation_en:
Your servant Li Zihua.

Your servant replies: I have heard that when emperors and kings govern the realm, only after the people's customs have become generous and sincere can their rule be called government through moral transformation [?]; only after their ministers make their hearts sincere can the work of transforming the people be accomplished. Why is this? Ministers are the people's exemplars, and the people are the foundation of the state. Since the state takes the people as its foundation, the flourishing or decline of its government depends on the integrity or degeneration of popular customs. Since the people take ministers as their exemplars, the integrity or degeneration of popular customs depends on whether ministers act sincerely or falsely. Thus ministers who hold office must bring genuine virtue and earnest intent to the work of moral transformation and government. They must neither use outward activities to please others nor embellish empty reputations to obtain salaries illicitly. What they harbor will then be sincere hearts; what they carry out, substantive policies; and what they accomplish, genuine achievements. Only then will the people below all be bound together by the deepest feelings and advance daily toward generous and sincere customs. When those above do not pursue outward appearances, those below will likewise be moved beyond mere appearances. When those above do not pursue reputation, those below will likewise respond with more than reputation alone. The benefits they receive will be tangible; the virtue they esteem will be genuine; and the feelings on which they act will be sincere. How closely ministers and people are bound together, and how exceedingly weighty is the responsibility of ministers!

If ministers fail to understand the gravity of their responsibility and do not strive to make their hearts sincere, they merely practice arts of dazzling display, without the earnest benevolence that generously nurtures those below. They merely devise commonplace schemes to secure their salaries, without the integrity of steadfast service that puts self aside. Consequently, falsehood becomes customary and simple integrity vanishes altogether. In all dealings between those above and those below, everyone pursues and solicits others through outward forms, while loyalty and sincerity are swept away without a trace. How, then, can they bring government and moral transformation to flourishing fulfillment? How can they satisfy their sovereign's intentions?

translation_en:
Thus, if we wish to make the people esteem sincerity and restore the ancient way of government, we must seek the means nowhere else. In examining the root, we must certainly value policies that demand substantive results; in considering how their influence works, we must also understand the workings of moral guidance. To possess this intention inwardly and carry it into action outwardly constitutes government that demands substance. For the wind to blow above and the grass to bend below illustrates how moral guidance works. If these policies are implemented and these workings understood, and if assessments are discerning and distinctions of merit appropriately made, everyone will seek to reject superficiality and honor substance, to reduce ornament and practice sincerity. Frivolous and corrupt customs can then be wholly reversed, and the simple spirit of antiquity fully restored. Such government may rank with that of the sage emperors and enlightened kings.
I reverently reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor has received the register of Heaven’s mandate in accordance with Heaven, holds the tally of authority, and presides over the destined age. With utmost sincerity you offer sacrifice to the Lord on High; with reverent self-possession you govern the people. The order of authority is correct and its governing principles are maintained with clarity; commands are strict, and rewards and punishments unfailingly trustworthy. Throughout all beneath Heaven, everyone is moved to gratitude and eager to exert himself, inspired and glad to obey. Your ignorant servant, living obscurely among the common people, has long wished to witness the fulfillment of your moral transformation. Recently, through the undeserved recommendation of the responsible officials, I have been able to join those answering in the great court. Your sagely questions speak earnestly of achieving good government. You wish your servants to honor sincerity of heart and carry out substantive deeds, to eliminate falsehood and give their utmost in loyalty and goodness, thereby setting a correct standard for the people below and bringing simplicity and generosity to their customs. Your ignorant servant has indeed thereby been able reverently to glimpse…

皇上之至意矣敢不披瀝愚衷以對先儒張栻有
曰廷對最是直言盖士人初見
君父此是第一步此時可欺則無往而非欺矣臣
愚雖無知識誠不敢欺也嘗聞之書曰股肱
良哉庶事康哉盖言君之致治必得臣以理
庶政而後可以成化於天下也又曰惟臣欽
若惟民從乂盖言臣之於民其相須為甚殷
而化導為甚切也為君者知治之有賴於臣
故秩之以位而委任之必專隆之以恩而禮
遇之必至申之以令而戒諭之必明是非自

punctuated:
皇上之至意矣。敢不披瀝愚衷以對？先儒張栻有曰：「廷對最是直言，盖士人初見君父，此是第一步。此時可欺，則無往而非欺矣。」臣愚雖無知識，誠不敢欺也。嘗聞之，《書》曰：「股肱良哉，庶事康哉。」盖言君之致治，必得臣以理庶政，而後可以成化於天下也。又曰：「惟臣欽若，惟民從乂。」盖言臣之於民，其相須為甚殷，而化導為甚切也。

為君者知治之有賴於臣，故秩之以位，而委任之必專；隆之以恩，而禮遇之必至；申之以令，而戒諭之必明。是非自處於逸而遺臣以勞也。盖君猶天也，百司庶府猶四時五行也。天不言，而四時五行各宣其氣，以化生乎萬物；君無為，而百司庶府各效其職，以奠安乎萬民。其道一也。

為臣者知職之甚切於民，故帥之以正，而不敢為詭道之趨；輸之以誠，而不務為聲譽之美；要之以久，而不徒為旦夕之効。是非不知自逸而顧為是勞也。盖臣之職在於導民，猶之盂也；民之責在於從上，猶之水也。盂圓則水随以圓，盂方則水随以方。臣盡忠，而民亦尚忠；臣營
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s deepest intent. How could I dare not lay bare my humble heart in reply? The earlier Confucian scholar Zhang Shi said: “In answering at court, forthright speech matters above all. When a scholar first appears before his ruler and father, this is his first step. If he can deceive at this moment, there will be no occasion on which he will not deceive.” Though your foolish servant lacks understanding, I truly dare not deceive. I have heard these words from the Book of Documents: “When the limbs are good, all affairs prosper.” This means that, to achieve good government, a ruler must obtain ministers to administer the various affairs of government; only then can he bring about the moral transformation of all under Heaven. It also says: “When ministers reverently comply, the people follow and are well governed.” This means that ministers and the people depend profoundly upon one another, and that transforming and guiding the people is an especially pressing duty.

Knowing that good government depends upon ministers, the ruler assigns them ranked positions and entrusts them fully with their responsibilities; he exalts them with favor and treats them with the utmost courtesy; he reiterates his commands and makes his admonitions clear. This is not to place himself at ease and leave his ministers to toil. For the ruler is like Heaven, and the various offices and bureaus are like the four seasons and the five phases. Heaven does not speak, yet the four seasons and five phases each give forth their vital energies to transform and bring forth the myriad things. The ruler acts without contrivance, yet the various offices and bureaus each discharge their duties to secure the peace of the myriad people. The principle is the same.

Knowing how closely their duties concern the people, ministers lead them with rectitude and dare not pursue devious courses; they offer their sincerity and do not strive merely for a fine reputation; they seek enduring results and do not work merely for effects achieved overnight. It is not that they do not know how to enjoy ease themselves, yet choose instead to undertake this toil. Rather, a minister’s duty is to guide the people: he is like a basin. The people’s responsibility is to follow those above them: they are like water. If the basin is round, the water follows its round shape; if the basin is square, the water follows its square shape. When ministers are wholly loyal, the people likewise esteem loyalty; when ministers pursue…

text:
僞而民亦用僞其機同也甞觀之司馬光曰
天下之治本乎理而風俗之善係於習及其
風俗旣失流弊旣成則雖智辯不易諭也強
毅不能制也重賞不能勸也嚴刑不能止也
自非聖人得位而臨之任賢臣而化導之積
百年之功弗能變也朱熹曰百工之釐庶事
之所以康也世道之泰國脉之所以堅也必
人臣有法守而後朝廷有紀綱朝廷有紀綱
而後天下有風俗然則人臣者非君之所賴
以圖治民之所望以觀法而風化之所由以
===
出者乎考之上古治莫盛於唐虞而臣之有
實忠者亦莫過於唐虞故當時民俗之隆但
見其渾渾爾噩噩爾太朴未漓純一未散固
不知所謂忠也而况於文乎迨夫有夏氏興
而因時立政於是始以忠爲尚矣忠可尚也
而後之不善用其忠者不免流於野故殷之
興也易之以質質可尚也而後之不善用其
質者未免流於鬼故周之興也易之以文是
皆古之聖人隨時變易以從道所謂與民宜
之者也而要之夏商之忠質非無文也文實

punctuated:
僞，而民亦用僞，其機同也。甞觀之，司馬光曰：「天下之治本乎理，而風俗之善係於習。及其風俗旣失，流弊旣成，則雖智辯不易諭也，強毅不能制也，重賞不能勸也，嚴刑不能止也。自非聖人得位而臨之，任賢臣而化導之，積百年之功，弗能變也。」朱熹曰：「百工之釐，庶事之所以康也；世道之泰，國脉之所以堅也。必人臣有法守，而後朝廷有紀綱；朝廷有紀綱，而後天下有風俗。」然則人臣者，非君之所賴以圖治、民之所望以觀法，而風化之所由以出者乎？

考之上古，治莫盛於唐虞，而臣之有實忠者亦莫過於唐虞。故當時民俗之隆，但見其渾渾爾、噩噩爾，太朴未漓，純一未散，固不知所謂忠也，而况於文乎？迨夫有夏氏興，而因時立政，於是始以忠爲尚矣。忠可尚也，而後之不善用其忠者，不免流於野。故殷之興也，易之以質。質可尚也，而後之不善用其質者，未免流於鬼。故周之興也，易之以文。是皆古之聖人隨時變易以從道，所謂與民宜之者也。而要之，夏商之忠質非無文也，文實
translation_en:
…practice deceit, and the people likewise employ deceit: the mechanism is the same. I have considered this. Sima Guang said: “Order throughout the realm is rooted in principle, while the goodness of customs depends upon habituation. Once customs have gone astray and harmful tendencies have become established, even the wise and eloquent cannot readily bring people to understand; the strong and resolute cannot restrain them; lavish rewards cannot encourage them; and severe punishments cannot stop them. Unless a sage gains the throne and presides over them, appoints worthy ministers to transform and guide them, and accumulates a hundred years of effort, these customs cannot be changed.” Zhu Xi said: “The orderly discharge of duties by all officials is what brings the many affairs of government into good order; the flourishing of the moral order is what secures the vitality of the state. Only when ministers uphold established standards can the court possess governing discipline; only when the court possesses governing discipline can the realm possess sound customs.” Are ministers, then, not those upon whom the ruler relies to achieve good government, to whom the people look for models to follow, and from whom moral transformation proceeds?

Examining high antiquity, no government flourished more than that of Tang and Yu, and no ministers surpassed those of Tang and Yu in genuine loyalty. Thus, at the height of popular virtue in those times, one saw only an unspoiled wholeness and unaffected simplicity: primal simplicity had not been diluted, nor had pure unity been dispersed. People did not even know what was called loyalty, much less cultural refinement. When the Xia dynasty arose, it established government suited to its times, and only then did loyalty become the quality most esteemed. Loyalty deserved esteem, but those in later times who failed to employ it well inevitably lapsed into rustic coarseness. Thus, when Yin arose, it replaced loyalty with plain substance. Plain substance deserved esteem, but those in later times who failed to employ it well inevitably lapsed into preoccupation with spirits. Thus, when Zhou arose, it replaced plain substance with cultural refinement. In all these cases, the ancient sages changed with the times in order to follow the Way: this is what is meant by making things appropriate for the people. Yet, fundamentally, the loyalty and plain substance of Xia and Shang were not without refinement. Refinement in fact …

行於忠質之內周之文非無忠與質也忠質
實寓於文之中此古今稱盛治者必言唐虞
言三代也然而所以致此者豈堯舜禹湯文
武之聖獨勞於上哉實以當時之在位者九
官師師五臣濟美六德允讓四哲登庸上體
君心以行實政下端民表以敷實化故隨其
所尚而有實功耳自
今日言之我
皇上壽考作人久道成化推心以置人心腹開誠
以任使臣僚殆與唐虞三代之世所以待其

報

自今日言之，我皇上壽考作人，久道成化，推心以置人心腹，開誠以任使臣僚，殆與唐虞三代之世所以待其臣者比隆矣。故一時臣子咸思奮勵，以盡忠報國，以輔理成化，以致民俗雍熈之治，以追唐虞三代之隆，臣固樂觀其盛者也。然而人心不同，智愚相越，則有不可一律齊者。故大而論道於密勿，小而任事於郎署，內而保乂乎黎庶，外而防禦乎疆圉，其受職者非一人也。其間脩政者，能建保邦之業，上希伊傅之惇德允元者有之矣，寧無徒美觀聽而侈文為以示經綸者乎？獻議者，能效濟時之猷，遠宗周
translation_en:
…operates within loyalty and substance. Nor was the cultural refinement of Zhou devoid of loyalty and substance: loyalty and substance were truly embodied within it. This is why those who speak of flourishing government, past or present, invariably invoke Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Yet was this achieved solely through the labors of such sages as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu at the summit? It was indeed because those then holding office—the nine officials who learned from one another, the five ministers who furthered one another’s excellence, the six virtuous men who sincerely yielded precedence, and the four worthies raised to service—embodied their sovereign’s intentions above and carried out substantive government, while below they set upright examples for the people and spread genuine moral transformation. Thus, whatever quality their age esteemed, they achieved substantial results.
Speaking of the present day, our Emperor, blessed with longevity, nurtures men of talent; through long perseverance in the Way, he brings moral transformation to fruition. He gives others his whole heart and treats them as trusted confidants, employing his ministers with complete sincerity. This surely rivals the greatness with which rulers treated their ministers in the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Thus all his servants today aspire to exert themselves, to repay the state with utmost loyalty, to assist its governance and accomplish moral transformation, to bring about harmonious and prosperous customs among the people, and to match the flourishing rule of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Your servant certainly delights in witnessing this greatness. Yet people’s hearts differ, and their wisdom and folly vary greatly; they cannot all be brought into conformity with a single standard. Whether in high office discussing the Way in confidential deliberations, or in lesser office handling affairs in the bureaux; whether securing and governing the common people within, or defending the frontiers without—many different men bear these responsibilities. Among those attending to government, there are indeed men capable of establishing achievements that preserve the state, aspiring to the earnest virtue and genuine goodness of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. Yet are there none who merely make a fine impression on the eyes and ears, indulging in elaborate formalities to display their supposed capacity for ordering the realm? Among those submitting proposals, there are men capable of offering plans that meet the needs of the age, taking as their distant exemplar the Duke of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
召之陳風納德者有之矣寧無徒工詞說而
繁簡牘以沽忠直者乎愛民而有一體之心
如泂酌所謂豈弟君子民之父母固多見於
世也而其口與心違徒飾甘言以愚弄斯民
者豈盡無乎任事而有特立之操如南山所
謂樂只君子邦家之基固恒有於朝也而其
色厲內荏徒張虛聲以欺罔天下者豈絕無
乎致身之義習聞於子夏人臣非不知也而
一臨利害輒為規避倖免之計如諸葛亮之
鞠躬盡瘁富弼之大節難奪者果多其人與
===
慎獨之訓相傳於子思人臣非不知也而一
至隱微輒為苟且放縱之非如楊震之暮夜
却金趙抃之焚香夜告者果多其人與此固
聖心之所洞察而形之
聖問者甚詳且切也夫我
皇上始焉
申務實之令以告戒臣工真如風雷之鼓舞震
懾肅然其甚嚴也而諸臣顧不能相砥礪輸
忠悃既有負於
聖教之切繼焉

translation_en:
…Shao in presenting admonitions and guiding their ruler toward virtue: such men do exist. Yet are there none who merely polish their rhetoric and multiply documents to purchase a reputation for loyalty and candor? Those who love the people and regard themselves as one body with them—as expressed in Drawing Water from Afar (Jiong Zhuo), “The gracious and gentle gentleman is the father and mother of the people”—are indeed often seen in the world. Yet are there truly none whose words contradict their hearts, who merely embellish sweet phrases to fool these people? Those who undertake their duties with integrity that stands firm and independent—as expressed in Southern Mountain (Nan Shan), “The joyous gentleman is the foundation of the state”—are indeed regularly found at court. Yet are there absolutely none who appear stern but are weak within, merely putting on an empty show to deceive all under Heaven? Ministers are not ignorant of the duty to devote their lives to their ruler, a teaching long familiar from Zixia. Yet whenever confronted with personal advantage or harm, they devise ways to evade their responsibilities and escape unscathed. Are there truly many like Zhuge Liang, who bent himself to his duties and exhausted his strength, or Fu Bi, whose integrity in great matters could not be shaken? Ministers are not ignorant of the injunction to be watchful over oneself when alone, handed down from Zisi. Yet whenever they enter the realm of the hidden and imperceptible, they lapse into careless self-indulgence. Are there truly many like Yang Zhen, who refused gold offered at night, or Zhao Bian, who burned incense and reported his conduct to Heaven each night? These are matters that Your Majesty’s sagely mind has thoroughly discerned and expressed in the imperial examination question with great detail and urgency.

At the outset, Our Emperor reiterated the command to attend to substantive achievement, admonishing his officials. Like wind and thunder stirring and striking awe into all, it was solemn and exceedingly stern. Yet the ministers failed to encourage one another toward improvement and offer their heartfelt loyalty, thus already falling short of the earnest imperial instruction. Subsequently …

text:
出智臨之哲以稽考臣工又若日月之容光必
照灼然其甚明也而諸臣竟不能為文飾為
廋匿無所逃於
聖鑒之精是諸臣者亦何樂而為此也蓋
陛下之心以一家視天下而在下之臣或各自有
其家
陛下之心以一身視中國而在下之臣或各自有
其身惟身家之念一萌於中故矯飾之私遂
肆於外其流之弊不特仰焉無以副
聖天子屬望之心而以此居導民之任其所以不
===
能成忠厚之俗者未必非斯人之故矣何也
蓋使其以誠而臨民也則民亦以誠應之而
篤實之風興焉書之所謂協衷詩之所謂日
用飲食者日漸漬焉而不自知矣使其以偽
而臨民也則民亦以偽應之而詭譎之風興
焉書之所謂滅義記之所謂誣上行私者不
將日淪溺焉而罔自覺乎信乎孫洙之言曰
在朝有羔羊之節而後在野有蟋蟀之勤在
上有薈蔚之風而後在下有蜉蝣之習蓋言
民之必從乎上而臣之當慎所感也今之時

何也？蓋使其以誠而臨民也，則民亦以誠應之，而篤實之風興焉。《書》之所謂協衷，《詩》之所謂日用飲食者，日漸漬焉而不自知矣。使其以偽而臨民也，則民亦以偽應之，而詭譎之風興焉。《書》之所謂滅義，《記》之所謂誣上行私者，不將日淪溺焉而罔自覺乎？信乎孫洙之言曰：「在朝有羔羊之節，而後在野有蟋蟀之勤；在上有薈蔚之風，而後在下有蜉蝣之習。」蓋言民之必從乎上，而臣之當慎所感也。今之時
translation_en:
…you brought forth the wisdom of discerning oversight to scrutinize your officials. Like the sun and moon, whose light reaches even the smallest openings, your discernment was brilliantly clear. In the end, your ministers could neither disguise nor conceal their conduct: nothing could escape your penetrating imperial scrutiny. What pleasure, then, could these ministers take in behaving this way? Your Majesty regards all under Heaven as one family, yet some ministers below you each regard their own family as a separate concern. Your Majesty regards the Central Kingdom as one body, yet some ministers below you each regard their own person as a separate concern. Once concern for self and family sprouts within, selfish impulses toward deception and embellishment run unchecked without. The resulting harm is not merely that they fail to fulfill the expectations of the sagely Son of Heaven above them. When such men occupy positions responsible for guiding the people, the failure to establish customs of loyalty and generosity may well be their doing.

Why is this? If they govern the people with sincerity, the people will respond with sincerity, and a spirit of earnest integrity will arise. What the Book of Documents calls “harmony with the proper mean,” and what the Book of Odes describes as “daily eating and drinking,” will gradually permeate the people's lives without their knowing it. If officials govern the people with deceit, however, the people will respond with deceit, and a spirit of cunning will arise. Will they not then sink daily, without awareness, into what the Book of Documents calls “destroying righteousness” and what the Book of Rites calls “deceiving superiors and pursuing private interests”? How true are Sun Zhu's words: “Only when those at court possess the integrity of ‘Lamb's Wool’ will those in the countryside display the diligence of ‘The Cricket’; when those above exhibit the temper of ‘Gathering Clouds,’ those below will acquire the habits of ‘The Mayfly.’” His point is that the people inevitably follow those above them, and ministers must therefore take care over the influence they exert. In the present age…

text:
民俗之弊也極矣直道而行其良心之素具
者雖與三代之民不殊而習俗易移其流風
之漸被者雖賢者亦不能自免間有甚者吾
見其忠實盡廢而薄劣成風要不止於文勝
而已也愈趨愈下誠有如
聖制所云者兹欲障百川而之東迴狂瀾於既倒
挽頹敗之俗而振敦朴之風則凡我諸臣居
導民之位者可不思所以盡其責乎是故善
醫者不視人之肥瘠察脉之病否而已善計
天下者不視天下之安危察民俗之純偽而
===
已苟在内服之臣而能以
聖天子之心為心則尚忠之風行於畿甸安知無

廷尉省刑具者乎所謂大臣法小臣廉而朝
無比德斯成其為淳龐之政也苟在外服之
臣而能以

而民不事淫祠者乎所謂上有好者下必甚

punctuated:
民俗之弊也極矣！直道而行，其良心之素具者，雖與三代之民不殊，而習俗易移，其流風之漸被者，雖賢者亦不能自免。間有甚者，吾見其忠實盡廢而薄劣成風，要不止於文勝而已也。愈趨愈下，誠有如聖制所云者。兹欲障百川而之東，迴狂瀾於既倒，挽頹敗之俗而振敦朴之風，則凡我諸臣居導民之位者，可不思所以盡其責乎？是故善醫者，不視人之肥瘠，察脉之病否而已；善計天下者，不視天下之安危，察民俗之純偽而已。
苟在内服之臣而能以聖天子之心為心，則尚忠之風行於畿甸，安知無楊綰執政而京兆減騶從者乎？魏相當國而廷尉省刑具者乎？所謂大臣法，小臣廉，而朝無比德，斯成其為淳龐之政也。苟在外服之臣而能以聖天子之心為心，則尚忠之風行於邦國，安知無李膺按河東而民不忍欺者乎？朱熹知漳州而民不事淫祠者乎？所謂上有好者，下必甚焉，而野無淫朋，斯成其為淳龐之俗也。政美
translation_en:
…the corruption of popular customs has reached its utmost extreme! In their innate possession of a good conscience, which leads them to act uprightly, the people are no different from those of the Three Dynasties. Yet customary practices readily transform them, and even the worthy cannot escape the gradual influence of prevailing habits. In some especially grave instances, I see sincerity and honesty wholly abandoned, while frivolity and baseness become fashionable. This is certainly more than a matter of outward refinement prevailing over substance. The decline grows ever worse, just as Your Majesty’s sagely decree states. If we now wish to dam the hundred rivers and direct them eastward, turn back the raging waters already pouring forth, rescue deteriorating customs, and revive a spirit of integrity and simplicity, can any of us officials charged with guiding the people fail to consider how to discharge our responsibilities fully? Thus, a skilled physician does not judge people by their stoutness or thinness, but simply examines their pulse for illness. Likewise, one skilled in planning for the realm does not judge it by its apparent security or peril, but simply examines whether popular customs are sincere or false.
If officials serving at court can take the sagely Son of Heaven’s heart as their own, a spirit of valuing sincerity will spread throughout the capital region. How do we know there will not again be cases like that of Yang Wan, under whose administration the Metropolitan Governor reduced his mounted attendants, or Wei Xiang, under whose leadership the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement reduced the instruments of punishment? As the saying goes, “The great ministers observe the law, and the lesser ministers are incorruptible”; with no collusion in wrongdoing at court, government of genuine integrity and substance will thereby be achieved. If officials serving outside the capital can take the sagely Son of Heaven’s heart as their own, a spirit of valuing sincerity will spread throughout the realm. How do we know there will not again be cases like that of Li Ying, when he inspected Hedong and the people could not bear to deceive him, or Zhu Xi, when he served as Prefect of Zhangzhou and the people ceased to worship at unauthorized shrines? As the saying goes, “Whatever those above favor, those below will pursue still more intensely”; with no pernicious cliques among the people, customs of genuine integrity and substance will thereby be established. With government excellent…

text:

盛時雍迓衡之治也哉顧今内外諸臣或不
能盡實其心則已且未忠也而何以作民之
忠無惑乎民俗之愈趨於偽也臣愚仰承
明問而欲効一得之愚以飭臣工以風民俗則有
三言焉
陛下陳之曰賞罰也考課也教化也臣竊觀
陛下之待臣庶有一可用之才未嘗不錄有一干
法之吏未嘗不斥甚者微勞可紀而賚賞即
為之優渥罪惡既著而誅戮遂有所不免賞
===
罰亦既行矣臣愚則以有司奉行之未善則
賞罰之間不有拘於常格而不能超拔以激
勵人心者乎誠於審察之下知其人之果有
異能也則不特賞之而已而必加以不次之
榮如黃潁川政事大治而徵為太子太傅可
也知其人之果有隱惡也則不但罰之而已
而必加以不測之辱如阿大夫譽言日至而

罰之然賞一人而天下莫不勸罰一人而天
下莫不懲要皆以忠自勉而以偽為戒矣朱

…above, and customs are sound below, what could still be lacking for achieving enduring prosperity in harmony and peace, and a government that brings the age into concord and welcomes equilibrium? It is no wonder that popular customs tend increasingly toward deceit. Humbly receiving Your Majesty’s enlightened question, I wish to offer my one modest insight toward bringing officials into order and transforming popular customs. I have three points to lay before Your Majesty [?]: rewards and punishments, performance evaluations, and moral instruction.
I observe that, in Your Majesty’s treatment of officials and commoners, whenever someone has a useful talent, you invariably employ him; whenever an official violates the law, you invariably dismiss him. Indeed, even a small service worthy of record receives generous rewards, while those whose crimes have become manifest cannot escape execution. Rewards and punishments have thus already been put into effect. Yet I humbly believe that the responsible authorities have not implemented them well. In administering rewards and punishments, are there not instances in which they cling to routine rules and fail to make exceptional promotions that would inspire people? If careful investigation establishes that someone truly possesses extraordinary ability, he should not merely be rewarded, but must receive the honor of promotion outside the regular order. One may follow the example of Huang of Yingchuan, whose outstanding administration led to his being summoned to serve as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent. If someone is found truly to harbor concealed wickedness, he should not merely be punished, but must receive disgrace beyond what he could have anticipated. One may follow the example of the Grand Master of A, who, despite praise arriving daily on his behalf, did not escape public execution. Although it is impossible to reward or punish every individual in this way, when one person is rewarded, everyone under Heaven is encouraged; when one person is punished, everyone under Heaven is admonished. All will thus strive to be loyal and guard against deceit. Zhu …

…Master Zhu said: “If the ruler conducts himself with reverence above and casts his discerning gaze over all under Heaven, invariably rewarding those with merit and punishing those with guilt, people will each exert themselves and encourage one another to abandon evil and follow goodness. The prevailing practices of ritual propriety and righteousness, integrity and a sense of shame will then undergo a great transformation.” This is precisely what is meant.
In the laws and regulations established by Your Majesty, prefectures and counties submit periodic reports on the worthiness or unworthiness of officials to the surveillance authorities, who forward reports to the provincial administrations and censorial offices. Every third year, an evaluation is conducted under the direction of the Ministry of Personnel, with scrutiny by the censorial and remonstrance officials. The judgments of many are combined to distinguish the lowest and highest performers and determine demotions and promotions. In more serious cases, imperial edicts are issued from time to time, setting aside ordinary procedures to conduct a comprehensive review of officials’ administration and dismiss those found wanting. Official evaluation is thus already strict. Yet your foolish servant believes that the responsible authorities have not fully carried out these provisions. When evaluations take place, might there not be those who follow the traces recorded in registers and documents without actually verifying the facts?
If, during an investigation, someone is said to be worthy and capable, one must thoroughly examine what makes him so. Those outstanding in filial conduct and integrity, whose aspirations and conduct rise above the ordinary, should be honored; those adept at ingratiating themselves, who oppress the people to gratify themselves, should not receive such recognition. If someone is said to be negligent and remiss, one must thoroughly examine what makes him so. Those who are unrestrained in corruption, neglect timely duties, and mishandle affairs should be dismissed; those who are sincere and unadorned, frugal and plain, simple and restrained, should not be removed. 人言而必考其心術之微則真才可得而用
智者不售其欺矣正此之謂也至於教化也
者尤為圖治之要機而不可一日不講者也

臣况我
皇上躬行仁孝

既行矣然而文華日勝實學漸漓士習之壞
實有可慨進身庠序之時即以富貴功名為
===
念則登名仕籍之日焉能有忠君愛國之心
是當申飭學校之官文藝固有可取矣而德
行之優長者尤必特為甄録明經固有足嘉
矣而節義之是尚者尤必特致褒崇夫如是
則人皆敦本而抑末尚忠而戒偽矣羅仲素

風俗者天下之大事朝廷有教化則士人有
廉耻士人有廉耻則天下有風俗正此之謂
也夫是賞罰也考課也教化也三者皆大務
也教化行於未仕之先所以培養其忠實之

As for moral instruction, it is especially crucial to achieving good government and must not be neglected for even a single day. Moreover, our Emperor personally practices benevolence and filial piety, his heart wholly devoted to reverence and singleness of purpose. Yet literary ornament grows daily more prevalent, while substantive learning gradually declines. The deterioration of scholars’ habits is truly lamentable. Officials responsible for schools should therefore be admonished anew. Literary skill certainly has its merits, but those outstanding in virtuous conduct must especially be singled out for selection. In this way, everyone will strengthen what is fundamental and restrain what is secondary, esteem loyalty and guard against falsehood. text:
本名實賞罰行於既仕之後所以益端其忠
實之趨如是而有不盡忠以事上務實以導
民者臣知其必無矣况
聖天子篤恭以刑百辟賢宰執敦信以佐萬幾則
賈誼之四維陸贄之王術范仲淹之所謂端
好尚程頤之所謂正人心者不將兼舉而無

陛下更化善治之衷教戒臣民之念則願

由是使在下之臣觀感既深而省悟自切忠

本。名實賞罰行於既仕之後，所以益端其忠實之趨。如是而有不盡忠以事上、務實以導民者，臣知其必無矣。况聖天子篤恭以刑百辟，賢宰執敦信以佐萬幾，則賈誼之四維、陸贄之王術、范仲淹之所謂端好尚、程頤之所謂正人心者，不將兼舉而無遺乎？
雖然，臣又有說焉。天下之忠偽固當嚴其辨，而一心之忠偽尤當慎其防。誠欲防閑乎此心，亦惟省察克治而已。我陛下身履神聖之極，而尤時切修省之懷，固將以極誠無妄之道而建臣民之極矣。臣愚仰體陛下更化善治之衷、教戒臣民之念，則願陛下益檢此心於宥密之地，而不忘夫敬一之真。由是使在下之臣觀感既深，而省悟自切。忠誠之有素者，將益効於亹亹；而此心之少有未實者，亦革故而鼎新。凡致身之義、慎獨之功，匪徒知之，亦允蹈之。而保邦之業、濟時之猷、愛民一體之心、任事獨立之操，皆此出矣。何也？士大夫者，民之表也，而陛下則又臣工之表也。表正則影隨，理固有相須
translation_en:
…foundation. The assessment of reputation against reality, together with rewards and punishments, is applied after men enter office, further directing their aspirations toward loyalty and sincerity. With this in place, your servant knows that there will surely be none who fail to serve their sovereign with utmost loyalty and guide the people through substantive deeds. Moreover, when the sagely Son of Heaven exemplifies earnest reverence for all officials, and worthy grand councilors uphold trustworthiness in assisting with the myriad affairs of government, will not Jia Yi’s Four Bonds, Lu Zhi’s arts of kingship, what Fan Zhongyan called rectifying preferences, and what Cheng Yi called rectifying people’s hearts all be put into practice, with nothing omitted?
Nevertheless, your servant has something further to say. Loyalty and falsity throughout the realm must certainly be distinguished rigorously, but still greater care must be taken to guard against falsity within one’s own heart. Truly to safeguard this heart requires only self-examination and the mastery and correction of one’s faults. Your Majesty has personally attained the highest reaches of sagehood, yet remains constantly intent upon self-cultivation and examination. Surely, through the Way of perfect sincerity without falsehood, you will establish the supreme standard for your officials and people. In my ignorance, I reverently comprehend Your Majesty’s intention to renew moral transformation and govern well, and your concern to instruct and admonish officials and people. I therefore pray that Your Majesty examine this heart still more closely in its deepest, quietest recesses, never forgetting the true meaning of reverent concentration on the One. Thus the officials below, profoundly moved by observing your example, will naturally become earnest in examining themselves and awakening to their faults. Those long established in loyalty and sincerity will redouble their tireless efforts; those whose hearts retain even a little insincerity will also discard the old and renew themselves. They will not merely understand the duty of devoting themselves to service and the discipline of vigilance when alone, but will truly practice them. The work of preserving the state, plans for meeting the needs of the age, the heart that loves the people as parts of one body, and the integrity to shoulder responsibilities and stand firm alone will all arise from this. Why is this so? Scholar-officials are the standard for the people, while Your Majesty is in turn the standard for your officials. When the gnomon is upright, its shadow follows accordingly; by principle, there is indeed a mutual dependence…

title: 嘉靖四十四年進士登科錄
text:
臣陳棟
臣對臣聞帝王之以道經世也操損益之權
於其上而後有可久之治責真實之政於其
下而後有共濟之功夫道原於天固歷萬世
以無弊然及其行之既久也而不有以維之
則易窮補其偏而救其弊司化者之責也聖
人觀時勢之會酌古今之宜於是乎有變通
之政而道揆之宰於上者自日運而不窮政
出於君固合萬民以觀化然方其習之已成
也而欲有以變之則難從行其令而致之民
===
承宣者之事也聖人立臣民之極察向背之
由於是乎有責實之政而法守之遵於下者
自共濟而不偏盖上之化下也有機而下之
從上也貴實上之人不狃於習尚而預識其
機下之人不事於虚文而務圖其實上下一
心如一元之為運而五行迭布以成功華實
並茂如太素之為體而五采章施以為美帝
王之所以移風易俗而成久安長治之業者
端不外於此也欽惟
皇帝陛下

punctuated:
臣陳棟。
臣對：臣聞帝王之以道經世也，操損益之權於其上，而後有可久之治；責真實之政於其下，而後有共濟之功。夫道原於天，固歷萬世以無弊，然及其行之既久也，而不有以維之，則易窮。補其偏而救其弊，司化者之責也。聖人觀時勢之會，酌古今之宜，於是乎有變通之政，而道揆之宰於上者，自日運而不窮。政出於君，固合萬民以觀化，然方其習之已成也，而欲有以變之，則難從。行其令而致之民，承宣者之事也。聖人立臣民之極，察向背之由，於是乎有責實之政，而法守之遵於下者，自共濟而不偏。盖上之化下也有機，而下之從上也貴實。上之人不狃於習尚，而預識其機；下之人不事於虚文，而務圖其實。上下一心，如一元之為運，而五行迭布以成功；華實並茂，如太素之為體，而五采章施以為美。帝王之所以移風易俗，而成久安長治之業者，端不外於此也。欽惟皇帝陛下
translation_en:
Your servant Chen Dong.
Your servant replies: I have heard that when emperors and kings order the world through the Way, only by exercising from above the authority to diminish or augment can they establish enduring government; only by demanding substantive administration from those below can they achieve success through common effort. The Way originates in Heaven and can indeed endure for ten thousand generations without defect. Yet after it has long been put into practice, unless something is done to sustain it, its application readily reaches an impasse. Correcting its imbalances and remedying its abuses is the responsibility of those who oversee transformation. The sage observes the conjunction of circumstances and weighs what is appropriate in ancient and modern times. Thus he institutes measures for adaptation, and the standards of the Way governing affairs above operate daily without exhaustion. Government issues from the ruler and indeed brings all the people together to behold his transforming influence. Yet once their accustomed practices have become established, if he seeks to change them, they find it difficult to comply. Carrying out his commands and bringing them to the people is the task of those charged with receiving and promulgating them. The sage establishes the highest standard for officials and people and examines why they turn toward or away from it. Thus he institutes measures that demand actual results, and those below who adhere to their prescribed duties naturally cooperate in accomplishing their work without deviation.
For those above to transform those below requires recognition of the pivotal moment; for those below to follow those above, substance is essential. Those above must not be bound by prevailing habits but must recognize the pivotal moment in advance. Those below must not occupy themselves with empty formalities but must strive for substantive results. When those above and below are of one mind, they resemble the single primal force in its movement, with the Five Phases unfolding in succession to accomplish their work. When outward refinement and inner substance flourish together, they resemble primordial substance as a foundation, upon which the five colors are brilliantly displayed to create beauty. The means by which emperors and kings transform customs and accomplish lasting peace and enduring good government lie precisely in this and nothing beyond it. Reverently considering Your Majesty the Emperor …

translation_en:
…endowed with divine sagacity, occupying the position of ruler and teacher, You have answered the auspicious occasion that comes once in five hundred years. Through reverence and singleness of purpose, You have continued the transmission of the Way handed down by emperors and kings. Inheriting Heaven’s allotted succession for countless millions of years, You have established the supreme standard and the mean, thereby revealing the profound essentials of the ancestral emperors’ teaching of the mind. Your reverent silence accords with Heaven’s workings; Your civilizing influence spreads to the farthest shores. You have brought good order and peace to the myriad states for forty-four years now.
Ignorant and lowly though Your servant is, I have been fortunate to live amid the achievements of Your Majesty’s enduring Way and the accomplishments of Your long life. I have received the unmerited recommendation of the responsible officials and reverently received the question posed in the great court. First, You examined what the Three Dynasties esteemed, particularly lamenting how readily people incline toward the predominance of outward refinement. Next, You investigated the grounds for curtailing or augmenting inherited practices, sternly reproaching the assembled officials for their lack of substance. Your servant reverently understands that Your Majesty wishes to recover the flourishing purity of antiquity and remedy the abuses of the present: a most exalted intention. Yet I am one who follows the Way daily without understanding it. How could I answer even a ten-thousandth part of Your august inquiry?
Nevertheless, I have heard that farmers exert their strength and thereby nourish gentlemen, while the foolish devise plans from which the wise select. If this is so, then Your servant ventures to think that I may offer my words. How could I fail to lay bare my innermost sincerity in reply? I reverently consider…
